115.s:
agnir uvāca
udyataścedgayāṃ yātuṃ(1) śrāddhaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ /
vidhāya kārpaṭīveśaṃ grāmasyāpi pradakṣiṇaṃ //
115.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
उद्यतश्चेद्गयां यातुं(1) श्राद्धं कृत्वा विधानतः /
विधाय कार्पटीवेशं ग्रामस्यापि प्रदक्षिणं //
115.m: Agni said: / If one is prepared to go to Gayā, having performed an ancestral rite according to rule, / having assumed the attire of a pilgrim, and having circumambulated the village,

115.s:
kṛtvā pratidinaṅgacchet saṃyataścāpratigrahī /
gṛhāccalitamātrasya gayayā gamanaṃ prati //
115.d:
कृत्वा प्रतिदिनङ्गच्छेत् संयतश्चाप्रतिग्रही /
गृहाच्चलितमात्रस्य गयया गमनं प्रति //
115.m: he should travel every day, self-restrained and receiving no gifts. / As soon as one has set forth from home towards Gayā,

115.s:
svargārohaṇasopānaṃ pitṝṇāntu pade pade /
brahmajñānena kiṃ kāryaṃ gogṛhe maraṇena kiṃ //
115.d:
स्वर्गारोहणसोपानं पितॄणान्तु पदे पदे /
ब्रह्मज्ञानेन किं कार्यं गोगृहे मरणेन किं //
115.m: at every step there is a stairway to heaven for the ancestors. / What need is there for knowledge of Brahman? What need for dying in a cowshed?

115.s:
kiṃ kurukṣetravāsena yadā(2) putro gayāṃ vrajet /
gayāprāptaṃ sutaṃ dṛṣṭvā pitṝṇāmutsavo bhavet //
115.d:
किं कुरुक्षेत्रवासेन यदा(2) पुत्रो गयां व्रजेत् /
गयाप्राप्तं सुतं दृष्ट्वा पितॄणामुत्सवो भवेत् //
115.m: What need for dwelling in Kurukṣetra, when a son goes to Gayā? / Seeing the son arrived at Gayā, there is rejoicing for the ancestors:

115.s:
padbhyāmapi jalaṃ spṛṣṭvā asmabhyaṃ kinna dāsyati /
brahmajñānaṃ gayāśrāddhaṃ gogṛhe maraṇaṃ tathā //
115.d:
पद्भ्यामपि जलं स्पृष्ट्वा अस्मभ्यं किन्न दास्यति /
ब्रह्मज्ञानं गयाश्राद्धं गोगृहे मरणं तथा //
115.m: "Touching even the water with his feet, what will he not give to us?" / Knowledge of Brahman, an ancestral rite at Gayā, and likewise death in a cowshed,

115.s:
vāsaḥ puṃsāṃ kurukṣetre muktireṣā caturvidhā /
kāṅkṣanti pitaraḥ putraṃ narakādbhayabhīravaḥ //
115.d:
वासः पुंसां कुरुक्षेत्रे मुक्तिरेषा चतुर्विधा /
काङ्क्षन्ति पितरः पुत्रं नरकाद्भयभीरवः //
115.m: and dwelling in Kurukṣetra—these are the four kinds of liberation for men. / Frightened by fear of hell, the ancestors desire a son:

115.s:
gayāṃ yāsyati yaḥ putraḥ sa nastrātā bhaviṣyati /
muṇḍanañcopavāsaś ca sarvatīrtheṣvayaṃ vidhiḥ //
115.d:
गयां यास्यति यः पुत्रः स नस्त्राता भविष्यति /
मुण्डनञ्चोपवासश् च सर्वतीर्थेष्वयं विधिः //
115.m: "Whichever son goes to Gayā, he will be our deliverer." / Shaving the head and fasting—this is the rule at all sacred fords.

115.s:
na kālādirgayātīrthe dadyāt piṇḍāṃś ca nityaśaḥ /
pakṣatrayanivāsī ca punātyāsaptatamaṃ kulaṃ //
:n
1 gantumiti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , cha.. , ja.. ca
2 yadi iti gha.. , ga.. , jha.. ca
:p 1
115.d:
न कालादिर्गयातीर्थे दद्यात् पिण्डांश् च नित्यशः /
पक्षत्रयनिवासी च पुनात्यासप्ततमं कुलं //
:न्
1 गन्तुमिति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , छ.. , ज.. च
2 यदि इति घ.. , ग.. , झ.. च
:प् 1
115.m:
At the sacred ford of Gayā there is no restriction of time or the like; one should offer rice-balls daily. / And one who dwells [there] for three fortnights purifies up to seventy generations of his family.
[Footnote]
1 "gantum" in kha., ga., gha., cha., and ja.
2 "yadi" in gha., ga., and jha.

115.s:
aṣṭakāsu ca vṛddhauca(1) gayāyāṃ mṛtavāsare /
atra mātuḥ pṛthak śrāddhamanyatra patinā saha //
115.d:
अष्टकासु च वृद्धौच(1) गयायां मृतवासरे /
अत्र मातुः पृथक् श्राद्धमन्यत्र पतिना सह //
115.m: On the Aṣṭakā days, during a rite for prosperity, at Gayā, and on the anniversary of death, / an ancestral rite is performed here separately for the mother; elsewhere, it is together with the husband.

115.s:
pitrādinavadaityaṃ tathā dvādaśadaivataṃ /
prathame divase snāyāttīrthe hy uttaramānase //
115.d:
पित्रादिनवदैत्यं तथा द्वादशदैवतं /
प्रथमे दिवसे स्नायात्तीर्थे ह्य् उत्तरमानसे //
115.m: [An ancestral rite] for nine deities beginning with the father, and likewise for twelve deities— / on the first day, one should bathe in the sacred ford Uttaramānasa.

115.s:
uttare mānase puṇye āyurārogyavṛddhaye /
sarvāghaughavidhānāya(2) snānaṃ kuryād vimuktaye(3) //
115.d:
उत्तरे मानसे पुण्ये आयुरारोग्यवृद्धये /
सर्वाघौघविधानाय(2) स्नानं कुर्याद् विमुक्तये(3) //
115.m: In the holy Uttaramānasa, for the increase of life and health, / to destroy the flood of all sins, and for liberation, one should perform a bath:

115.s:
santarpya devapitrādīn śrāddhakṛt piṇḍado bhavet /
divyāntarīkṣabhaumasthān(4) devān santarpayāmyahaṃ //
115.d:
सन्तर्प्य देवपित्रादीन् श्राद्धकृत् पिण्डदो भवेत् /
दिव्यान्तरीक्षभौमस्थान्(4) देवान् सन्तर्पयाम्यहं //
115.m: Having satisfied the gods, ancestors, and others, the performer of the ancestral rite should offer rice-balls: / 'I satisfy the gods residing in heaven, the atmosphere, and on earth.

115.s:
divyāntarīkṣabhaumādi pitṛmātrādi tarpayet /
pitā pitāmahaś caiva tathaiva prapitāmahaḥ //
115.d:
दिव्यान्तरीक्षभौमादि पितृमात्रादि तर्पयेत् /
पिता पितामहश् चैव तथैव प्रपितामहः //
115.m: One should satisfy the ancestors and mothers in heaven, the atmosphere, and on earth: / father, paternal grandfather, and likewise paternal great-grandfather;

115.s:
mātā pitāmahī caiva(5) tathaiva prapitāmahī /
mātāmahaḥ pramātāmaho vṛddhapramātāmahaḥ(6) //
115.d:
माता पितामही चैव(5) तथैव प्रपितामही /
मातामहः प्रमातामहो वृद्धप्रमातामहः(6) //
115.m: mother, paternal grandmother, and likewise paternal great-grandmother; / maternal grandfather, maternal great-grandfather, and maternal great-great-grandfather.

115.s:
tebhyo.nyebhya(7) imān piṇḍānuddhārāya dadāmyahaṃ /
oṃ namaḥ sūryadevāya somabhaumajñarūpiṇe(8) //
115.d:
तेभ्यो.न्येभ्य(7) इमान् पिण्डानुद्धाराय ददाम्यहं /
ओं नमः सूर्यदेवाय सोमभौमज्ञरूपिणे(8) //
115.m: To them and to the others I offer these rice-balls for their deliverance. / Oṃ, reverence to the Sun-god, who has the forms of the Moon, Mars, and Mercury,

115.s:
jīvaśukraśanaiścārirāhuketusvarūpiṇe /
uttare mānase snātā(9) uddharetsakalaṃ kulaṃ //
115.d:
जीवशुक्रशनैश्चारिराहुकेतुस्वरूपिणे /
उत्तरे मानसे स्नाता(9) उद्धरेत्सकलं कुलं //
115.m: who has the forms of Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, Rāhu, and Ketu.' / Having bathed in Uttaramānasa, he delivers his entire lineage.

115.s:
sūryaṃ natvā(10) vrajenmaunī naro dakṣiṇamānasaṃ(11) /
:n
1 anvaṣṭakāsu vṛddhau ceti gha.. , ṅa.. ca
2 sarvāghaughavināśāyeti kha.. , gha.. , cha.. ca
3 snānaṃ sarvavimuktaye iti cha..
4 divyāntarīkṣagān bhaumāniti ga..
5 mātā mātāmahī caiveti ka.. , kha.. , ga.. , cha.. , ja.. ca
6 vṛddhapramātṛkāmaha iti ka.. , ga.. , cha.. , ja.. ca
7 tebhyastebhya iti gha.. , ja.. ca
8 somabhaumasvarūpiṇe iti gha..
9 snātveti ka..
10 sūryaṃ dṛṣṭvā iti ṅa..
11 tato dakṣiṇamānasamiti ga.. , gha.. , ja.. , jha.. ca
:p 2
dakṣiṇe mānase snānaṃ karomi pitṛtṛptaye(1) //
115.d:
सूर्यं नत्वा(10) व्रजेन्मौनी नरो दक्षिणमानसं(11) /
:न्
1 अन्वष्टकासु वृद्धौ चेति घ.. , ङ.. च
2 सर्वाघौघविनाशायेति ख.. , घ.. , छ.. च
3 स्नानं सर्वविमुक्तये इति छ..
4 दिव्यान्तरीक्षगान् भौमानिति ग..
5 माता मातामही चैवेति क.. , ख.. , ग.. , छ.. , ज.. च
6 वृद्धप्रमातृकामह इति क.. , ग.. , छ.. , ज.. च
7 तेभ्यस्तेभ्य इति घ.. , ज.. च
8 सोमभौमस्वरूपिणे इति घ..
9 स्नात्वेति क..
10 सूर्यं दृष्ट्वा इति ङ..
11 ततो दक्षिणमानसमिति ग.. , घ.. , ज.. , झ.. च
:प् 2
दक्षिणे मानसे स्नानं करोमि पितृतृप्तये(1) //
115.m:
Having bowed to the Sun, a man should go in silence to Dakṣiṇamānasa:
[Footnotes]
1 'anvaṣṭakāsu vṛddhau ca' according to manuscripts gha and ṅa.
2 'sarvāghaughavināśāya' according to manuscripts kha, gha, and cha.
3 'snānaṃ sarvavimuktaye' according to manuscript cha.
4 'divyāntarīkṣagān bhaumān' according to manuscript ga.
5 'mātā mātāmahī caiva' according to manuscripts ka, kha, ga, cha, and ja.
6 'vṛddhapramātṛkāmahaḥ' according to manuscripts ka, ga, cha, and ja.
7 'tebhyastebhyaḥ' according to manuscripts gha and ja.
8 'somabhaumasvarūpiṇe' according to manuscript gha.
9 'snātvā' according to manuscript ka.
10 'sūryaṃ dṛṣṭvā' according to manuscript ṅa.
11 'tato dakṣiṇamānasam' according to manuscripts ga, gha, ja, and jha.
'I bathe in Dakṣiṇamānasa for the satisfaction of the ancestors.

115.s:
gayāyāmāgataḥ svargaṃ yāntu me pitaro 'khilāḥ /
śrāddhaṃ piṇḍantataḥ kṛtvā sūryaṃ natvā vadedidaṃ //
115.d:
गयायामागतः स्वर्गं यान्तु मे पितरो ऽखिलाः /
श्राद्धं पिण्डन्ततः कृत्वा सूर्यं नत्वा वदेदिदं //
115.m: Having come to Gayā, may all my ancestors go to heaven.' / Then, having performed the ancestral rite and offered rice-balls, he should bow to the Sun and recite this:

115.s:
oṃ namo bhānave bhartre(2) bhavāya bhava me vibho /
bhuktimuktipradaḥ sarvapitṝṇāṃ bhavabhāvitaḥ //
115.d:
ओं नमो भानवे भर्त्रे(2) भवाय भव मे विभो /
भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदः सर्वपितॄणां भवभावितः //
115.m: 'Oṃ, reverence to the Sun, the maintainer, the origin [of all]; be [gracious] to me, O Lord! / Bestower of worldly enjoyment and liberation, revered by the world, [gratify] all ancestors!

115.s:
kavyavālānalaḥ somo yamaś caivāryamā tathā /
agniṣvāttā varhiṣada ājyapāḥ pitṛdevatāḥ //
115.d:
कव्यवालानलः सोमो यमश् चैवार्यमा तथा /
अग्निष्वात्ता वर्हिषद आज्यपाः पितृदेवताः //
115.m: Kavyavāhana fire, Soma, Yama, and Aryaman, / the Agniṣvāttas, the Barhiṣads, the Ājyapas, the ancestral deities—

115.s:
āgacchantu mahābhāgā yuṣmābhī rakṣitāstviha /
madīyāḥ pitaro ye ca mātṛmātāmahādayaḥ //
115.d:
आगच्छन्तु महाभागा युष्माभी रक्षितास्त्विह /
मदीयाः पितरो ये च मातृमातामहादयः //
115.m: may the illustrious ones come here, protected by you! / And those who are my ancestors, the maternal ancestors and the rest,

115.s:
teṣāṃ piṇḍapradātāhamāgato 'smi gayāmimāṃ /
udīcyāṃ muṇḍapṛṣṭhasya devarṣigaṇapūjitaṃ(3) //
115.d:
तेषां पिण्डप्रदाताहमागतो ऽस्मि गयामिमां /
उदीच्यां मुण्डपृष्ठस्य देवर्षिगणपूजितं(3) //
115.m: I, the giver of rice-balls to them, have come to this Gayā.' / North of Muṇḍapṛṣṭha is [the ford] worshipped by hosts of divine sages,

115.s:
nāmnā kanakhalaṃ tīrthaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaṃ /
siddhānāṃ prītijananaiḥ pāpānāñca bhayaṅkaraiḥ //
115.d:
नाम्ना कनखलं तीर्थं त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतं /
सिद्धानां प्रीतिजननैः पापानाञ्च भयङ्करैः //
115.m: by name the Kanakhala sacred ford, renowned in the three worlds, / which causes delight to the perfected ones and strikes terror into sinners,

115.s:
lelihānair mahānāgai rakṣyate caiva nityaśaḥ /
tatra snātvā divaṃ(4) yānti krīḍante bhuvi mānavāḥ //
115.d:
लेलिहानैर् महानागै रक्ष्यते चैव नित्यशः /
तत्र स्नात्वा दिवं(4) यान्ति क्रीडन्ते भुवि मानवाः //
115.m: and is constantly guarded by darting-tongued great serpents. / Having bathed there, humans go to heaven [or] delight on earth.

115.s:
phalgutīrthaṃ tato gacchenmahānadyāṃ sthitaṃ paraṃ /
nāgājjanārdanāt kūpādvaṭāccottaramānasāt //
115.d:
फल्गुतीर्थं ततो गच्छेन्महानद्यां स्थितं परं /
नागाज्जनार्दनात् कूपाद्वटाच्चोत्तरमानसात् //
115.m: Then one should go to Phalgu sacred ford, the supreme [spot] situated on the Mahānadī. / From the serpent, from Janārdana, from the well, from the banyan tree, and from Uttaramānasa—

115.s:
etad gayāśiraḥ(5) proktaṃ phalgutīrthaṃ taducyate /
muṇḍapṛṣṭhanāgādyāś ca sārāt sāramathāntaraṃ //
:n
1 karomi pitṛdaivate iti ja..
2 bhānave tasmai iti ṅa..
3 devarṣigaṇasevitamiti gha.. , ja.. ca / devatāgaṇasevitamiti jha..
4 tatra snātā divamiti ja..
5 phalguṃ gayāśira iti kha.. , ṅa.. , cha.. ca
:p 3
115.d:
एतद् गयाशिरः(5) प्रोक्तं फल्गुतीर्थं तदुच्यते /
मुण्डपृष्ठनागाद्याश् च सारात् सारमथान्तरं //
:न्
1 करोमि पितृदैवते इति ज..
2 भानवे तस्मै इति ङ..
3 देवर्षिगणसेवितमिति घ.. , ज.. च / देवतागणसेवितमिति झ..
4 तत्र स्नाता दिवमिति ज..
5 फल्गुं गयाशिर इति ख.. , ङ.. , छ.. च
:प् 3
115.m:
this is declared to be Gayāśiras, and it is called Phalgu sacred ford; / and Muṇḍapṛṣṭha, Nāga, and others are the innermost essence of the essence.
[Footnotes]
1 'karomi pitṛdaivate' according to manuscript ja.
2 'bhānave tasmai' according to manuscript ṅa.
3 'devarṣigaṇasevitam' according to manuscripts gha and ja; 'devatāgaṇasevitam' according to manuscript jha.
4 'tatra snātā divam' according to manuscript ja.
5 'phalguṃ gayāśiraḥ' according to manuscripts kha, ṅa, and cha.

115.s:
yasmin phalati śrīrgaurvā kāmadhenurjalaṃ mahī /
dṛṣṭiramyādikaṃ yasmāt phalgutīrthaṃ na phalguvat //
115.d:
यस्मिन् फलति श्रीर्गौर्वा कामधेनुर्जलं मही /
दृष्टिरम्यादिकं यस्मात् फल्गुतीर्थं न फल्गुवत् //
115.m: Because fortune, speech, the wish-granting cow, water, earth, / pleasant sights, and so on bear fruit there, Phalgu sacred ford is not unsubstantial.

115.s:
phalgutīrthe naraḥ snātvā dṛṣṭvā devaṃ gadādharaṃ /
etena kiṃ na paryāptaṃ nṛṇāṃ sukṛṭakāriṇāṃ //
115.d:
फल्गुतीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा दृष्ट्वा देवं गदाधरं /
एतेन किं न पर्याप्तं नृणां सुकृटकारिणां //
115.m: When a man has bathed in the Phalgu sacred ford and seen the god Gadādhara, / is this not sufficient for men who perform good deeds?

115.s:
pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni āsamudrātsarāṃsi ca /
phalgutīrthaṃ gamiṣyanti vāramekaṃ dine dine //
115.d:
पृथिव्यां यानि तीर्थानि आसमुद्रात्सरांसि च /
फल्गुतीर्थं गमिष्यन्ति वारमेकं दिने दिने //
115.m: Whatever sacred fords and lakes there are on earth as far as the ocean, / they will go to Phalgu sacred ford once day after day.

115.s:
phalgutīrthe tīrtharāje karoti snānamādṛtaḥ /
pitṝṇāṃ brahmalokāptyai ātmano bhuktimuktaye //
115.d:
फल्गुतीर्थे तीर्थराजे करोति स्नानमादृतः /
पितॄणां ब्रह्मलोकाप्त्यै आत्मनो भुक्तिमुक्तये //
115.m: Devoutly he bathes in Phalgu sacred ford, the king of sacred fords, / for the ancestors' attainment of the world of Brahmā and for his own worldly enjoyment and liberation.

115.s:
snātvā śrāddhī piṇḍado 'tha nameddevaṃ pitāmahaṃ /
kalau māheśvarā lokā atra devī(1) gadādharaḥ //
115.d:
स्नात्वा श्राद्धी पिण्डदो ऽथ नमेद्देवं पितामहं /
कलौ माहेश्वरा लोका अत्र देवी(1) गदाधरः //
115.m: Having bathed, the performer of the ancestral rite, offering rice-balls, should then bow to the god Pitāmaha. / In the Kali age people are devotees of Maheśvara; here the god is Gadādhara.

115.s:
pitāmaho liṅgarūpī tannamāmi maheśvaraṃ /
gadādharaṃ balaṃ kāmamaniruddhaṃ narāyaṇaṃ(2) //
115.d:
पितामहो लिङ्गरूपी तन्नमामि महेश्वरं /
गदाधरं बलं काममनिरुद्धं नरायणं(2) //
115.m: Pitāmaha has the form of a liṅga, so I bow to Maheśvara, / to Gadādhara, Bala, Kāma, Aniruddha, and Nārāyaṇa.

115.s:
brahmaviṣṇunṛsiṃhākhyaṃ varāhādiṃ namāmyahaṃ /
tato gadādharaṃ dṛṣṭvā kulānāṃ śatamuddharet //
115.d:
ब्रह्मविष्णुनृसिंहाख्यं वराहादिं नमाम्यहं /
ततो गदाधरं दृष्ट्वा कुलानां शतमुद्धरेत् //
115.m: I bow to the one called Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Nṛsiṃha, and to Varāha and the rest. / Then, having beheld Gadādhara, he delivers a hundred [generations of his] families.

115.s:
dharmāraṇyaṃ dvitīye 'hni mataṅgasyāśrame vare /
mataṅgavāpyāṃ saṃsnāya śrāddhakṛt piṇḍado(3) bhavet //
115.d:
धर्मारण्यं द्वितीये ऽह्नि मतङ्गस्याश्रमे वरे /
मतङ्गवाप्यां संस्नाय श्राद्धकृत् पिण्डदो(3) भवेत् //
115.m: On the second day, in Dharmāraṇya at the excellent hermitage of Mataṅga, / having bathed in Mataṅga's pond, he should perform the ancestral rite and offer rice-balls.

115.s:
mataṅgeśaṃ suddheśaṃ(4) natvā cedamudīrayet /
pramāṇaṃ devatāḥ santu lokapālāś ca sākṣiṇaḥ //
115.d:
मतङ्गेशं सुद्धेशं(4) नत्वा चेदमुदीरयेत् /
प्रमाणं देवताः सन्तु लोकपालाश् च साक्षिणः //
115.m: Having bowed to Mataṅgeśa and Siddheśa, he should speak this: / 'May the deities be the authority and the world-protectors the witnesses!

115.s:
mayāgatya mataṅge 'smin pitṝṇāṃ niṣkṛtiḥ kṛtā /
snānatarpaṇaśrāddhādirbrahmatīrthe 'tha(5) kūpake //
:n
1 ato deva iti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , cha.. ca
2 nārāyaṇamiti kha.. , ga.. , ṅa.. ca
3 śrāddhadaḥ piṇḍada iti kha..
4 mataṅgeśañca siddheśamiti ja..
5 brahmatīrthetreti kha..
:p 4
115.d:
मयागत्य मतङ्गे ऽस्मिन् पितॄणां निष्कृतिः कृता /
स्नानतर्पणश्राद्धादिर्ब्रह्मतीर्थे ऽथ(5) कूपके //
:न्
1 अतो देव इति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , छ.. च
2 नारायणमिति ख.. , ग.. , ङ.. च
3 श्राद्धदः पिण्डद इति ख..
4 मतङ्गेशञ्च सिद्धेशमिति ज..
5 ब्रह्मतीर्थेत्रेति ख..
:प् 4
115.m:
Having come to this Mataṅga, redemption has been made by me for the ancestors.' / Then bath, water-libations, ancestral rites, and other [rites] in the Brahma sacred ford and at the well—
[Footnotes]
1 'ato devaḥ' according to manuscripts kha, ga, gha, and cha.
2 'nārāyaṇam' according to manuscripts kha, ga, and ṅa.
3 'śrāddhadaḥ piṇḍadaḥ' according to manuscript kha.
4 'mataṅgeśañca siddheśam' according to manuscript ja.
5 'brahmatīrthetra' according to manuscript kha.

115.s:
tatkūrpayūpayormadhye śrāddhaṃ kulaśatoddhṛtau /
mahābodhaturuṃ natvā dharmavān svargalokabhāk //
115.d:
तत्कूर्पयूपयोर्मध्ये श्राद्धं कुलशतोद्धृतौ /
महाबोधतुरुं नत्वा धर्मवान् स्वर्गलोकभाक् //
115.m: between that well and the sacrificial post, an ancestral rite [serves] for the deliverance of a hundred families. / Having bowed to the tree of great enlightenment, the virtuous one shares in the heavenly world.

115.s:
tṛtīye brahmasarasi(1) snānaṃ kuryādyatavrataḥ(2) /
snānaṃ brahmasarastīrthe(3) karomi brahmabhūtaye //
115.d:
तृतीये ब्रह्मसरसि(1) स्नानं कुर्याद्यतव्रतः(2) /
स्नानं ब्रह्मसरस्तीर्थे(3) करोमि ब्रह्मभूतये //
115.m: On the third day, firm in his votive observance, he should bathe in Brahmasaras: / 'I bathe in the sacred ford of Brahmasaras for the attainment of Brahmā

115.s:
pitṝṇāṃ brahmalokāya brahmarṣigaṇasevite /
tarpaṇaṃ śrāddhakṛt piṇḍaṃ pradadyāttu prasecanaṃ(4) /
kuryācca vājapeyārthī brahmayūpapradakṣiṇaṃ //
115.d:
पितॄणां ब्रह्मलोकाय ब्रह्मर्षिगणसेविते /
तर्पणं श्राद्धकृत् पिण्डं प्रदद्यात्तु प्रसेचनं(4) /
कुर्याच्च वाजपेयार्थी ब्रह्मयूपप्रदक्षिणं //
115.m: and for the world of Brahmā for the ancestors, [at the lake] frequented by hosts of Brahmanical sages.' / The performer of the ancestral rite should offer libation, rice-balls, and sprinkling of water; / and desiring [the fruit of] a Vājapeya sacrifice, he should circumambulate Brahmā's sacrificial post.

115.s:
eko muniḥ kumbhakuśāgrahasta āmrasya mūle salilandadāti /
āmnāya siktāḥ pitaraś ca tṛptā ekā kriyā dvyarthakarī prasiddhā //
115.d:
एको मुनिः कुम्भकुशाग्रहस्त आम्रस्य मूले सलिलन्ददाति /
आम्नाय सिक्ताः पितरश् च तृप्ता एका क्रिया द्व्यर्थकरी प्रसिद्धा //
115.m: A single sage, holding a jar and kuśa grass tips in hand, pours water at the root of a mango tree: / the sacred traditions are watered, and the ancestors are satisfied—a single rite is well known to accomplish two purposes.

115.s:
brahmāṇañca namaskṛtya kulānāṃ śatamuddharet /
phalgutīrthe caturthe 'hni snātvā devāditarpaṇaṃ //
115.d:
ब्रह्माणञ्च नमस्कृत्य कुलानां शतमुद्धरेत् /
फल्गुतीर्थे चतुर्थे ऽह्नि स्नात्वा देवादितर्पणं //
115.m: And having bowed to Brahmā, he delivers a hundred families. / On the fourth day, having bathed in Phalgu sacred ford and offered libations to the gods and others,

115.s:
kṛtvā śrāddhaṃ sapiṇḍañca gayāśirasi kārayet /
pañcakrośaṃ gayākṣetraṃ krośamekaṃ gayāśiraḥ //
115.d:
कृत्वा श्राद्धं सपिण्डञ्च गयाशिरसि कारयेत् /
पञ्चक्रोशं गयाक्षेत्रं क्रोशमेकं गयाशिरः //
115.m: and having performed the ancestral rite with rice-balls, he should have it done on Gayāśiras. / The sacred precinct of Gayā is five krośas; Gayāśiras is one krośa.

115.s:
tatra piṇḍapradānena kulānāṃ śatamudharet /
muṇḍapṛṣṭhe padaṃ nnyāstaṃ mahādevena dhīmatā //
115.d:
तत्र पिण्डप्रदानेन कुलानां शतमुधरेत् /
मुण्डपृष्ठे पदं न्न्यास्तं महादेवेन धीमता //
115.m: By offering rice-balls there, he delivers a hundred families. / On Muṇḍapṛṣṭha the footprint was imprinted by the wise Mahādeva.

115.s:
muṇḍapṛṣṭhe śiraḥ sākṣād gayāśira udāhṛtaṃ /
:n
1 brahmasadasi iti kha.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , ja.. ca
2 mayāgatyetyādiḥ, snānaṃ kuryādyatavrata ity antaḥ pāṭhaścha..
pustake nāsti
3 brahmasadastīrthe iti gha.. / brahmaśirastīrthe iti kha..
4 tarpaṇaśrāddhakṛt piṇḍapradaścāpi prasecanamiti kha.. , cha.. ca /
tarpaṇaśrāddhakṛt piṇḍapradaścāmraprasecanamiti ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. ,
ja.. ca
:p 5
sākṣād gayāśirastatra phalgutīrthāśramaṃ(1) kṛtaṃ //
115.d:
मुण्डपृष्ठे शिरः साक्षाद् गयाशिर उदाहृतं /
:न्
1 ब्रह्मसदसि इति ख.. , घ.. , ङ.. , ज.. च
2 मयागत्येत्यादिः, स्नानं कुर्याद्यतव्रत इत्य् अन्तः पाठश्छ..
पुस्तके नास्ति
3 ब्रह्मसदस्तीर्थे इति घ.. / ब्रह्मशिरस्तीर्थे इति ख..
4 तर्पणश्राद्धकृत् पिण्डप्रदश्चापि प्रसेचनमिति ख.. , छ.. च /
तर्पणश्राद्धकृत् पिण्डप्रदश्चाम्रप्रसेचनमिति ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. ,
ज.. च
:प् 5
साक्षाद् गयाशिरस्तत्र फल्गुतीर्थाश्रमं(1) कृतं //
115.m:
Muṇḍapṛṣṭha is declared to be visibly the head, Gayāśiras.
[Footnote]
1 'In the assembly of Brahmā' [brahmasadasi] thus in manuscripts kha, gha, ṅa, and ja.
2 The reading beginning with 'mayāgatya' and ending with 'snānaṃ kuryādyatavrataḥ' is absent in manuscript cha.
3 'At the Brahmasadas sacred ford' [brahmasadastīrthe] thus in manuscript gha; 'At the Brahmaśiras sacred ford' [brahmaśirastīrthe] thus in manuscript kha.
4 'Performing libations and ancestral rites, offering funeral cakes, and [doing] libations' [tarpaṇaśrāddhakṛt piṇḍapradaścāpi prasecanam] thus in manuscripts kha and cha.
'Performing libations and ancestral rites, offering funeral cakes, and sprinkling mango trees' [tarpaṇaśrāddhakṛt piṇḍapradaścāmraprasecanam] thus in manuscripts ga, gha, ṅa, and ja.
There, manifestly at the Gayāśiras, the hermitage at the Phalgu sacred ford was made.

115.s:
amṛtaṃ tatra vahati pitṝṇāndattamakṣayaṃ /
snātvā daśāśvamedhe tu dṛṣṭvā devaṃ pitāmahaṃ //
115.d:
अमृतं तत्र वहति पितॄणान्दत्तमक्षयं /
स्नात्वा दशाश्वमेधे तु दृष्ट्वा देवं पितामहं //
115.m: Nectar flows there, imperishable for the ancestors when offered. / Having bathed at Daśāśvamedha and seen the god, the grandfather [Brahmā],

115.s:
rudrapādaṃ naraḥ spṛṣṭvā neha bhūyo 'bhijāyate /
śamīpatrapramāṇena piṇḍaṃ datvā gayāśire(2) //
115.d:
रुद्रपादं नरः स्पृष्ट्वा नेह भूयो ऽभिजायते /
शमीपत्रप्रमाणेन पिण्डं दत्वा गयाशिरे(2) //
115.m: And having touched the footstep of Rudra, a man is not born here again. / Having offered a funeral cake the size of a śamī leaf at Gayāśiras,

115.s:
narakasthā divaṃ yānti svargasthā mokṣamāpnuyuḥ /
pāyasenātha piṣṭena śaktunā caruṇā tathā //
115.d:
नरकस्था दिवं यान्ति स्वर्गस्था मोक्षमाप्नुयुः /
पायसेनाथ पिष्टेन शक्तुना चरुणा तथा //
115.m: Those staying in hell go to heaven, and those in heaven attain liberation. / Then, with milk rice, flour, barley meal, or sacrificial boiled rice,

115.s:
piṇḍadānaṃ taṇḍulaiś ca godhūmaistilamiśritaiḥ /
piṇḍaṃ datvā rudrapade kulānāṃ śatamuddharet //
115.d:
पिण्डदानं तण्डुलैश् च गोधूमैस्तिलमिश्रितैः /
पिण्डं दत्वा रुद्रपदे कुलानां शतमुद्धरेत् //
115.m: With rice grains and wheat mixed with sesame seeds, the offering of funeral cakes [is performed]. / Having offered a funeral cake at the footstep of Rudra, one delivers a hundred families.

115.s:
tathā viṣṇupade śrāddhapiṇḍado hy ṛṇamuktikṛt(3) /
pitrādīnāṃ śatakulaṃ svātmānaṃ(4) tārayennaraḥ //
115.d:
तथा विष्णुपदे श्राद्धपिण्डदो ह्य् ऋणमुक्तिकृत्(3) /
पित्रादीनां शतकुलं स्वात्मानं(4) तारयेन्नरः //
115.m: Likewise, offering an ancestral rite and funeral cakes at the footstep of Viṣṇu, he is freed from debts; / a man rescues a hundred families of ancestors and others, and himself.

115.s:
tathā brahmapade śrāddhī(5) brahmalokaṃ nayetpitṝn /
dakṣiṇāgnipade tadvadgārhapatyapade tathā //
115.d:
तथा ब्रह्मपदे श्राद्धी(5) ब्रह्मलोकं नयेत्पितॄन् /
दक्षिणाग्निपदे तद्वद्गार्हपत्यपदे तथा //
115.m: Likewise, performing the ancestral rite at the footstep of Brahmā, he leads the ancestors to the world of Brahmā. / In the same way at the footstep of the Dakṣiṇāgni, likewise at the footstep of the Gārhapatya,

115.s:
pade vāhavanīyasya śrāddhī yajñaphalaṃ labhet /
āvasathyasya candrasya(6) sūryasya ca gaṇasya ca //
115.d:
पदे वाहवनीयस्य श्राद्धी यज्ञफलं लभेत् /
आवसथ्यस्य चन्द्रस्य(6) सूर्यस्य च गणस्य च //
115.m: Or at the footstep of the Āhavanīya, the performer of the ancestral rite obtains the fruit of a Vedic sacrifice. / At [the footsteps] of the Āvasathya fire, the Moon, the Sun, the Gaṇa,

115.s:
agastyakārttikeyasya śrāddhī tārayate kulaṃ /
ādityasya rathaṃ natvā(7) karṇādityaṃ namīnnaraḥ //
:n
1 phalgutīrthāśrayamiti ga.. , gha.. , ja.. , jha.. ca
2 piṇḍaṃ dadyādgayāśire iti ja..
3 piṇḍadaḥ kulamuktikṛditi ga.. , ja.. ca / piṇḍado hy atimuktikṛditi
gha..
4 svātmaneti ja..
5 brahmapade śrāddhamiti jha..
6 varuṇasyātha cendrasyeti ṅa.. / āvasathyasya cendrasyeti cha.. / āvasathyasya
sendrasyeti ja..
7 rathaṃ dṛṣṭveti kha.. , cha.. ca
:p 6
115.d:
अगस्त्यकार्त्तिकेयस्य श्राद्धी तारयते कुलं /
आदित्यस्य रथं नत्वा(7) कर्णादित्यं नमीन्नरः //
:न्
1 फल्गुतीर्थाश्रयमिति ग.. , घ.. , ज.. , झ.. च
2 पिण्डं दद्याद्गयाशिरे इति ज..
3 पिण्डदः कुलमुक्तिकृदिति ग.. , ज.. च / पिण्डदो ह्य् अतिमुक्तिकृदिति
घ..
4 स्वात्मनेति ज..
5 ब्रह्मपदे श्राद्धमिति झ..
6 वरुणस्याथ चेन्द्रस्येति ङ.. / आवसथ्यस्य चेन्द्रस्येति छ.. / आवसथ्यस्य
सेन्द्रस्येति ज..
7 रथं दृष्ट्वेति ख.. , छ.. च
:प् 6
115.m:
Of Agastya, and of Kārttikeya, the performer of the ancestral rite delivers his family. / Having bowed to the chariot of the Sun, a man should bow to Karṇāditya.
[Footnote]
1 'Sheltered by the Phalgu sacred ford' [phalgutīrthāśrayam] thus in manuscripts ga, gha, ja, and jha.
2 'One should offer a funeral cake at Gayāśiras' [piṇḍaṃ dadyādgayāśire] thus in manuscript ja.
3 'Offering funeral cakes delivers the family' [piṇḍadaḥ kulamuktikṛt] thus in manuscripts ga and ja; 'Offering funeral cakes delivers greatly' [piṇḍado hy atimuktikṛt] thus in manuscript gha.
4 'By oneself' [svātmanā] thus in manuscript ja.
5 'An ancestral rite at the footstep of Brahmā' [brahmapade śrāddham] thus in manuscript jha.
6 'Of Varuṇa and Indra' [varuṇasyātha cendrasya] thus in manuscript ṅa; 'Of the Āvasathya and Indra' [āvasathyasya cendrasya] thus in manuscript cha; 'Of the Āvasathya together with Indra' [āvasathyasya sendrasya] thus in manuscript ja.
7 'Having seen the chariot' [rathaṃ dṛṣṭvā] thus in manuscripts kha and cha.

115.s:
kanakeśapadaṃ natvā gayākedārakaṃ namet /
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ pitṝn brahmapuraṃ nayet //
115.d:
कनकेशपदं नत्वा गयाकेदारकं नमेत् /
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः पितॄन् ब्रह्मपुरं नयेत् //
115.m: Having bowed to the footstep of Kanakeśa, he should bow to Gayākedāra. / Freed from all sins, he leads the ancestors to the city of Brahmā.

115.s:
viśālo 'pi gayāśīrṣe piṇḍado 'bhūcca putravān /
viśālāyāṃ viśālo 'bhūdrājaputro 'bravīd dvijān //
115.d:
विशालो ऽपि गयाशीर्षे पिण्डदो ऽभूच्च पुत्रवान् /
विशालायां विशालो ऽभूद्राजपुत्रो ऽब्रवीद् द्विजान् //
115.m: Even Viśāla, offering funeral cakes at Gayāśīrṣa, obtained sons. / Viśāla was born as a prince in Viśālā; he addressed the brahmins:

115.s:
kathaṃ putrādayaḥ syurme dvijā ūcurviśālakaṃ /
gayāyāṃ piṇḍadānena tava sarvaṃ bhaviṣyati //
115.d:
कथं पुत्रादयः स्युर्मे द्विजा ऊचुर्विशालकं /
गयायां पिण्डदानेन तव सर्वं भविष्यति //
115.m: "How may I have sons and the like?" The brahmins said to Viśālaka: / "By the offering of funeral cakes at Gayā, everything will be yours."

115.s:
viśālo 'pi gayāśīrṣe pitṛpiṇḍāndadau tataḥ(1) /
dṛṣṭvākāśe sitaṃ raktaṃ puruṣāṃstāṃś capṛṣṭavān //
115.d:
विशालो ऽपि गयाशीर्षे पितृपिण्डान्ददौ ततः(1) /
दृष्ट्वाकाशे सितं रक्तं पुरुषांस्तांश् चपृष्टवान् //
115.m: Then Viśāla too offered funeral cakes to the ancestors at Gayāśīrṣa. / Having seen white and red persons in the sky, he asked them:

115.s:
ke yuyanteṣu caivaikaḥ sitaḥ proce viśālakaṃ /
ahaṃ sitaste janaka indralokaṃ gataḥ śubhān //
115.d:
के युयन्तेषु चैवैकः सितः प्रोचे विशालकं /
अहं सितस्ते जनक इन्द्रलोकं गतः शुभान् //
115.m: "Who are you?" And one white one among them said to Viśālaka: / "I, white, am your father; through auspicious deeds I have gone to Indra's world.

115.s:
mama raktaḥ pitā putra kṛṣṇaś caiva pitāmahaḥ /
abravīt narakaṃ prāptā tvayā muktīkṛtā vayaṃ //
115.d:
मम रक्तः पिता पुत्र कृष्णश् चैव पितामहः /
अब्रवीत् नरकं प्राप्ता त्वया मुक्तीकृता वयं //
115.m: The red one is my father, O son, and the black one is the grandfather." / He said, "Having reached hell, we have been liberated by you.

115.s:
piṇḍadānād brahmalokaṃ brajāma iti te gatāḥ /
viśālaḥ prāptaputādī rājyaṃ kṛtvā hariṃ yayau //
115.d:
पिण्डदानाद् ब्रह्मलोकं ब्रजाम इति ते गताः /
विशालः प्राप्तपुतादी राज्यं कृत्वा हरिं ययौ //
115.m: From the offering of funeral cakes, we go to the world of Brahmā." Having spoken thus, they departed. / Viśāla, having obtained sons and other blessings, ruled the kingdom and went to Hari.

115.s:
pretarājaḥ svamuktyai ca vaṇijañcedamabravīt /
pretaiḥ sarvaiḥ sahārtaḥ san sukṛtaṃ bhujyate phalaṃ //
115.d:
प्रेतराजः स्वमुक्त्यै च वणिजञ्चेदमब्रवीत् /
प्रेतैः सर्वैः सहार्तः सन् सुकृतं भुज्यते फलं //
115.m: And the king of ghosts spoke thus to a merchant for his own liberation: / "Afflicted along with all the ghosts, the fruit of good deeds is being enjoyed.

115.s:
śravaṇadvādaśīyoge kumbhaḥ sānnaś ca sodakaḥ(2) /
dattaḥ purā sa madhyāhne jīvanāyopatiṣṭhate //
115.d:
श्रवणद्वादशीयोगे कुम्भः सान्नश् च सोदकः(2) /
दत्तः पुरा स मध्याह्ने जीवनायोपतिष्ठते //
115.m: On the conjunction of the twelfth lunar day of Śravaṇa, a pot with food and water / was formerly given at midday; that presents itself for our subsistence.

115.s:
dhanaṃ gṛhītvā me gaccha gayāyāṃ piṇḍado bhava /
vaṇigdhanaṃ gṛhītvā tu gayāyāṃ piṇḍado 'bhavat //
:n
1 dadau gata iti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , cha.. , ja.. ca
2 sārthaś ca sodaka iti cha..
:p 7
115.d:
धनं गृहीत्वा मे गच्छ गयायां पिण्डदो भव /
वणिग्धनं गृहीत्वा तु गयायां पिण्डदो ऽभवत् //
:न्
1 ददौ गत इति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , छ.. , ज.. च
2 सार्थश् च सोदक इति छ..
:प् 7
115.m:
Take my wealth, go, and become an offerer of funeral cakes at Gayā." / Then the merchant, taking the wealth, became an offerer of funeral cakes at Gayā.
[Footnote]
1 'Having gone, he gave' [dadau gataḥ] thus in manuscripts kha, ga, gha, ṅa, cha, and ja.
2 'Accompanied by a caravan and with water' [sārthaś ca sodakaḥ] thus in manuscript cha.

115.s:
pretarājaḥ saha pretair mukto nīto hareḥ puraṃ /
gayāśīrṣe piṇḍadānādātmānaṃ svapitṝṃs tathā(1) //
115.d:
प्रेतराजः सह प्रेतैर् मुक्तो नीतो हरेः पुरं /
गयाशीर्षे पिण्डदानादात्मानं स्वपितॄंस् तथा(1) //
115.m: The king of ghosts, along with the ghosts, was liberated and led to the city of Hari. / From offering funeral cakes at Gayāśīrṣa, [one delivers] oneself and one's ancestors,

115.s:
pitṛvaṃśe sutā ye ca mātṛvaṃśe tathaiva ca /
guruśvaśurabandhūnāṃ ye cānye bāndhavā mṛtāḥ //
115.d:
पितृवंशे सुता ये च मातृवंशे तथैव च /
गुरुश्वशुरबन्धूनां ये चान्ये बान्धवा मृताः //
115.m: And the sons who are in the paternal lineage and likewise in the maternal lineage, / and the other deceased kinsmen of teachers, fathers-in-law, and friends;

115.s:
ye me kule luptapiṇḍāḥ putradāravivarjitāḥ(2) /
kriyālopagatā ye ca jātyandhāḥ puṅgavas tathā //
115.d:
ये मे कुले लुप्तपिण्डाः पुत्रदारविवर्जिताः(2) /
क्रियालोपगता ये च जात्यन्धाः पुङ्गवस् तथा //
115.m: Those in my family who have been deprived of funeral cakes, destitute of sons and wives, / those who have missed funeral rites, those born blind, and the bull-like men,

115.s:
virūpā āmagarbhā ye jñātājñātāḥ kule mama /
teṣāṃ piṇḍo mayā datto hy akṣayyamupatiṣṭhatāṃ //
115.d:
विरूपा आमगर्भा ये ज्ञाताज्ञाताः कुले मम /
तेषां पिण्डो मया दत्तो ह्य् अक्षय्यमुपतिष्ठतां //
115.m: The deformed, the miscarried embryos, known or unknown in my family— / to them a funeral cake has been offered by me; may it present itself as imperishable!

115.s:
ye kecit pretarūpeṇa tiṣṭhanti pitaro mama /
te sarve tṛptimāyāntu piṇḍadānena(3) sarvadā //
115.d:
ये केचित् प्रेतरूपेण तिष्ठन्ति पितरो मम /
ते सर्वे तृप्तिमायान्तु पिण्डदानेन(3) सर्वदा //
115.m: Whichever of my ancestors abide in the form of ghosts, / may all of them attain satisfaction forever through this offering of funeral cakes!

115.s:
piṇḍo deyastu sarvebhyaḥ sarvair vai kulatārakaiḥ /
ātmanastu tathā deyo hy akṣayaṃ lokamicchatā //
115.d:
पिण्डो देयस्तु सर्वेभ्यः सर्वैर् वै कुलतारकैः /
आत्मनस्तु तथा देयो ह्य् अक्षयं लोकमिच्छता //
115.m: A funeral cake should indeed be offered to all by all saviours of their lineage; / and it should likewise be offered for oneself by one desiring an imperishable world.

115.s:
pañcame 'hni gadālole snāyānmantreṇa buddhimān /
gadāprakṣālane tīrthe gadālole 'tipāvane //
115.d:
पञ्चमे ऽह्नि गदालोले स्नायान्मन्त्रेण बुद्धिमान् /
गदाप्रक्षालने तीर्थे गदालोले ऽतिपावने //
115.m: On the fifth day, a wise man should bathe at Gadālola with the mantra: / "At Gadālola, the sacred ford for cleansing the mace, which is supremely purifying,

115.s:
snānaṃ karāmi saṃsāragadaśāntyai janārdana /
namo 'kṣayavaṭāyaiva akṣayasvargadāyine //
115.d:
स्नानं करामि संसारगदशान्त्यै जनार्दन /
नमो ऽक्षयवटायैव अक्षयस्वर्गदायिने //
115.m: I bathe for the pacification of the disease of worldly existence, O Janārdana!" / "Homage to the imperishable banyan tree, the granter of imperishable heaven,

115.s:
pitrādīnāmakṣayāya sarvapāpakṣayāya ca /
śrāddhaṃ vaṭatale(4) kuryād brāhmaṇānāñca bhojanaṃ //
115.d:
पित्रादीनामक्षयाय सर्वपापक्षयाय च /
श्राद्धं वटतले(4) कुर्याद् ब्राह्मणानाञ्च भोजनं //
115.m: For the imperishable benefit of father and other ancestors, and for the destruction of all sins!" / One should perform an ancestral rite at the foot of the banyan tree and feed brahmins.

115.s:
ekasmin bhojite vipre koṭirbhavati bhojitā /
kimpunarbahubhirbhuktaiḥ pitṝṇāṃ dattamakṣayaṃ //
:n
1 pretarājetyādiḥ, svapitṝṃstathetyantaḥ pāṭho jha.. pustake
nāsti
2 śubhakarmavivarjitā iti jha..
3 piṇḍenāneneti ṅa..
4 vaṭataṭe iti ja..
:p 8
115.d:
एकस्मिन् भोजिते विप्रे कोटिर्भवति भोजिता /
किम्पुनर्बहुभिर्भुक्तैः पितॄणां दत्तमक्षयं //
:न्
1 प्रेतराजेत्यादिः, स्वपितॄंस्तथेत्यन्तः पाठो झ.. पुस्तके
नास्ति
2 शुभकर्मविवर्जिता इति झ..
3 पिण्डेनानेनेति ङ..
4 वटतटे इति ज..
:प् 8
115.m:
When one brahmin is fed, ten million are fed; / what then when many have eaten? That which is given to the ancestors becomes imperishable.
[Footnote]
1 The passage beginning with 'pretarāja' and ending with 'svapitṝṃstathā' is absent in manuscript jha.
2 'Destitute of auspicious deeds' [śubhakarmavivarjitāḥ] thus in manuscript jha.
3 'By this funeral cake' [piṇḍenānena] thus in manuscript ṅa.
4 'On the bank of the banyan tree' [vaṭataṭe] thus in manuscript ja.

115.s:
gayāyāmannadātā yaḥ pitarastena putriṇaḥ /
vaṭaṃ vaṭeśvaraṃ natvā pūjayet prapitāmahaṃ //
115.d:
गयायामन्नदाता यः पितरस्तेन पुत्रिणः /
वटं वटेश्वरं नत्वा पूजयेत् प्रपितामहं //
115.m: He who gives food at Gayā—through him the ancestors possess a son. / Having bowed to the banyan tree and to Vaṭeśvara, one should worship the great-grandfather [Brahmā].

115.s:
akṣayāṃllabhate lokān kulānāṃ śatamuddharet /
kramato 'kramato vāpi gayāyatrā mahāphalā //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe gayāmāhātmye gayayātrā nāma
pañcadaśādhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha ṣoḍaśādhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
gayāyātrāvidhiḥ
115.d:
अक्षयांल्लभते लोकान् कुलानां शतमुद्धरेत् /
क्रमतो ऽक्रमतो वापि गयायत्रा महाफला //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे गयामाहात्म्ये गययात्रा नाम
पञ्चदशाधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ षोडशाधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
गयायात्राविधिः
115.m:
He attains imperishable worlds and delivers a hundred families. / In due order or out of order, the pilgrimage to Gayā bears great fruit.
Thus ends the one hundred and fifteenth chapter, entitled 'The Pilgrimage to Gayā', in the greatness of Gayā in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now the one hundred and sixteenth chapter.
The Rules for the Pilgrimage to Gayā.

116.s:
agnir uvāca
gāyatryaiva mahānadyāṃ snātaḥ(1) sandhyāṃ samācaret /
gāyatryā agrataḥ prātaḥ śrāddhaṃ piṇḍamathākṣayaṃ //
116.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
गायत्र्यैव महानद्यां स्नातः(1) सन्ध्यां समाचरेत् /
गायत्र्या अग्रतः प्रातः श्राद्धं पिण्डमथाक्षयं //
116.m: Agni said: / Having bathed in the Mahānadī along with [recitation of] the Gāyatrī, one should perform the twilight devotion. / In front of Gāyatrī in the morning, [one should perform] the ancestral rite and the imperishable funeral cake.

116.s:
madhyāhne codyati(2) snātvā gītavādyair hyupāsya ca /
sāvitrīpurataḥ sandhyāṃ piṇḍadānañca tatpade //
116.d:
मध्याह्ने चोद्यति(2) स्नात्वा गीतवाद्यैर् ह्युपास्य च /
सावित्रीपुरतः सन्ध्यां पिण्डदानञ्च तत्पदे //
116.m: And having bathed at midday at Udyanta and worshipped with songs and musical instruments, / [one should perform] the twilight devotion before Sāvitrī and the offering of funeral cakes at her footstep.

116.s:
agastyasya pade kuryādyonidvāraṃ praviśya ca /
nirgato na punaryoniṃ praviśenmucyate bhavāt(3) //
:n
1 prāta iti ka..
2 madhyāhne sarasīti ga..
3 mucyate bhayāditi cha.. , jha.. ca
:p 9
116.d:
अगस्त्यस्य पदे कुर्याद्योनिद्वारं प्रविश्य च /
निर्गतो न पुनर्योनिं प्रविशेन्मुच्यते भवात्(3) //
:न्
1 प्रात इति क..
2 मध्याह्ने सरसीति ग..
3 मुच्यते भयादिति छ.. , झ.. च
:प् 9
116.m:
One should do so at the footstep of Agastya, and having entered the womb-gate, / having emerged, one does not enter the womb again; he is freed from worldly existence.
[Footnote]
1. "prātaḥ" thus in manuscript ka.
2. "madhyāhne sarasi" thus in manuscript ga.
3. "mucyate bhayāt" thus in manuscripts cha and jha.

116.s:
baliṃ kākaśilāyāñca kumārañca namettataḥ(1) /
svargadvāryāṃ somakuṇḍe vāyutīrthe 'tha piṇḍadaḥ //
116.d:
बलिं काकशिलायाञ्च कुमारञ्च नमेत्ततः(1) /
स्वर्गद्वार्यां सोमकुण्डे वायुतीर्थे ऽथ पिण्डदः //
116.m: Then, having offered an oblation at Kākaśilā, one should bow to Kumāra. / Then, offering funeral cakes at Svargadvārī, Somakuṇḍa, and Vāyutīrtha,

116.s:
bhavedākaśagaṅgāyāṃ kapilāyāñca piṇḍadaḥ /
kapileśaṃ śivaṃ natvā rukmikuṇḍe ca piṇḍadaḥ //
116.d:
भवेदाकशगङ्गायां कपिलायाञ्च पिण्डदः /
कपिलेशं शिवं नत्वा रुक्मिकुण्डे च पिण्डदः //
116.m: one should offer funeral cakes at Ākāśagaṅgā and Kapilā; / and having bowed to Śiva as Kapileśa, one should offer funeral cakes at Rukmikuṇḍa.

116.s:
koṭītīrthe ca koṭīśaṃ natvāmoghapade naraḥ(2) /
gadālole vānarake gopracāre ca piṇḍadaḥ(3) //
116.d:
कोटीतीर्थे च कोटीशं नत्वामोघपदे नरः(2) /
गदालोले वानरके गोप्रचारे च पिण्डदः(3) //
116.m: And bowing to Koṭīśa at Koṭītīrtha, a man [offers funeral cakes] at the footprint of Amogha; / he should offer funeral cakes at Gadālola, Vānaraka, and Gopracāra.

116.s:
natvā gāvaṃ vaitaraṇyāmekaviṃśakuloddhṛtiḥ /
śrāddhapiṇḍapradātā(4) syāt krauñcapade ca piṇḍadaḥ(5) //
116.d:
नत्वा गावं वैतरण्यामेकविंशकुलोद्धृतिः /
श्राद्धपिण्डप्रदाता(4) स्यात् क्रौञ्चपदे च पिण्डदः(5) //
116.m: Having bowed to the cow at the Vaitaraṇī, he delivers twenty-one generations; / he should become an offerer of ancestral rites and cakes, and offer funeral cakes at Krauñcapada.

116.s:
tṛtīyāyāṃ viśālāyāṃ niścirāyāñca piṇḍadaḥ /
ṛṇamokṣe pāpamokṣe bhasmakuṇḍe 'tha bhasmanā //
116.d:
तृतीयायां विशालायां निश्चिरायाञ्च पिण्डदः /
ऋणमोक्षे पापमोक्षे भस्मकुण्डे ऽथ भस्मना //
116.m: He should offer funeral cakes at Tṛtīyā, Viśālā, and Niścirā. / Then, bathing with ashes at Bhasmakuṇḍa, at the [sites for] release from debt and release from sin,

116.s:
snānakṛn mucyate pāpānnameddevaṃ janārdanam /
eṣa piṇḍo mayā dattastava haste janārdana //
116.d:
स्नानकृन् मुच्यते पापान्नमेद्देवं जनार्दनम् /
एष पिण्डो मया दत्तस्तव हस्ते जनार्दन //
116.m: one who has bathed is freed from sin; he should bow to the god Janārdana: / 'This funeral cake is offered by me into your hand, O Janārdana!

116.s:
paralokagate mahyamakṣyayyamupatiṣṭhatāṃ /
gayāyāṃ pitṛrūpeṇa svayameva janārdanaḥ //
116.d:
परलोकगते मह्यमक्ष्यय्यमुपतिष्ठतां /
गयायां पितृरूपेण स्वयमेव जनार्दनः //
116.m: May imperishable [merit] accrue to me who have gone to the other world.' / At Gayā, Janārdana himself [is present] in the form of the ancestors;

116.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ mucyate vai ṛṇatrayāt /
mārkaṇḍeyeśvaraṃ natvā namedgṛdhreśvaraṃ naraḥ(6) //
116.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा पुण्डरीकाक्षं मुच्यते वै ऋणत्रयात् /
मार्कण्डेयेश्वरं नत्वा नमेद्गृध्रेश्वरं नरः(6) //
116.m: having seen that lotus-eyed one, one is truly released from the three debts. / Having bowed to Mārkaṇḍeyeśvara, a man should bow to Gṛdhreśvara.

116.s:
mūlakṣetre maheśasya dhārāyāṃ piṇḍado bhavet /
:n
1 namennara iti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , cha.. ca
2 māsapade 'nnada iti kha.. , gha.. ca
3 kapileśamityādiḥ, gopracāre ca piṇḍada ity antaḥ pāṭho ga..
pustake nāsti
4 śrāddhe piṇḍapradateti kha..
5 bhavedākāśagaṅgāyāmaityādiḥ, krauñcapāde ca piṇḍada ity
antaḥ pāṭhaḥ cha.. pustake nāsti
6 namedbhūteśvaraṃ nara iti gha..
:p 10
(1)gṛdhrakūṭe gṛdhravaṭe dhautapāde ca piṇḍadaḥ //
116.d:
मूलक्षेत्रे महेशस्य धारायां पिण्डदो भवेत् /
:न्
1 नमेन्नर इति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , छ.. च
2 मासपदे ऽन्नद इति ख.. , घ.. च
3 कपिलेशमित्यादिः, गोप्रचारे च पिण्डद इत्य् अन्तः पाठो ग..
पुस्तके नास्ति
4 श्राद्धे पिण्डप्रदतेति ख..
5 भवेदाकाशगङ्गायामैत्यादिः, क्रौञ्चपादे च पिण्डद इत्य्
अन्तः पाठः छ.. पुस्तके नास्ति
6 नमेद्भूतेश्वरं नर इति घ..
:प् 10
(1)गृध्रकूटे गृध्रवटे धौतपादे च पिण्डदः //
116.m:
In the root sacred site of Maheśa, he should offer funeral cakes at the stream.
[Footnote]
1. "namennaraḥ" thus in manuscripts kha, ga, gha, ṅa, and cha.
2. "māsapade 'nnadaḥ" thus in manuscripts kha and gha.
3 The reading beginning with “kapileśam” and ending with “gopracāre ca piṇḍadaḥ” is not found in manuscript ga.
4 “śrāddhe piṇḍapradatā” in manuscript kha.
5 The reading beginning with “bhavedākāśagaṅgāyām” and ending with “krauñcapāde ca piṇḍadaḥ” is not found in manuscript cha.
6 “namedbhūteśvaraṃ naraḥ” in manuscript gha.
:p 10
One should offer a funerary ball at Gṛdhrakūṭa, at Gṛdhravaṭa, and at Dhautapāda.

116.s:
puṣkariṇyāṃ kardamāle rāmatīrthe ca piṇḍadaḥ /
prabhāseśannamet pretaśilāyāṃ piṇḍado bhavet //
116.d:
पुष्करिण्यां कर्दमाले रामतीर्थे च पिण्डदः /
प्रभासेशन्नमेत् प्रेतशिलायां पिण्डदो भवेत् //
116.m: One should offer a funerary ball at the Puṣkariṇī, at Kardamāla, and at Rāmatīrtha. / One should bow to Prabhāseśa, and should offer a funerary ball upon the Pretaśilā.

116.s:
divyāntarīkṣabhūmiṣṭhāḥ pitaro bāndhavādayaḥ /
pretādirūpā muktāḥ(2) syuḥ piṇḍair dattair mayākhilāḥ //
116.d:
दिव्यान्तरीक्षभूमिष्ठाः पितरो बान्धवादयः /
प्रेतादिरूपा मुक्ताः(2) स्युः पिण्डैर् दत्तैर् मयाखिलाः //
116.m: “May all my ancestors, kinsmen, and others—those dwelling in heaven, the atmosphere, or on earth, / [even] those in the form of ghosts—be liberated by the funerary balls offered by me!”

116.s:
sthānatraye pretaśilā gayāśirasi pāvanī /
prabhāse pretakuṇḍe ca piṇḍadastārayet kulam //
116.d:
स्थानत्रये प्रेतशिला गयाशिरसि पावनी /
प्रभासे प्रेतकुण्डे च पिण्डदस्तारयेत् कुलम् //
116.m: The purifying Pretaśilā is in three places at Gayāśiras; / offering a funerary ball at Prabhāsa and at Pretakuṇḍa, one delivers one's family line.

116.s:
vasiṣṭheśannamaskṛtya tadagre piṇḍado bhavet /
gayānābhau suṣumṇāyāṃ mahākoṣṭyāñca piṇḍadaḥ //
116.d:
वसिष्ठेशन्नमस्कृत्य तदग्रे पिण्डदो भवेत् /
गयानाभौ सुषुम्णायां महाकोष्ट्याञ्च पिण्डदः //
116.m: Having bowed to Vasiṣṭheśa, one should offer a funerary ball before him; / one should offer a funerary ball at the navel of Gayā, at Suṣumṇā, and at the Mahākoṣṭhī;

116.s:
gadādharāgrato muṇḍapṛṣṭhe devyāś ca sannidhau /
muṇdapṛṣṭhaṃ namedādau kṣetrapālādisaṃyutam //
116.d:
गदाधराग्रतो मुण्डपृष्ठे देव्याश् च सन्निधौ /
मुण्दपृष्ठं नमेदादौ क्षेत्रपालादिसंयुतम् //
116.m: in front of Gadādhara, upon Muṇḍapṛṣṭha, and in the presence of the Goddess. / One should first bow to Muṇḍapṛṣṭha together with the protector of the site and others;

116.s:
pūjayitvā bhayaṃ na syādviṣarogādināśanam /
brahmāṇañca namaskṛtya brahmalokaṃ nayet kulam //
116.d:
पूजयित्वा भयं न स्याद्विषरोगादिनाशनम् /
ब्रह्माणञ्च नमस्कृत्य ब्रह्मलोकं नयेत् कुलम् //
116.m: having worshipped [it], there will be no fear, and poison, illness, and the like will be destroyed. / And having bowed to Brahmā, one leads one's family line to the realm of Brahmā.

116.s:
subhadrāṃ balabhadrañca prapūjya puruṣottamam /
sarvakāmasamāyuktaḥ kulamuddhṛtya nākabhāk(3) //
116.d:
सुभद्रां बलभद्रञ्च प्रपूज्य पुरुषोत्तमम् /
सर्वकामसमायुक्तः कुलमुद्धृत्य नाकभाक्(3) //
116.m: Having worshipped Subhadrā, Balabhadra, and Puruṣottama, / endowed with all desires, having delivered one's family line, one partakes of heaven.

116.s:
hṛṣīkeśaṃ namaskṛtya tadagre piṇḍado bhavet /
mādhavaṃ pūjayitvā ca devo vaimāniko(4) bhavet //
116.d:
हृषीकेशं नमस्कृत्य तदग्रे पिण्डदो भवेत् /
माधवं पूजयित्वा च देवो वैमानिको(4) भवेत् //
116.m: Having bowed to Hṛṣīkeśa, one should offer a funerary ball before him; / and having worshipped Mādhava, one becomes a deity traveling in a celestial chariot.

116.s:
mahālakṣmīṃ prārcya gaurīṃ maṅgalāñca sarasvatīm /
pitṝnuddhṛtya svargastho bhuktabhogo 'tra śāstradhīḥ //
:n
1 sarvakāmasamāyuktaḥ kulamuddhṛtya lokabhāgiti pāṭhotra jha..
pustake 'dhiko 'sti
2 pretādirūpamuktā iti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , ja.. ca
3 kulamuddhṛtya lokabhāgiti ga.. , ja.. ca / vaśiṣṭheśamityādiḥ,
kulamuddhṛtya nākabhāgityantaḥ pāṭho jha.. pustake nāsti
4 devair vaimānika iti cha..
:p 11
116.d:
महालक्ष्मीं प्रार्च्य गौरीं मङ्गलाञ्च सरस्वतीम् /
पितॄनुद्धृत्य स्वर्गस्थो भुक्तभोगो ऽत्र शास्त्रधीः //
:न्
1 सर्वकामसमायुक्तः कुलमुद्धृत्य लोकभागिति पाठोत्र झ..
पुस्तके ऽधिको ऽस्ति
2 प्रेतादिरूपमुक्ता इति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , ज.. च
3 कुलमुद्धृत्य लोकभागिति ग.. , ज.. च / वशिष्ठेशमित्यादिः,
कुलमुद्धृत्य नाकभागित्यन्तः पाठो झ.. पुस्तके नास्ति
4 देवैर् वैमानिक इति छ..
:प् 11
116.m:
Having worshipped Mahālakṣmī, Gaurī, Maṅgalā, and Sarasvatī, / having delivered one's ancestors, one resides in heaven; having enjoyed worldly pleasures here, one's intellect is established in the scriptures.
:n
1 The reading “sarvakāmasamāyuktaḥ kulamuddhṛtya lokabhāk” is found as an addition here in manuscript jha.
2 “pretādirūpamuktāḥ” in manuscripts kha, ga, gha, ṅa, and ja.
3 “kulamuddhṛtya lokabhāk” in manuscripts ga and ja. / The reading beginning with “vaśiṣṭheśam” and ending with “kulamuddhṛtya nākabhāk” is not found in manuscript jha.
4 “devair vaimānikaḥ” in manuscript cha.
:p 11

116.s:
dvādaśādityamabhyarya vahniṃ revantamindrakam /
rogādimuktaḥ svargī syācchrīkapardivināyakam //
116.d:
द्वादशादित्यमभ्यर्य वह्निं रेवन्तमिन्द्रकम् /
रोगादिमुक्तः स्वर्गी स्याच्छ्रीकपर्दिविनायकम् //
116.m: Having worshipped the twelve suns, fire, Revanta, and Indra, / freed from diseases and the like, one will go to heaven; having worshipped glorious Kapardivināyaka

116.s:
prapūjya kārttikeyañca nirvighnaḥ siddhimāpnuyāt /
somanāthañca kāleśaṅkedāraṃ prapitāmaham //
116.d:
प्रपूज्य कार्त्तिकेयञ्च निर्विघ्नः सिद्धिमाप्नुयात् /
सोमनाथञ्च कालेशङ्केदारं प्रपितामहम् //
116.m: and Kārttikeya, one will obtain perfection without obstacles. / Somanātha, Kāleśa, Kedāra, Prapitāmaha,

116.s:
siddheśvarañca rudreśaṃ rāmeśaṃ brahmakeśvaram /
aṣṭaliṅgāni guhyāni pūjayitvā tu(1) sarvabhāk //
116.d:
सिद्धेश्वरञ्च रुद्रेशं रामेशं ब्रह्मकेश्वरम् /
अष्टलिङ्गानि गुह्यानि पूजयित्वा तु(1) सर्वभाक् //
116.m: Siddheśvara, Rudreśa, Rāmeśa, and Brahmakeśvara— / having worshipped these eight secret liṅgas, one attains everything.

116.s:
nārāyaṇaṃ varāhañca nārasiṃhaṃ namecchriye /
brahmaviṣṇumaheśākhyaṃ tripuraghnamaśeṣadam //
116.d:
नारायणं वराहञ्च नारसिंहं नमेच्छ्रिये /
ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेशाख्यं त्रिपुरघ्नमशेषदम् //
116.m: For the sake of prosperity one should bow to Nārāyaṇa, Varāha, and Narasiṃha, / to the one known as Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa, the slayer of Tripura, who bestows everything.

116.s:
sītāṃ rāmañca garuḍaṃ vāmanaṃ samprapūjya ca /
sarvakāmānavāpnoti brahmalokaṃ nayet pitṝn //
116.d:
सीतां रामञ्च गरुडं वामनं सम्प्रपूज्य च /
सर्वकामानवाप्नोति ब्रह्मलोकं नयेत् पितॄन् //
116.m: And having fully worshipped Sītā, Rāma, Garuḍa, and Vāmana, / one obtains all desires and leads the ancestors to the realm of Brahmā.

116.s:
devaiḥ sārdhaṃ samprapūjya devamādigadādharam /
ṛṇatrayavinirmuktastārayet sakalaṃ kulam //
116.d:
देवैः सार्धं सम्प्रपूज्य देवमादिगदाधरम् /
ऋणत्रयविनिर्मुक्तस्तारयेत् सकलं कुलम् //
116.m: Having fully worshipped the primordial deity Gadādhara together with the gods, / freed from the three debts, one delivers one's entire family line.

116.s:
devarūpā śilā puṇyā tasmāddevamayī śilā /
gayāyāṃ nahi tat sthānaṃ yatra tīrthaṃ na vidyate //
116.d:
देवरूपा शिला पुण्या तस्माद्देवमयी शिला /
गयायां नहि तत् स्थानं यत्र तीर्थं न विद्यते //
116.m: The holy slab is of the form of the gods; therefore the slab is made of the deities. / There is no place in Gayā where there is no sacred ford.

116.s:
yannāmnā pātayet piṇḍaṃ tannayedbrahma śāśvatam /
phalgvīśaṃ phalgucaṇḍīṃ ca praṇamyāṅgārakeśvaram //
116.d:
यन्नाम्ना पातयेत् पिण्डं तन्नयेद्ब्रह्म शाश्वतम् /
फल्ग्वीशं फल्गुचण्डीं च प्रणम्याङ्गारकेश्वरम् //
116.m: In whose name one casts down a funerary ball, that [person] one leads to the eternal Brahman. / Having bowed to Phalgvīśa, Phalgucaṇḍī, and Aṅgārakeśvara,

116.s:
mataṅgasya pade śrāddhī bharatāśramake bhavet /
haṃsatīrthe koṭitīrthe yatra pāṇḍuśilānnadaḥ //
116.d:
मतङ्गस्य पदे श्राद्धी भरताश्रमके भवेत् /
हंसतीर्थे कोटितीर्थे यत्र पाण्डुशिलान्नदः //
116.m: the performer of the ancestral rite should go to the foot of Mataṅga and to the hermitage of Bharata; / at Haṃsatīrtha and at Koṭitīrtha, where the Pāṇḍu stone is, one gives food;

116.s:
tatra syādagnidhārāyāṃ madhusravasi piṇḍadaḥ /
rudreśaṃ kilikileśaṃ namedvṛddhivināyakam(2) //
116.d:
तत्र स्यादग्निधारायां मधुस्रवसि पिण्डदः /
रुद्रेशं किलिकिलेशं नमेद्वृद्धिविनायकम्(2) //
116.m: there, at Agnidhārā and at Madhusravas, one should offer a funerary ball; / one should bow to Rudreśa, Kilikileśa, and Vṛddhivināyaka.

116.s:
piṇḍado dhenukāraṇye pade dhenor namecca gām /
:n
1 pūjayitvātheti ka.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , ja.. ca
2 namedbuddhivināyakamiti kha.. , ga.. , cha.. ca / namedvṛddhavināyakamiti
gha..
:p 12
sarvān pitṝṃstārayecca sarasvatyāñca piṇḍadaḥ //
116.d:
पिण्डदो धेनुकारण्ये पदे धेनोर् नमेच्च गाम् /
:न्
1 पूजयित्वाथेति क.. , घ.. , ङ.. , ज.. च
2 नमेद्बुद्धिविनायकमिति ख.. , ग.. , छ.. च / नमेद्वृद्धविनायकमिति
घ..
:प् 12
सर्वान् पितॄंस्तारयेच्च सरस्वत्याञ्च पिण्डदः //
116.m:
Offering a funerary ball in Dhenukāraṇya at the foot of Dhenu, one should bow to the cow.
:n
1 “pūjayitvātha” in manuscripts ka, gha, ṅa, and ja.
2 “namedbuddhivināyakam” in manuscripts kha, ga, and cha; “namedvṛddhavināyakam” in manuscript gha.
:p 12
And offering a funerary ball at the Sarasvatī, one delivers all the ancestors.

116.s:
sandhyāmupāsya sāyāhne nameddevīṃ sarasvatīm /
trisandhyākṛdbhavedvipro vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ //
116.d:
सन्ध्यामुपास्य सायाह्ने नमेद्देवीं सरस्वतीम् /
त्रिसन्ध्याकृद्भवेद्विप्रो वेदवेदाङ्गपारगः //
116.m: Having performed the twilight ritual in the evening, one should bow to goddess Sarasvatī; / performing the three twilight rituals, the twice-born becomes one who has mastered the Vedas and their auxiliary branches.

116.s:
gayāṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya gayāviprān prapūjya ca /
annadānādikaṃ sarvaṃ kṛtantatrākṣayaṃ bhavet //
116.d:
गयां प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य गयाविप्रान् प्रपूज्य च /
अन्नदानादिकं सर्वं कृतन्तत्राक्षयं भवेत् //
116.m: Having circumambulated Gayā and worshipped the brāhmaṇas of Gayā, / all that is done—gifts of food and the like—becomes imperishable there.

116.s:
stutvā samprārthayedevamādidevaṃ gadādharam /
gadādharaṃ gayāvāsaṃ pitrādīnāṃ gatipradam //
116.d:
स्तुत्वा सम्प्रार्थयेदेवमादिदेवं गदाधरम् /
गदाधरं गयावासं पित्रादीनां गतिप्रदम् //
116.m: Having praised him, one should pray thus to Gadādhara, the primordial deity: / “To Gadādhara, dwelling in Gayā, who bestows the ultimate goal upon the ancestors and others,

116.s:
dharmārthakāmamokṣārthaṃ yogadaṃ praṇamāmyaham /
dehendriyamanobuddhiprāṇāhaṅkāravarjitam //
116.d:
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षार्थं योगदं प्रणमाम्यहम् /
देहेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिप्राणाहङ्कारवर्जितम् //
116.m: for the sake of dharma, material wealth, desire, and liberation, the bestower of yoga, I bow; / to the one free from body, senses, mind, intellect, life-breath, and ego,

116.s:
nityaśuddhaṃ buddhiyuktaṃ(1) satyaṃ brahma namāmyaham /
ānandamadvayaṃ devaṃ devadānavavanditam //
116.d:
नित्यशुद्धं बुद्धियुक्तं(1) सत्यं ब्रह्म नमाम्यहम् /
आनन्दमद्वयं देवं देवदानववन्दितम् //
116.m: eternally pure, endowed with consciousness, truth, the Brahman, I bow; / to the bliss, the non-dual God, praised by gods and demons,

116.s:
devadevīvṛndayuktaṃ sarvadā praṇamāmyaham /
kalikalmaṣakālārtidamanaṃ(2) vanamālinam //
116.d:
देवदेवीवृन्दयुक्तं सर्वदा प्रणमाम्यहम् /
कलिकल्मषकालार्तिदमनं(2) वनमालिनम् //
116.m: accompanied by the host of gods and goddesses, I bow at all times; / to the one who wears a garland of forest flowers, who subdues the afflictions of time and the stains of the Kali age,

116.s:
pālitākhilalokeśaṃ(3) kuloddharaṇamānasam /
vyaktāvyaktavibhaktātmāvibhaktātmānamātmani //
116.d:
पालिताखिललोकेशं(3) कुलोद्धरणमानसम् /
व्यक्ताव्यक्तविभक्तात्माविभक्तात्मानमात्मनि //
116.m: who protects the lord of all the worlds, whose mind is set upon delivering family lines, / whose Self is differentiated into manifest and unmanifest, yet whose Self is undivided within the Self,

116.s:
sthitaṃ sthirataraṃ(4) sāraṃ vande ghorāghamardanam(5) /
āgato 'smi gayāṃ deva pitṛkārye gadādharaḥ //
116.d:
स्थितं स्थिरतरं(4) सारं वन्दे घोराघमर्दनम्(5) /
आगतो ऽस्मि गयां देव पितृकार्ये गदाधरः //
116.m: who is stationed, exceedingly steadfast, the essence, the crusher of terrible sins, I praise! / O God Gadādhara, I have come to Gayā on ancestral business.

116.s:
tvaṃ me sākṣī bhavādyeha anṛṇo 'hamṛṇatrayāt /
:n
1 nityaśuddhabuddhiyuktamiti gha.. , cha.. ca
2 kālārtināśanamiti gha.. / kālārtidalanamiti ga.. , ṅa.. , gha.. , ja.. ca
3 pālitākhiladeveśamiti gha..
4 sthitataramiti ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. ca
5 vandehamarimardanamiti ṅa.. / vande saṃsāramardanamiti ja..
:p 13
sākṣiṇaḥ santu me devā brahmeśānādayas tathā //
116.d:
त्वं मे साक्षी भवाद्येह अनृणो ऽहमृणत्रयात् /
:न्
1 नित्यशुद्धबुद्धियुक्तमिति घ.. , छ.. च
2 कालार्तिनाशनमिति घ.. / कालार्तिदलनमिति ग.. , ङ.. , घ.. , ज.. च
3 पालिताखिलदेवेशमिति घ..
4 स्थिततरमिति ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. च
5 वन्देहमरिमर्दनमिति ङ.. / वन्दे संसारमर्दनमिति ज..
:प् 13
साक्षिणः सन्तु मे देवा ब्रह्मेशानादयस् तथा //
116.m:
Be my witness today, here; I am freed from the three debts!
:n
1 “nityaśuddhabuddhiyuktam” in manuscripts gha and cha.
2 “kālārtināśanam” in manuscript gha; “kālārtidalanam” in manuscripts ga, ṅa, gha, and ja.
3 “pālitākhiladeveśam” in manuscript gha.
4 “sthitataram” in manuscripts ga, gha, and ṅa.
5 “vandehamarimardanam” in manuscript ṅa; “vande saṃsāramardanam” in manuscript ja.
:p 13
May the gods, Brahmā, Īśāna, and the others, likewise be my witnesses!

116.s:
mayā gayāṃ samāsādya pitṝṇāṃ niṣkṛtiḥ kṛtā /
gayāmāhātmyapaṭhanācchrāddhādau brahmalokabhāk //
116.d:
मया गयां समासाद्य पितॄणां निष्कृतिः कृता /
गयामाहात्म्यपठनाच्छ्राद्धादौ ब्रह्मलोकभाक् //
116.m: Having arrived at Gayā, the redemption of the ancestors has been performed by me.” / From reciting this Gayā-māhātmya during an ancestral rite and the like, one partakes of the realm of Brahmā;

116.s:
pitṝṇāmakṣayaṃ śrāddhamakṣayaṃ brahmalokadam //43//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe gayāmāhātmye gayāyātrā nāma
ṣoḍaśādhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha saptadaśādhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
śrāddhakalpaḥ
116.d:
पितॄणामक्षयं श्राद्धमक्षयं ब्रह्मलोकदम् //43//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे गयामाहात्म्ये गयायात्रा नाम
षोडशाधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ सप्तदशाधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
श्राद्धकल्पः
116.m:
the ancestral rite for the ancestors is imperishable, and bestows the imperishable realm of Brahmā. //43
:e Thus in the holy Mahāpurāṇa of Agni, in the Glorification of Gayā, the hundred and sixteenth chapter, entitled “The Pilgrimage to Gayā.”
:ś Now the hundred and seventeenth chapter.
The procedure for ancestral rites.

117.s:
agnir uvāca
kātyāyanī munīnāha yathā śrāddhaṃ tathā vade /
gayādau śrāddhaṃ kurvīta saṅkrāntyādau viśeṣataḥ //
117.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
कात्यायनी मुनीनाह यथा श्राद्धं तथा वदे /
गयादौ श्राद्धं कुर्वीत सङ्क्रान्त्यादौ विशेषतः //
117.m:
Agni said:
As Kātyāyanī spoke to the sages, so will I declare the ancestral rite: / One should perform the ancestral rite at Gayā and other places, especially on the transition of the sun and other [astronomical occasions],

117.s:
kāle vāparapakṣe ca caturthyā ūrdhvameva va /
samyādya ca padarkṣe ca(1) pūrvedyuś ca nimantrayet //
117.d:
काले वापरपक्षे च चतुर्थ्या ऊर्ध्वमेव व /
सम्याद्य च पदर्क्षे च(1) पूर्वेद्युश् च निमन्त्रयेत् //
117.m: or in due season, or in the waning fortnight, particularly after the fourth lunar day, / and having properly assembled on the asterism of the [ancestor's] foot; and on the preceding day one should invite

117.s:
yatīn gṛhasthasādhūn vā snātakāñchrotriyān dvijān /
anavadyān karmaniṣṭhān śiṣṭānācārasaṃyutān(2) //
:n
1 sampādya paramarkṣe ceti cha..
2 ācārasaṃskṛtāniti ga.. , ja.. ca
:p 14
117.d:
यतीन् गृहस्थसाधून् वा स्नातकाञ्छ्रोत्रियान् द्विजान् /
अनवद्यान् कर्मनिष्ठान् शिष्टानाचारसंयुतान्(2) //
:न्
1 सम्पाद्य परमर्क्षे चेति छ..
2 आचारसंस्कृतानिति ग.. , ज.. च
:प् 14
117.m:
renunciants, or virtuous householders, twice-born students who have taken the ceremonial bath, learned brāhmaṇas, / blameless men dedicated to their duties, disciplined and endowed with correct conduct.
:n
1. "sampādya paramarkṣe ca" thus in manuscript cha.
2. "ācārasaṃskṛtān" thus in manuscripts ga and ja.

117.s:
varjayecchitrikuṣṭhyādīnna gṛhṇīyānnimantritān /
snātāñchucīṃs tathā dāntān prāṅmukhān devakarmaṇi //
117.d:
वर्जयेच्छित्रिकुष्ठ्यादीन्न गृह्णीयान्निमन्त्रितान् /
स्नाताञ्छुचींस् तथा दान्तान् प्राङ्मुखान् देवकर्मणि //
117.m: One should avoid those with white leprosy, leprosy, and the like, nor should one accept invited [guests]; / [one should seat] those who have bathed, are pure, self-controlled, facing east in the rites for gods.

117.s:
upaveśayettrīn pitryādīnekaikamubhayatra vā /
evaṃ mātāmahādeś ca śākair api ca kārayet //
117.d:
उपवेशयेत्त्रीन् पित्र्यादीनेकैकमुभयत्र वा /
एवं मातामहादेश् च शाकैर् अपि च कारयेत् //
117.m: He should seat three for the ancestors and others, or one in each of the two [rites]; / he should also do likewise for maternal grandfathers and others, even with [mere] vegetables.

117.s:
tadahni brahmacārī syādakopo 'tvarito mṛduḥ(1) /
satyo 'pramatto 'nadhvanyo asvādhyāyaś ca(2) vāgyataḥ //
117.d:
तदह्नि ब्रह्मचारी स्यादकोपो ऽत्वरितो मृदुः(1) /
सत्यो ऽप्रमत्तो ऽनध्वन्यो अस्वाध्यायश् च(2) वाग्यतः //
117.m: On that day he should be celibate, free from anger, unhurried, gentle, / truthful, attentive, not traveling, abstaining from Vedic recitation, and silent.

117.s:
sarvāṃś ca paṅktimūrdhanyān pṛcchet praśne tathāsane /
darbhānāstīrya dviguṇān pitre devādikañcaret //
117.d:
सर्वांश् च पङ्क्तिमूर्धन्यान् पृच्छेत् प्रश्ने तथासने /
दर्भानास्तीर्य द्विगुणान् पित्रे देवादिकञ्चरेत् //
117.m: And he should consult all those foremost in the row concerning the question and the seating; / having spread doubled darbha-grass, he should perform [the rites] for the ancestors, beginning with the gods.

117.s:
viśvāndevānāvāhayiṣye pṛcchedāvāhayeti ca /
viśvedevāsa āvāhya vikīryātha yavān japet //
117.d:
विश्वान्देवानावाहयिष्ये पृच्छेदावाहयेति च /
विश्वेदेवास आवाह्य विकीर्याथ यवान् जपेत् //
117.m: He should ask, 'I shall invite the All-gods,' and [the reply is], 'Invite them'; / having invited them with 'viśve devāsaḥ' and scattered barley, he should recite:

117.s:
viśve devāḥ śṛṇutemaṃ pitṝnāvāhayiṣye ca /
pṛcchedāvāhayetyukte uśantastvā samāhvayet //
117.d:
विश्वे देवाः शृणुतेमं पितॄनावाहयिष्ये च /
पृच्छेदावाहयेत्युक्ते उशन्तस्त्वा समाह्वयेत् //
117.m: 'viśve devāḥ śṛṇutemaṃ'. Then [saying], 'I shall invite the ancestors,' / he should ask; when it is said, 'Invite them,' he should invoke them with 'uśantas tvā'.

117.s:
tilān vikīryātha japedāyāntvityādi pitrake /
sapitritre niṣiñcedvā śanno devīrabhi tṛcā //
117.d:
तिलान् विकीर्याथ जपेदायान्त्वित्यादि पित्रके /
सपित्रित्रे निषिञ्चेद्वा शन्नो देवीरभि तृचा //
117.m: Having scattered sesame seeds, he should recite 'āyāntu' and so forth for the ancestors; / or he should sprinkle on the ring-finger [kuśa ring] with the triplet 'śanno devīr abhiṣṭaye'.

117.s:
yavo 'sīti yavān datvā pitre sarvatra vai tilān /
tilo 'si somadevatyo gosavo devanirmitaḥ /
pratnamadbhiḥ pṛktaḥ svadhayā pitṝn lokān prīṇāhi naḥ
svadhā / iti
śrīś ca teti dadetpuṣpaṃ pātre haime 'tha rājate //
117.d:
यवो ऽसीति यवान् दत्वा पित्रे सर्वत्र वै तिलान् /
तिलो ऽसि सोमदेवत्यो गोसवो देवनिर्मितः /
प्रत्नमद्भिः पृक्तः स्वधया पितॄन् लोकान् प्रीणाहि नः
स्वधा / इति
श्रीश् च तेति ददेत्पुष्पं पात्रे हैमे ऽथ राजते //

117.s:
audumvare vā khaḍge vā parṇapātre pradakṣiṇam /
devānāmapasavyaṃ tu pitṝṇāṃ savyamācaret //
:n
1 atvarito 'tyṛjuriti ṅa..
2 satye prapanno 'nadhvanyo hy asvādhyāyaśceti kha.. , gha.. ca
:p 15
117.d:
औदुम्वरे वा खड्गे वा पर्णपात्रे प्रदक्षिणम् /
देवानामपसव्यं तु पितॄणां सव्यमाचरेत् //
:न्
1 अत्वरितो ऽत्यृजुरिति ङ..
2 सत्ये प्रपन्नो ऽनध्वन्यो ह्य् अस्वाध्यायश्चेति ख.. , घ.. च
:प् 15
117.m:
or in one of udumbara wood, rhinoceros horn, or leaves, from left to right; / he should perform [the rites] for the gods with the sacred thread on the left, but for the ancestors on the right.
[Footnote]
1. "atvarito 'tyṛjuḥ" thus in manuscript ṅa.
2. "satye prapanno 'nadhvanyo hyasvādhyāyaśca" thus in manuscripts kha and gha.

117.s:
ekaikasya ekaikena sapavitrakareṣu ca /
yā divyā āpaḥ payasā sambabhūvuryā antarikṣā
utapārthivīryāḥ
hiraṇyavarṇā yajñiyāstā na āpaḥ śivāḥ saṃśyonāḥ
suhavā bhavantu ||
viśve devā eṣa vo 'rghaḥ svāhā ca pitareṣa te //
117.d:
एकैकस्य एकैकेन सपवित्रकरेषु च /
या दिव्या आपः पयसा सम्बभूवुर्या अन्तरिक्षा
उतपार्थिवीर्याः
हिरण्यवर्णा यज्ञियास्ता न आपः शिवाः संश्योनाः
सुहवा भवन्तु ||
विश्वे देवा एष वो ऽर्घः स्वाहा च पितरेष ते //
117.m:
For each [ancestor], into their hands provided with the sacred grass ring, one by one:
'May those celestial waters that arose with milk, those of the intermediate realm, / and those of the earth, golden-coloured, worthy of sacrifice—may those waters be auspicious, gentle, and easily invoked for us.'
'O All-gods, this is your water offering, svāhā! And O father, this is yours!'

117.s:
avadhaivaṃ pitāmahadeḥ saṃsravāt prathame caret(1) /
pitṛbhyaḥ sthānamasīti nyubjaṃ pātraṃ karotyadhaḥ //
117.d:
अवधैवं पितामहदेः संस्रवात् प्रथमे चरेत्(1) /
पितृभ्यः स्थानमसीति न्युब्जं पात्रं करोत्यधः //
117.m: Downwards in this manner from the grandfather and others, he should perform it from the dripping in the first [vessel]; / saying, 'You are the resting place for the ancestors,' he turns the vessel upside down below.

117.s:
atra gandhapuṣpadhūpadīpācchādanadānakaṃ /
ghṛtāktamannamuddhṛtya pṛcchatyagnau kariṣye ca //
117.d:
अत्र गन्धपुष्पधूपदीपाच्छादनदानकं /
घृताक्तमन्नमुद्धृत्य पृच्छत्यग्नौ करिष्ये च //
117.m: Here [is] the giving of fragrance, flowers, incense, light, and covering; / having taken up food smeared with clarified butter, he asks: 'I shall perform [it] in the fire.'

117.s:
kuruṣvetyabhyanujñāto juhuyātsāgniko 'nale /
anagnikaḥ pitṛhaste(2) sapavitre tu mantrataḥ //
117.d:
कुरुष्वेत्यभ्यनुज्ञातो जुहुयात्साग्निको ऽनले /
अनग्निकः पितृहस्ते(2) सपवित्रे तु मन्त्रतः //
117.m: Permitted with 'Perform it!', one who maintains a sacred fire should sacrifice in the fire; / one without a sacred fire [should sacrifice] into the hand of the ancestor [priest] with the sacred grass ring, using the mantra.

117.s:
agnaye kavyavāhanāya svāheti(3) prathamāhutiḥ /
somāya pitṛmate 'tha yamāyāṅgirase pare //
117.d:
अग्नये कव्यवाहनाय स्वाहेति(3) प्रथमाहुतिः /
सोमाय पितृमते ऽथ यमायाङ्गिरसे परे //
117.m: 'To Agni, conveyor of the kavyas, svāhā!' is the first oblation; / then 'To Soma accompanied by the ancestors,' and the next 'To Yama, descendant of Aṅgiras.'

117.s:
hutaśeṣaṃ cānnapātre datvā pātraṃ samālabhet /
pṛthivī te pātrandyauḥ pidhānaṃ brāhmaṇasya mukhe amṛte
amṛtaṃ juhomi svāheti
japtvedaṃ viṣṇurityanne dvijāṅguṣṭhanniveśayet //
117.d:
हुतशेषं चान्नपात्रे दत्वा पात्रं समालभेत् /
पृथिवी ते पात्रन्द्यौः पिधानं ब्राह्मणस्य मुखे अमृते
अमृतं जुहोमि स्वाहेति
जप्त्वेदं विष्णुरित्यन्ने द्विजाङ्गुष्ठन्निवेशयेत् //
117.m:
Having placed the remainder of the oblation into the food vessel, he should touch the vessel:
'The earth is your vessel, heaven is the cover; in the mouth of the brāhmaṇa, into the nectar, I offer nectar, svāhā!'—thus.
Having recited this, saying 'Viṣṇu', he should place the thumb of the brāhmaṇa into the food.

117.s:
apahateti ca tilān vikīryānnaṃ pradāyayet /
juṣadhvamiti coktvātha gāyatryādi tato japet //
:n
1 ekaikasyetyādiḥ, prathame caredityantaḥ pāṭho jha.. pustake nāsti
2 anagniko jale caiveti ṅa..
3 svadheti ka..
:p 16
117.d:
अपहतेति च तिलान् विकीर्यान्नं प्रदाययेत् /
जुषध्वमिति चोक्त्वाथ गायत्र्यादि ततो जपेत् //
:न्
1 एकैकस्येत्यादिः, प्रथमे चरेदित्यन्तः पाठो झ.. पुस्तके नास्ति
2 अनग्निको जले चैवेति ङ..
3 स्वधेति क..
:प् 16
117.m:
Saying 'Destroyed [are the asuras]' and scattering sesame seeds, he should cause the food to be served; / and having said 'Enjoy it!', he should then recite the Gāyatrī and other verses.
[Footnote]
1. The passage beginning with "ekaikasya" up to "prathame caret" is missing in manuscript jha.
2. "anagniko jale caiva" thus in manuscript ṅa. / 3. "svadhā" thus in manuscript ka.

117.s:
devatābhyaḥ pitṛbhyaś ca mahāyogibhya eva ca /
namaḥ svadhāyai svāhayai nityameva namo namaḥ(1) //
117.d:
देवताभ्यः पितृभ्यश् च महायोगिभ्य एव च /
नमः स्वधायै स्वाहयै नित्यमेव नमो नमः(1) //
117.m: 'To the deities, to the ancestors, and to the great yogins, / homage to svadhā, to svāhā, homage, homage forever!'

117.s:
tṛptān jñātvānnaṃ vikiredapo dadyāt sakṛt sakṛt /
gāyatrīṃ pūrvavajjaptvā madhu madhviti vai japet //
117.d:
तृप्तान् ज्ञात्वान्नं विकिरेदपो दद्यात् सकृत् सकृत् /
गायत्रीं पूर्ववज्जप्त्वा मधु मध्विति वै जपेत् //
117.m: Knowing them to be satisfied, he should scatter food and offer water once and again; / having recited the Gāyatrī as before, he should indeed recite 'madhu madhu'.

117.s:
tṛptāḥ stha iti sampṛcchettṛptāḥ sma iti vai vadet /
śeṣamannamanujñāpya sarvamannamathaikataḥ //
117.d:
तृप्ताः स्थ इति सम्पृच्छेत्तृप्ताः स्म इति वै वदेत् /
शेषमन्नमनुज्ञाप्य सर्वमन्नमथैकतः //
117.m: He should ask, 'Are you satisfied?'; [the guest] should say, 'We are satisfied.' / Having asked permission regarding the remaining food, [gathering] all the food together in one place,

117.s:
uddhṛtyocchiṣṭapārśve tu kṛtvā caivāvanejanaṃ /
dadyātkuśeṣu trīn piṇḍānācānteṣu pare jaguḥ //
117.d:
उद्धृत्योच्छिष्टपार्श्वे तु कृत्वा चैवावनेजनं /
दद्यात्कुशेषु त्रीन् पिण्डानाचान्तेषु परे जगुः //
117.m: and having taken it up near the remnants and performed the cleansing with water, / he should place three funeral cakes on kuśa grass; others have declared [this should be done] when they have sipped water.

117.s:
ācānteṣūdakaṃ puṣpāṇyakṣatāni pradāpayet /
akṣayyodakamevātha āśiṣaḥ prārthayennaraḥ(2) //
117.d:
आचान्तेषूदकं पुष्पाण्यक्षतानि प्रदापयेत् /
अक्षय्योदकमेवाथ आशिषः प्रार्थयेन्नरः(2) //
117.m: When they have sipped water, he should give water, flowers, and unbroken grains; / then [giving] the imperishable water, a man should request blessings:

117.s:
aghorāḥ pitaraḥ santu gotranno vardhatāṃ sadā /
dātāro no 'bhivardhantāṃ vedāḥ santatireva ca //
117.d:
अघोराः पितरः सन्तु गोत्रन्नो वर्धतां सदा /
दातारो नो ऽभिवर्धन्तां वेदाः सन्ततिरेव च //
117.m: 'May our ancestors be benign; may our lineage ever flourish! / May our givers increase, as well as the Vedas and our progeny!

117.s:
śraddhā ca no māvyagamadbahudeyaṃ ca no 'stviti /
annañca no bahu bhavedatithīṃś ca labhemahi //
117.d:
श्रद्धा च नो माव्यगमद्बहुदेयं च नो ऽस्त्विति /
अन्नञ्च नो बहु भवेदतिथींश् च लभेमहि //
117.m: And may faith not depart from us, and may there be much for us to give! / May we have abundant food, and may we receive guests!

117.s:
yācitāraś ca naḥ santu mā ca yācisma kañcana /
svadhāvācanīyān kuśānāstīrya sapavitrakān(3) //
117.d:
याचितारश् च नः सन्तु मा च याचिस्म कञ्चन /
स्वधावाचनीयान् कुशानास्तीर्य सपवित्रकान्(3) //
117.m: May we have supplicants, and may we never beg from anyone!' / Having spread the kuśa grass for the svadhā-recitation along with sacred grass rings,

117.s:
svadhāṃ vācayiṣye pṛcchedanujñātaś ca vācyatāṃ /
pitṛbhyaḥ pitāmahebhyaḥ prapitāmahamukhyake //
117.d:
स्वधां वाचयिष्ये पृच्छेदनुज्ञातश् च वाच्यतां /
पितृभ्यः पितामहेभ्यः प्रपितामहमुख्यके //
117.m: he should ask, 'I shall cause the svadhā to be recited,' and being permitted, 'Let it be recited,' / for the ancestors, grandfathers, and primarily the great-grandfathers:

117.s:
svadhocyatāmastu svadhā ucyamānastathaiva ca /
apo niṣiñceduttānaṃ pātraṃ kṛtvātha dakṣiṇāṃ //
:n
1 svāhāyai nityameva bhavantviti iti kha.. , cha.. ca
2 prārthayettata iti gha.. , ja.. , jha.. ca
3 aghorāḥ pitara ity ādiḥ, āstīrya sapavitrakānityantaḥ pāṭhaḥ
kha.. , cha.. pustakadvaye nāsti
:p 17
117.d:
स्वधोच्यतामस्तु स्वधा उच्यमानस्तथैव च /
अपो निषिञ्चेदुत्तानं पात्रं कृत्वाथ दक्षिणां //
:न्
1 स्वाहायै नित्यमेव भवन्त्विति इति ख.. , छ.. च
2 प्रार्थयेत्तत इति घ.. , ज.. , झ.. च
3 अघोराः पितर इत्य् आदिः, आस्तीर्य सपवित्रकानित्यन्तः पाठः
ख.. , छ.. पुस्तकद्वये नास्ति
:प् 17
117.m:
'Let svadhā be uttered! May there be svadhā!' and likewise while it is being uttered, / he should sprinkle water; and having turned the vessel upwards, [he gives] the sacrificial fee.
[Footnote]
1. "svāhāyai nityameva bhavantu" thus in manuscripts kha and cha.
2. "prārthayettataḥ" thus in manuscripts gha, ja, and jha.
3. The reading beginning with "aghorāḥ pitaraḥ" up to "āstīrya sapavitrakān" is absent in the two manuscripts kha and cha.

117.s:
yathāśakti pradadyācca daive paitre 'tha vācayet /
viśve devāḥ prīyantāñca vāje visarjayet //
117.d:
यथाशक्ति प्रदद्याच्च दैवे पैत्रे ऽथ वाचयेत् /
विश्वे देवाः प्रीयन्ताञ्च वाजे विसर्जयेत् //
117.m: And he should give [gifts] according to his means, and have [the blessings] recited regarding the deities and the ancestors: / 'May the Viśvedevas be pleased,' and he should dismiss [them] with the [verse] beginning with 'Vāje'.

117.s:
āmāvājasyetyanuvrajya kṛtvā viprān pradakṣiṇaṃ /
gṛhe viśedamāvāsyāṃ māsi māsi carettathā //
117.d:
आमावाजस्येत्यनुव्रज्य कृत्वा विप्रान् प्रदक्षिणं /
गृहे विशेदमावास्यां मासि मासि चरेत्तथा //
117.m: Having accompanied [them] with 'Ā mā vājasya,' and circumambulated the brāhmaṇas clockwise, / he should enter the house; he should perform [this] in the same manner month by month on the new moon day.

117.s:
ekoddiṣṭaṃ pravakṣyāmi śrāddhaṃ pūrvavadācaret /
ekaṃ pavitramekārdhaṃ ekaṃ piṇḍampradāpayet //
117.d:
एकोद्दिष्टं प्रवक्ष्यामि श्राद्धं पूर्ववदाचरेत् /
एकं पवित्रमेकार्धं एकं पिण्डम्प्रदापयेत् //
117.m: I shall explain the ancestral rite for a single deceased person (ekoddiṣṭa); he should perform it as before: / he should offer one blade of sacred grass, one [half-measure of water], and one funeral cake.

117.s:
nāvāhanāgnaukaraṇaṃ viśve devā na cātra hi /
tṛptipraśne svaditamiti vadetsukhaditaṃ dvijaḥ //
117.d:
नावाहनाग्नौकरणं विश्वे देवा न चात्र हि /
तृप्तिप्रश्ने स्वदितमिति वदेत्सुखदितं द्विजः //
117.m: Here there is neither invocation nor offering into the fire, nor indeed the Viśvedevas. / At the inquiry of satisfaction, the twice-born should say 'svaditam' ('it is well relished'), [not] 'sukhaditam'.

117.s:
upatiṣṭhatāmityakṣayye visarge cābhiramyatāṃ /
abhiratāḥ sma ity apare śeṣaṃ pūrvavadācaret //
117.d:
उपतिष्ठतामित्यक्षय्ये विसर्गे चाभिरम्यतां /
अभिरताः स्म इत्य् अपरे शेषं पूर्ववदाचरेत् //
117.m: [He says] 'May it remain' for imperishability, and at dismissal, 'Be delighted'; / others [reply], 'We are delighted.' He should perform the remainder as before.

117.s:
sapiṇṭhīkaraṇaṃ vakṣye abdānte madhyato 'pi vā /
pitṝṇāṃ trīṇi pātrāṇi ekampretasya pātrakaṃ //
117.d:
सपिण्ठीकरणं वक्ष्ये अब्दान्ते मध्यतो ऽपि वा /
पितॄणां त्रीणि पात्राणि एकम्प्रेतस्य पात्रकं //
117.m: I shall explain the rite of sapīṇḍīkaraṇa, [performed] at the end of a year or even in the middle [of it]: / [there are] three vessels for the ancestors and one vessel for the deceased.

117.s:
sapavitrāṇi catvāri tilapuṣpayutāni ca /
gandhodakena yuktāni(1) pūrayitvābhiṣiñcati //
117.d:
सपवित्राणि चत्वारि तिलपुष्पयुतानि च /
गन्धोदकेन युक्तानि(1) पूरयित्वाभिषिञ्चति //
117.m: The four [vessels], supplied with blades of sacred grass and containing sesame seeds and flowers, / filled and mixed with fragrant water, he sprinkles.

117.s:
pretapātraṃ pitṛpātre ye samanā iti dvayāt /
pūrvavat piṇḍadānādi pretānāṃ pitṛtā bhavet //
117.d:
प्रेतपात्रं पितृपात्रे ये समना इति द्वयात् /
पूर्ववत् पिण्डदानादि प्रेतानां पितृता भवेत् //
117.m: [Pouring] the vessel of the deceased into the vessels of the ancestors with the two [mantras] 'Ye samānāḥ,' / the offering of funeral cakes and the rest [is done] as before; the state of being an ancestor ensues for the deceased.

117.s:
athābhyudayikaṃ śrāddhaṃ vakṣye sarvaṃ tu pūrvavat /
japet pitṛmantravarjaṃ pūrvāhṇe tat pradakṣiṇaṃ //
117.d:
अथाभ्युदयिकं श्राद्धं वक्ष्ये सर्वं तु पूर्ववत् /
जपेत् पितृमन्त्रवर्जं पूर्वाह्णे तत् प्रदक्षिणं //
117.m: Now I shall explain the ancestral rite for prosperity (ābhyudayika); everything is as before, / [but] he should recite omitting the mantras to the ancestors, in the forenoon, circumambulating clockwise.

117.s:
upacārā ṛjukuśāstilārthaiś ca yavair iha(2) /
tṛptipraśnastu sampannaṃ susampannaṃ vadeddvijaḥ //
:n
1 gandhodakena siktāni iti ja..
2 athābhyudayikamityādiḥ, yavair iha ity antaḥ pāṭho jha.. pustake
nāsti
:p 18
117.d:
उपचारा ऋजुकुशास्तिलार्थैश् च यवैर् इह(2) /
तृप्तिप्रश्नस्तु सम्पन्नं सुसम्पन्नं वदेद्द्विजः //
:न्
1 गन्धोदकेन सिक्तानि इति ज..
2 अथाभ्युदयिकमित्यादिः, यवैर् इह इत्य् अन्तः पाठो झ.. पुस्तके
नास्ति
:प् 18
117.m:
The articles of worship [are offered with] straight kuśa grass, and here barley grains replace sesame seeds. / As for the inquiry of satisfaction, the twice-born should say: 'It is accomplished,' [and] 'It is well accomplished.'
[Footnote]
[Apparatus note:] 1 'gandhodakena siktāni' in ja.
[Apparatus note:] 2 The text from 'athābhyudayikaṃ' up to 'yavair iha' is missing in manuscript jha.

117.s:
dadhyakṣatavadarādyāḥ(1) piṇḍā nāndīmukhān pitṝn /
āvāhayiṣye pṛcchecca prīyantāmiti cākṣaye //
117.d:
दध्यक्षतवदराद्याः(1) पिण्डा नान्दीमुखान् पितॄन् /
आवाहयिष्ये पृच्छेच्च प्रीयन्तामिति चाक्षये //
117.m: The funeral cakes, consisting of curd, unbroken rice, jujube fruits, and the like, are for the cheerful-faced ancestors (nāndīmukhas). / He should ask: 'Shall I invoke [them]?' and at [the wish for] imperishability, 'May they be pleased.'

117.s:
nāndīmukhāś ca pitaro vācayiṣye 'tha pṛcchati /
nāndīmukhān pitṛgaṇān prīyantāmityatho vadet //
117.d:
नान्दीमुखाश् च पितरो वाचयिष्ये ऽथ पृच्छति /
नान्दीमुखान् पितृगणान् प्रीयन्तामित्यथो वदेत् //
117.m: Then he asks, “I shall make the cheerful-faced ancestors pronounce [blessings]”; / he should then say, “May the host of cheerful-faced ancestors be pleased.”

117.s:
nāndīmukhāś ca pitarastatpitā prapitāmahaḥ /
mātāmahaḥ pramātāmaho vṛddhapramātṛkāmahaḥ //
117.d:
नान्दीमुखाश् च पितरस्तत्पिता प्रपितामहः /
मातामहः प्रमातामहो वृद्धप्रमातृकामहः //
117.m: And the cheerful-faced ancestors are the father, his father, and the great-grandfather, / the maternal grandfather, the maternal great-grandfather, and the father of the maternal great-grandfather.

117.s:
svadhākāranna yuñjīta yugmān viprāṃś ca bhojayet /
tṛptiṃ vakṣye pitṝṇāṃ ca grāmyair oṣadhibhis tathā //
117.d:
स्वधाकारन्न युञ्जीत युग्मान् विप्रांश् च भोजयेत् /
तृप्तिं वक्ष्ये पितॄणां च ग्राम्यैर् ओषधिभिस् तथा //
117.m: One should not employ the svadhā-utterance, and one should feed an even number of Brahmins. / And I shall state the satisfaction of the ancestors with cultivated grains,

117.s:
māsantṛptis tathāraṇyaiḥ(2) kandamūlaphalādibhiḥ /
matsyair māsadvayaṃ mārgaistrayaṃ vai śākunena ca //
117.d:
मासन्तृप्तिस् तथारण्यैः(2) कन्दमूलफलादिभिः /
मत्स्यैर् मासद्वयं मार्गैस्त्रयं वै शाकुनेन च //
117.m: as well as a month's satisfaction with wild roots, tubers, and fruits; / two months with fish; three with venison and bird-meat;

117.s:
caturo rauraveṇātha(3) pañca ṣaṭ chāgalena tu(4) /
kūrmeṇa sapta cāṣṭau ca vārāheṇa navaiva tu //
117.d:
चतुरो रौरवेणाथ(3) पञ्च षट् छागलेन तु(4) /
कूर्मेण सप्त चाष्टौ च वाराहेण नवैव तु //
117.m: four with ruru-deer meat; five and six with goat meat; / seven with tortoise; eight and indeed nine with boar meat;

117.s:
meṣamāṃsena daśa ca māhiṣaiḥ pārṣataiḥ śivaiḥ /
saṃvatsarantu gavyena payasā pāyasena vā //
117.d:
मेषमांसेन दश च माहिषैः पार्षतैः शिवैः /
संवत्सरन्तु गव्येन पयसा पायसेन वा //
117.m: ten with sheep meat; and [similarly] with buffalo, spotted deer, and benevolent [offerings]; / and a full year with cow's milk or with milk-rice pudding.

117.s:
vārdhīnasasya māṃsena tṛptirdvādaśavārṣikī /
khaḍgamāṃsaṃ kālaśākaṃ lohitacchāgalo(5) madhu //
117.d:
वार्धीनसस्य मांसेन तृप्तिर्द्वादशवार्षिकी /
खड्गमांसं कालशाकं लोहितच्छागलो(5) मधु //
117.m: The satisfaction lasts twelve years with the meat of an old long-eared goat; / rhinoceros meat, black mustard greens, a red goat, honey,

117.s:
mahāśalkāś ca varṣāsu maghāśrāddhamathākṣayaṃ(6) /
mantrādhyāyyagnihotrī ca śākhādhyāyī ṣaḍaṅgavit //
117.d:
महाशल्काश् च वर्षासु मघाश्राद्धमथाक्षयं(6) /
मन्त्राध्याय्यग्निहोत्री च शाखाध्यायी षडङ्गवित् //
117.m: and large-scaled fish during the rainy season; and an ancestral rite under the Maghā asterism brings inexhaustible [merit]. / A reciter of mantras, an agnihotrin, a reciter of a Vedic recension, and one who knows the six ancillary sciences,

117.s:
tṛṇāciketaḥ trimadhurdharmadroṇasya(7) pāṭhakaḥ /
triṣuparṇajyeṣṭhasāmajñānī syuḥ paṅktipāvanāḥ //
:n
1 dadhyakṣatavadaryādyā iti ga.. , cha.. ca
2 tathā vanyair iti kha.. , ṅa.. ca
3 vatsaraṃ rauraveṇātheti gha..
4 pañcakaṃ chāgastena tu iti ṅa..
5 lohitacchāgaka iti ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. ca
6 maghāśrāddhamihākṣayamiti jha..
7 jaladroṇasyeti jha..
:p 19
117.d:
तृणाचिकेतः त्रिमधुर्धर्मद्रोणस्य(7) पाठकः /
त्रिषुपर्णज्येष्ठसामज्ञानी स्युः पङ्क्तिपावनाः //
:न्
1 दध्यक्षतवदर्याद्या इति ग.. , छ.. च
2 तथा वन्यैर् इति ख.. , ङ.. च
3 वत्सरं रौरवेणाथेति घ..
4 पञ्चकं छागस्तेन तु इति ङ..
5 लोहितच्छागक इति ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. च
6 मघाश्राद्धमिहाक्षयमिति झ..
7 जलद्रोणस्येति झ..
:प् 19
117.m:
one versed in the Triṇāciketa ritual, one knowing the Trimadhu hymns, a reader of the Dharmadroṇa, / and one who knows the Triṣuparṇa and the Jyeṣṭhasāman hymns are sanctifiers of the assembly.
[Footnotes]
1 dadhyakṣatavadaryādyāḥ in manuscripts ga and cha.
2 tathā vanyaiḥ in manuscripts kha and ṅa.
3 vatsaraṃ rauraveṇātha in manuscript gha.
4 pañcakaṃ chāgastena tu in manuscript ṅa.
5 lohitacchāgakaḥ in manuscripts ga, gha, and ṅa.
6 maghāśrāddhamihākṣayam in manuscript jha.
7 jaladroṇasya in manuscript jha.

117.s:
kamyānāṃ kalpamākhyāsye(1) pratipatsu dhanaṃ bahu /
striyaḥ parā dvitīyāyāñcaturthyāṃ dharmakāmadaḥ //
117.d:
कम्यानां कल्पमाख्यास्ये(1) प्रतिपत्सु धनं बहु /
स्त्रियः परा द्वितीयायाञ्चतुर्थ्यां धर्मकामदः //
117.m: I shall describe the procedure for optional rites: on the first lunar day, abundant wealth; / on the second lunar day, excellent women; on the fourth, [it] grants virtue and desires;

117.s:
pañcamyāṃ putrakāmastu ṣaṣṭhyāñca śraiṣṭhyabhāgapi(2) /
kṛṣibhāgī ca saptamyāmaṣṭamyāmarthalābhakaḥ //
117.d:
पञ्चम्यां पुत्रकामस्तु षष्ठ्याञ्च श्रैष्ठ्यभागपि(2) /
कृषिभागी च सप्तम्यामष्टम्यामर्थलाभकः //
117.m: on the fifth, one desiring sons; on the sixth, one attains pre-eminence; / on the seventh, one attains agricultural success; on the eighth, one gains wealth;

117.s:
navamyāñca ekaśaphā(3) daśamyāṅgogaṇo bhavet /
ekadaśyāṃ parīvāro dvādaśyāndhanadhānyakaṃ //
117.d:
नवम्याञ्च एकशफा(3) दशम्याङ्गोगणो भवेत् /
एकदश्यां परीवारो द्वादश्यान्धनधान्यकं //
117.m: on the ninth, one-hoofed animals; on the tenth, there will be herds of cattle; / on the eleventh, an entourage; on the twelfth, wealth and grain;

117.s:
jñātiśreṣṭhyaṃ trayodaśyāṃ caturdaśyāñca śastrataḥ(4) /
mṛtānāṃ śrāddhaṃ sarvāptamamāvāsyāṃ samīritaṃ(5) //
117.d:
ज्ञातिश्रेष्ठ्यं त्रयोदश्यां चतुर्दश्याञ्च शस्त्रतः(4) /
मृतानां श्राद्धं सर्वाप्तममावास्यां समीरितं(5) //
117.m: on the thirteenth, pre-eminence among kin; and on the fourteenth, for those killed by weapons; / an ancestral rite on the new moon day is proclaimed to grant all desires.

117.s:
sapta vyādhā daśāraṇye(6) mṛgāḥ kālañjare girau /
cakravākāḥ śaradvīpe haṃsāḥ sarasi mānse //
117.d:
सप्त व्याधा दशारण्ये(6) मृगाः कालञ्जरे गिरौ /
चक्रवाकाः शरद्वीपे हंसाः सरसि मान्से //
117.m: “The seven hunters in the Daśāraṇya forest, the deer on Mount Kālañjara, / the cakravāka birds on the island of Śara, the swans in Lake Mānasa—

117.s:
te 'pi jātāḥ(7) kurukṣetre brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ /
prasthitā dūramadhvānaṃ yūyantebhyo 'vasīdata //
117.d:
ते ऽपि जाताः(7) कुरुक्षेत्रे ब्राह्मणा वेदपारगाः /
प्रस्थिता दूरमध्वानं यूयन्तेभ्यो ऽवसीदत //
117.m: even they were born in Kurukṣetra as Brahmins who had crossed to the end of the Vedas. / Having set out upon the distant path, do not despond before them.”

117.s:
śrāddhādau paṭhite śrāddhaṃ pūrṇaṃ syādbrahmalokadaṃ /
śrāddhaṃ kuryācca putrādiḥ(8) piturjīvati tatpituḥ //
117.d:
श्राद्धादौ पठिते श्राद्धं पूर्णं स्याद्ब्रह्मलोकदं /
