सप्तमे पञ्चविंशः स्यात् खण्डशः पिण्डिकाद् भवेत्(3) /
कर्कटादौ हरेद्राशिमृतुवेदत्रयैः क्रमात् //
122.m:
in the seventh it is twenty-five; it should proceed fraction by fraction from the sum.
In Cancer and the rest, one should divide the sign by three, four, and six in order;

122.s:
tulādau prātilomyena trayo vedarasāḥ kramāt /
:n
1 saikena saptakair iti kha.. , ga.. ca
2 ṛtuhīna iti ṅa..
3 khaṇḍakaḥ piṇḍakādbhavediti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , cha.. , ja..
ca
:p 40
makarādau dīyate ca rasavedatrayaḥ kramāt /
122.d:
तुलादौ प्रातिलोम्येन त्रयो वेदरसाः क्रमात् /
:न्
1 सैकेन सप्तकैर् इति ख.. , ग.. च
2 ऋतुहीन इति ङ..
3 खण्डकः पिण्डकाद्भवेदिति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , छ.. , ज..
च
:प् 40
मकरादौ दीयते च रसवेदत्रयः क्रमात् /
122.m:
in Libra and the rest, in reverse order, three, four, and six in order;
[Footnote]
1. "saikena saptakaiḥ" in manuscripts kha. and ga.
2. "ṛtuhīnaḥ" in manuscript ṅa.
3. "khaṇḍakaḥ piṇḍakādbhavet" in manuscripts kha., ga., gha., ṅa., cha., and ja. / [page] 40
and in Capricorn and the rest, six, four, and three are given in order.

122.s:
meṣādau prātilomyena trayo vedarasāḥ kramāt(1) /
kheṣavaḥ khayugā maitraṃ meṣādau vikalā dhanam //
122.d:
मेषादौ प्रातिलोम्येन त्रयो वेदरसाः क्रमात्(1) /
खेषवः खयुगा मैत्रं मेषादौ विकला धनम् //
122.m:
In Aries and so forth, in reverse order, three [factors of] sixty-four in sequence;
fifty, forty, [and] twenty-four; in Aries and the rest, the seconds are additive.

122.s:
karkaṭe prātilomyaṃ syādṛṇametat tulādike /
caturguṇā tithirjñeyā vikalāśceha sarvadā //
122.d:
कर्कटे प्रातिलोम्यं स्यादृणमेतत् तुलादिके /
चतुर्गुणा तिथिर्ज्ञेया विकलाश्चेह सर्वदा //
122.m:
In Cancer there should be the reverse order; this is subtractive in Libra and the rest.
The lunar day is always to be known multiplied by four, and likewise the seconds here.

122.s:
hanyālliptāgatāgāmipiṇḍasaṅkhyāphalantaraiḥ /
ṣaṣṭyāptaṃ prathamoccārye hānau deyandhane dhanam //
122.d:
हन्याल्लिप्तागतागामिपिण्डसङ्ख्याफलन्तरैः /
षष्ट्याप्तं प्रथमोच्चार्ये हानौ देयन्धने धनम् //
122.m:
One should multiply by the differences between the minutes of elapsed and coming factors.
Divided by sixty: in the first operation, if there is a deficit it must be added; if a surplus, additive.

122.s:
dvitīyoccarite varge vaiparītyamiti sthitiḥ /
tithirdviguṇitā kāryā ṣaḍbhāgaparivarjitā //
122.d:
द्वितीयोच्चरिते वर्गे वैपरीत्यमिति स्थितिः /
तिथिर्द्विगुणिता कार्या षड्भागपरिवर्जिता //
122.m:
In the second pronounced group, the rule is the reverse:
The lunar day should be doubled, minus a sixth part.

122.s:
ravikarmaviparītā tithināḍīsamāyutā /
ṛṇe śuddhe tu nāḍyaḥ syurṛṇaṃ śudhyeta no yadā //
122.d:
रविकर्मविपरीता तिथिनाडीसमायुता /
ऋणे शुद्धे तु नाड्यः स्युरृणं शुध्येत नो यदा //
122.m:
Reverse to the solar calculation, combined with the nāḍīs of the lunar day;
when the negative is subtracted, there are nāḍīs; but when the negative is not subtractable,

122.s:
saṣaṣṭikaṃ pradeyantat ṣaṣṭyādhikye ca tattyajet(2) /
nakṣatraṃ tithimiśraṃ syāccaturbhirguṇitā tithiḥ //
122.d:
सषष्टिकं प्रदेयन्तत् षष्ट्याधिक्ये च तत्त्यजेत्(2) /
नक्षत्रं तिथिमिश्रं स्याच्चतुर्भिर्गुणिता तिथिः //
122.m:
that is to be given increased by sixty, and when exceeding sixty, one should drop it.
The lunar mansion is combined with the lunar day; the lunar day multiplied by four,

122.s:
tithistribhāgasaṃyuktā ṛṇena ca tathānvitā /
tithiratra citā kāryā tadvedādyogaśodhanaṃ //
122.d:
तिथिस्त्रिभागसंयुक्ता ऋणेन च तथान्विता /
तिथिरत्र चिता कार्या तद्वेदाद्योगशोधनं //
122.m:
combined with a third part of the lunar day, and likewise accompanied by the negative;
here the accumulated lunar day is to be calculated; then the reduction of the yoga [beginning with] Viṣkambha [is done].

122.s:
ravicandrau samau kṛtvā yogo bhavati niś calaḥ /
ekonā tithirdviguṇā saptabhinnā kṛtirdvidhā(3) //
122.d:
रविचन्द्रौ समौ कृत्वा योगो भवति निश् चलः /
एकोना तिथिर्द्विगुणा सप्तभिन्ना कृतिर्द्विधा(3) //
122.m:
Having made the sun and moon equal, the yoga becomes fixed.
The lunar day diminished by one, doubled, divided by seven, the remainder [is taken] in two ways.

122.s:
tithiś ca dviguṇaikonā kṛtāṅgaiḥ karaṇanniśi /
:n
1 makarādau ity ādiḥ, vedarasāḥ kramādityantaḥ pāṭhaḥ cha..
pustake nāsti
2 santyajediti gha..
3 saptabhinnā gatirdvidheti kha.. / saptacchinnā kṛtirdvidheti gha.. , ja.. ca
:p 41
kṛṣṇacaturdaśyante śakuniḥ parvaṇīha catuṣpadaṃ //
122.d:
तिथिश् च द्विगुणैकोना कृताङ्गैः करणन्निशि /
:न्
1 मकरादौ इत्य् आदिः, वेदरसाः क्रमादित्यन्तः पाठः छ..
पुस्तके नास्ति
2 सन्त्यजेदिति घ..
3 सप्तभिन्ना गतिर्द्विधेति ख.. / सप्तच्छिन्ना कृतिर्द्विधेति घ.. , ज.. च
:प् 41
कृष्णचतुर्दश्यन्ते शकुनिः पर्वणीह चतुष्पदं //
122.m:
And the lunar day doubled and minus one, [counted] by groups of four and six, is the karaṇa at night.
[Footnote]
[Note:] The reading beginning with "makarādau" up to "vedarasāḥ kramāt" is missing in manuscript cha.
[Note:] Manuscript gha reads "santyajet".
[Note:] Manuscript kha reads "saptabhinnā gatirdvidhā"; manuscripts gha and ja read "saptacchinnā kṛtirdvidhā".
At the end of the fourteenth [lunar day] of the dark fortnight, Śakuni [is the karaṇa]; on the new moon here, Catuṣpada;

122.s:
prathame tithyardhato hi kintughnaṃ pratipanmukhe //25//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe kālagaṇanaṃ nāma
dvāviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha trayoviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
yuddhajayārṇavīyanānāyogāḥ
122.d:
प्रथमे तिथ्यर्धतो हि किन्तुघ्नं प्रतिपन्मुखे //25//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे कालगणनं नाम
द्वाविंशत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ त्रयोविंशत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
युद्धजयार्णवीयनानायोगाः
122.m:
for in the first half-day, beginning with the first lunar day, Kiṃstughna [occurs]. // 25
Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-second chapter, named "Calculation of Time," in the great Purāṇa of Agni.
Now, the one hundred and twenty-third chapter:
Various Yogas from the Yuddhajayārṇava

123.s:
vakṣye jayaśubhādyarthaṃ sāraṃ yuddhajayārṇave /
a+i+u+e+o svarāḥ syuḥ kramānnandādikā tithiḥ //
123.d:
वक्ष्ये जयशुभाद्यर्थं सारं युद्धजयार्णवे /
अ+इ+उ+ए+ओ स्वराः स्युः क्रमान्नन्दादिका तिथिः //
123.m:
I shall declare the essence in the *Yuddhajayārṇava* for the purpose of victory, auspiciousness, and so forth:
The vowels shall be a, i, u, e, [and] o; the lunar days Nandā and so on, in sequence.

123.s:
kādihāntā bhaumaravī jñasomau gurubhārgavau /
śanirdakṣiṇanāḍyāntu bhaumārkaśanayaḥ pare //
123.d:
कादिहान्ता भौमरवी ज्ञसोमौ गुरुभार्गवौ /
शनिर्दक्षिणनाड्यान्तु भौमार्कशनयः परे //
123.m:
[The consonants] from ka to ha: Mars and the Sun, Mercury and the Moon, Jupiter and Venus,
[and] Saturn. On the right channel, however, are Mars, the Sun, and Saturn; the others [on the left].

123.s:
khārṇavaḥ khasasair guṇyo rudrair bhāgaṃ samāharet /
rasāhatantu tat kṛtvā pūrvabhāgena bhājayet //
123.d:
खार्णवः खससैर् गुण्यो रुद्रैर् भागं समाहरेत् /
रसाहतन्तु तत् कृत्वा पूर्वभागेन भाजयेत् //
123.m:
Forty is to be multiplied by sixty; one should divide by eleven.
Having multiplied that by six, one should divide by the former portion.

123.s:
vahnibhiścāhataṃ kṛtvā(1) rūpantatraiva nikṣipet /
spandanaṃ nāḍyāḥ phalāni saprāṇaspandanaṃ punaḥ //
123.d:
वह्निभिश्चाहतं कृत्वा(1) रूपन्तत्रैव निक्षिपेत् /
स्पन्दनं नाड्याः फलानि सप्राणस्पन्दनं पुनः //
123.m:
Having multiplied by three, one should add one there.
The results are the vibration of the nāḍī, along with the vibration of the breath.

123.s:
anenaiva tu mānena udayanti dine dine /
sphuraṇaisribhirucchvāsa ucchvāsaistu palaṃ smṛtam //
:n
1 vahnibhiś ca hṛtaṃ kṛtvā iti gha..
:p 42
123.d:
अनेनैव तु मानेन उदयन्ति दिने दिने /
स्फुरणैस्रिभिरुच्छ्वास उच्छ्वासैस्तु पलं स्मृतम् //
:न्
1 वह्निभिश् च हृतं कृत्वा इति घ..
:प् 42
123.m:
By this very measure they rise day after day.
By three pulses an exhalation [is formed]; by exhalations a pala is remembered.
[Footnote]
[Note:] Manuscript gha reads "vahnibhiś ca hṛtaṃ kṛtvā".

123.s:
ṣaṣṭibhiś ca palair liptā liptāṣaṣṭistvaharniśaṃ /
pañcamārdhodaye bālakumārayuvavṛddhakāḥ //
123.d:
षष्टिभिश् च पलैर् लिप्ता लिप्ताषष्टिस्त्वहर्निशं /
पञ्चमार्धोदये बालकुमारयुववृद्धकाः //
123.m:
And sixty palas make a minute; sixty minutes make a day and night.
At the rise of the fifth half [of the breath], there are child, youth, adult, and old [states].

123.s:
mṛtyuryenodayastena cāstamekādaśāṃśakaiḥ /
kulāgame bhavedbhaṅgaḥ samṛtyuḥ pañcamo 'pivā //
svarodayañcakraṃ
123.d:
मृत्युर्येनोदयस्तेन चास्तमेकादशांशकैः /
कुलागमे भवेद्भङ्गः समृत्युः पञ्चमो ऽपिवा //
स्वरोदयञ्चक्रं
123.m:
Death [comes] through that by which sunrise [occurs], and setting by eleven parts.
In the occurrence of a krama there will be failure; or the fifth brings death.
The Diagram of the Rise of Vowels

123.s:
śanicakre cārdhamāsaṅgrahāṇāmudayaḥ kramāt /
vibhāgaiḥ pañcadaśabhiḥ śanibhāgastu mṛtyudaḥ //
śanicakraṃ
123.d:
शनिचक्रे चार्धमासङ्ग्रहाणामुदयः क्रमात् /
विभागैः पञ्चदशभिः शनिभागस्तु मृत्युदः //
शनिचक्रं
123.m:
And in the Saturn diagram, the rise of the planets takes place half a month in sequence,
by fifteen divisions; but the division of Saturn brings death.
The Saturn Diagram

123.s:
daśakotisahasrāṇi arvudānyarvudaṃ haret(1) /
trayodaśe ca lakṣāṇi pramāṇaṃ kūrmarūpiṇaḥ //
123.d:
दशकोतिसहस्राणि अर्वुदान्यर्वुदं हरेत्(1) /
त्रयोदशे च लक्षाणि प्रमाणं कूर्मरूपिणः //
123.m:
One should take ten hundred thousand crores, hundred millions, [and] a hundred million;
and in the thirteenth, lakhs: [this is] the measure of the Tortoise-formed one.

123.s:
maghādau kṛttikādyantastaddeśāntaḥ śanisthitau /
kūrmacakraṃ
rāhucakre ca saptordhamadhaḥ sapta ca saṃlikhet(2) //
123.d:
मघादौ कृत्तिकाद्यन्तस्तद्देशान्तः शनिस्थितौ /
कूर्मचक्रं
राहुचक्रे च सप्तोर्धमधः सप्त च संलिखेत्(2) //
123.m:
Beginning with Maghā and ending with Kṛttikā, within that region, when Saturn resides [there].
The Tortoise Diagram
And in the Rāhu diagram, one should draw seven above and seven below.

123.s:
vāyvagnyoś caiva nairṛtye pūrṇimāgneyabhāgataḥ /
abhāvāsyāṃ vāyave ca rāhurvai tithirūpakaḥ //
123.d:
वाय्वग्न्योश् चैव नैरृत्ये पूर्णिमाग्नेयभागतः /
अभावास्यां वायवे च राहुर्वै तिथिरूपकः //
123.m:
In the northwest, northeast, and southwest; the full moon starting from the northeast portion,
and on the new moon in the northwest: Rāhu indeed has the form of the lunar day.

123.s:
rakāraṃ dakṣabhāge tu hakāraṃ vāyave likhet /
pratipadādau kakārādīn sakāraṃ nairṛte punaḥ //
123.d:
रकारं दक्षभागे तु हकारं वायवे लिखेत् /
प्रतिपदादौ ककारादीन् सकारं नैरृते पुनः //
123.m:
One should write the letter *ra* in the right portion, and the letter *ha* in the northwest;
beginning with the first lunar day, [the letters] beginning with *ka*, and again the letter *sa* in the southwest.

123.s:
rāhoemukhe tu bhaṅgaḥ syāditi rāhurudāhṛtaḥ /
viṣṭiragnau(3) paurṇamāsyāṃ karāṇīndre tṛtīyakaṃ //
123.d:
राहोएमुखे तु भङ्गः स्यादिति राहुरुदाहृतः /
विष्टिरग्नौ(3) पौर्णमास्यां कराणीन्द्रे तृतीयकं //
123.m:
In the mouth of Rāhu there would be defeat; thus Rāhu is declared.
Viṣṭi is in the southeast on the full moon; Karāṇī is the third in the east;

123.s:
ghorā yāmyāntu saptamyāṃ daśamyāṃ raudrasaumyagā /
caturdaśyāntu vāyavye caturthyāṃ varuṇāśraye //
:n
1 arvudānyarvudaṃ kramāditi jha..
2 saptarasāṃllikhediti jha..
3 viṣtirvahnau iti ga..
:p 43
123.d:
घोरा याम्यान्तु सप्तम्यां दशम्यां रौद्रसौम्यगा /
चतुर्दश्यान्तु वायव्ये चतुर्थ्यां वरुणाश्रये //
:न्
1 अर्वुदान्यर्वुदं क्रमादिति झ..
2 सप्तरसांल्लिखेदिति झ..
3 विष्तिर्वह्नौ इति ग..
:प् 43

123.s:
śuklāṣṭabhyāṃ dakṣiṇe ca ekādaśyāṃ bhṛśantyajet /
raudraś caiva tathā śveto maitraḥ sārabhaṭas tathā //
123.d:
शुक्लाष्टभ्यां दक्षिणे च एकादश्यां भृशन्त्यजेत् /
रौद्रश् चैव तथा श्वेतो मैत्रः सारभटस् तथा //
123.m:
on the eighth of the bright fortnight in the south, and on the eleventh, one should completely avoid [it].
Raudra, and likewise Śveta, Maitra, as well as Sārabhaṭa,

123.s:
sāvitrī virocanaś ca jayadevo 'bhijittathā(1) /
rāvaṇo vijayaś caiva nandī varuṇa eva ca //
123.d:
सावित्री विरोचनश् च जयदेवो ऽभिजित्तथा(1) /
रावणो विजयश् चैव नन्दी वरुण एव च //
123.m:
Sāvitrī, and Virocana, Jayadeva, likewise Abhijit,
Rāvaṇa, and Vijaya, Nandī, and Varuṇa,

123.s:
yamasaumyau bhavaścānte daśapañcamuhūrtakāḥ /
raudre raudrāṇi kurvīta śvete snānādikaṃ caret //
123.d:
यमसौम्यौ भवश्चान्ते दशपञ्चमुहूर्तकाः /
रौद्रे रौद्राणि कुर्वीत श्वेते स्नानादिकं चरेत् //
123.m:
Yama, Saumya, and Bhava at the end: these are the fifteen muhūrtas.
During Raudra one should perform fierce deeds; during Śveta one should undertake bathing and the like.

123.s:
maitre kanyāvivāhādi śubhaṃ sārabhaṭe caret /
sāvitre sthāpanādyaṃ vā virocane nṛpakriyā //
123.d:
मैत्रे कन्याविवाहादि शुभं सारभटे चरेत् /
सावित्रे स्थापनाद्यं वा विरोचने नृपक्रिया //
123.m:
During Maitra, the marriage of a maiden and the like [should be done]; one should perform auspicious acts during Sārabhaṭa;
during Sāvitra, installation and the like; during Virocana, royal rites.

123.s:
jayadeve jayaṃ kuryād rāvaṇe raṇakarma ca(2) /
vijaye kṛṣivāṇijyaṃ paṭabandhaṃ ca nandini //
123.d:
जयदेवे जयं कुर्याद् रावणे रणकर्म च(2) /
विजये कृषिवाणिज्यं पटबन्धं च नन्दिनि //
123.m:
During Jayadeva one should achieve victory; during Rāvaṇa, warfare;
during Vijaya, agriculture and commerce; and during Nandin, crowning [with a turban].

123.s:
varuṇe ca taḍāgādi nāśakarma yame caret /
saumye saumyādi kurvīta bhavellagnamahardivā //
123.d:
वरुणे च तडागादि नाशकर्म यमे चरेत् /
सौम्ये सौम्यादि कुर्वीत भवेल्लग्नमहर्दिवा //
123.m:
During Varuṇa, [excavating] ponds and the like; during Yama, one should perform destructive rites;
during Saumya, one should do gentle acts; the ascendant occurs day and night.

123.s:
yogā nāmnā viruddhāḥ syuryogā nāmnaiva śobhanāḥ /
rāhurindrātsamīrañca vāyordakṣaṃ yamācchivam(3) //
123.d:
योगा नाम्ना विरुद्धाः स्युर्योगा नाम्नैव शोभनाः /
राहुरिन्द्रात्समीरञ्च वायोर्दक्षं यमाच्छिवम्(3) //
123.m:
Yogas are discordant by name, or yogas are auspicious by their very name.
Rāhu [travels] from the east to the northwest, from the northwest to the south, from the south to the northeast,

123.s:
śivādāpyañjalādagniragneḥ saumyantatastrayam /
tataś ca saṅkramaṃ hanti catasro ghaṭikābhraman //
rāhucakraṃ
123.d:
शिवादाप्यञ्जलादग्निरग्नेः सौम्यन्ततस्त्रयम् /
ततश् च सङ्क्रमं हन्ति चतस्रो घटिकाभ्रमन् //
राहुचक्रं

123.s:
caṇḍīndrāṇī vārāhī ca muśalī girikarṇikā /
balā cātibalā kṣīrī mallikājātiyūthikāḥ //
123.d:
चण्डीन्द्राणी वाराही च मुशली गिरिकर्णिका /
बला चातिबला क्षीरी मल्लिकाजातियूथिकाः //
123.m:
Caṇḍī, Indrāṇī, Vārāhī, Muśalī, Girikarṇikā,
Balā, and Atibalā, Kṣīrī, Mallikā, Jāti, Yūthikā—

123.s:
yathālābhaṃ dhārayettāḥ śvetārkaś ca śatāvarī /
guḍūcī vāgurī divyā oṣadhyo dhāritā jaye //
:n
1 spandanamityādiḥ, jayadevobhijittathetyantaḥ pāṭhaḥ gha.. pustake
nāsti
2 jīvakarma ceti kha..
3 vāyoryāmyaṃ tataḥ śivamiti gha..
:p 44
oṃ namo bhairavāya(1) khaḍgaparaśuhastāya oṃ hrūṃ(2)
vighnavināśāya oṃ hrūṃ(3) phaṭ
123.d:
यथालाभं धारयेत्ताः श्वेतार्कश् च शतावरी /
गुडूची वागुरी दिव्या ओषध्यो धारिता जये //
:न्
1 स्पन्दनमित्यादिः, जयदेवोभिजित्तथेत्यन्तः पाठः घ.. पुस्तके
नास्ति
2 जीवकर्म चेति ख..
3 वायोर्याम्यं ततः शिवमिति घ..
:प् 44
ओं नमो भैरवाय(1) खड्गपरशुहस्ताय ओं ह्रूं(2)
विघ्नविनाशाय ओं ह्रूं(3) फट्
123.m:
one should wear them as available; and white arka, Śatāvarī,
Guḍūcī, Vāgurī—these divine herbs, worn, lead to victory.
[Footnote]
[Note:] The reading beginning with "spandanam" up to "jayadevobhijittathā" is missing in manuscript gha.
[Note:] Manuscript kha reads "jīvakarma ca".
[Note:] Manuscript gha reads "vāyoryāmyaṃ tataḥ śivam".
"Oṃ, obeisance to Bhairava who holds a sword and an axe in his hands! Oṃ hrūṃ, to the destroyer of obstacles! Oṃ hrūṃ phaṭ!"

123.s:
anenaiva tu mantreṇa śikhābandhādikṛjjaye /
tilakañcāñjanañcaiva dhūpalepanameva ca //
123.d:
अनेनैव तु मन्त्रेण शिखाबन्धादिकृज्जये /
तिलकञ्चाञ्जनञ्चैव धूपलेपनमेव च //
123.m:
One who ties the crest-lock and so forth with this very mantra wins victory;
and likewise [using it for] the frontal mark, collyrium, incense, and ointment.

123.s:
snānapānāni tailāni yogadhūlimataḥ śṛṇu /
śubhagā manaḥśilā tālaṃ lākṣārasasamanvitaṃ //
123.d:
स्नानपानानि तैलानि योगधूलिमतः शृणु /
शुभगा मनःशिला तालं लाक्षारससमन्वितं //
123.m: Listen next to the baths, potions, oils, and magical dusts. / Realgar, orpiment, combined with lac-resin,

123.s:
taruṇīkṣīrasaṃyukto lalāṭe tilako vaśe /
viṣṇukrāntā ca sarpākṣī sahadevañca(4) rocanā //
123.d:
तरुणीक्षीरसंयुक्तो ललाटे तिलको वशे /
विष्णुक्रान्ता च सर्पाक्षी सहदेवञ्च(4) रोचना //
123.m: mixed with the milk of a young woman [used as] a mark on the forehead, brings subjugation. / Viṣṇukrāntā, sarpākṣī, sahadevā, and rocanā,

123.s:
ajādugdhena saṃpiṣṭaṃ tilakovaśyakārakaḥ /
priyaṅgukuṅkumaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ mohanī tagaraṃ ghṛtaṃ //
123.d:
अजादुग्धेन संपिष्टं तिलकोवश्यकारकः /
प्रियङ्गुकुङ्कुमं कुष्ठं मोहनी तगरं घृतं //
123.m: ground with goat's milk, [makes] a mark that causes subjugation. / Priyaṅgu, saffron, kuṣṭha, mohanī, tagara, and ghee—

123.s:
tilako vaśyakṛttacca rocanā raktacandanaṃ /
niśā manaḥśilā tālaṃ priyaṅgusarṣapās tathā //
123.d:
तिलको वश्यकृत्तच्च रोचना रक्तचन्दनं /
निशा मनःशिला तालं प्रियङ्गुसर्षपास् तथा //
123.m: a mark [of these] causes subjugation; as does rocanā, red sandalwood, / turmeric, realgar, orpiment, priyaṅgu, and mustard seeds;

123.s:
mohanī haritā krāntā sahadevī śikhā tathā /
mātulaṅgarasaiḥ piṣṭaṃ lalāṭe tilako vaśe //
123.d:
मोहनी हरिता क्रान्ता सहदेवी शिखा तथा /
मातुलङ्गरसैः पिष्टं ललाटे तिलको वशे //
123.m: mohanī, haritā, krāntā, sahadevī, and śikhā, / ground with citron juice [and applied as] a mark on the forehead, causes subjugation.

123.s:
sendrāḥ surā vaśaṃ yānti kiṃ punaḥ kṣudramānuṣāḥ /
mañjiṣṭhā candanaṃ raktaṃ kaṭkandā vilāsinī //
123.d:
सेन्द्राः सुरा वशं यान्ति किं पुनः क्षुद्रमानुषाः /
मञ्जिष्ठा चन्दनं रक्तं कट्कन्दा विलासिनी //
123.m: The gods with Indra come under subjugation; how much more so petty humans? / Madder, red sandalwood, kaṭkandā, vilāsinī,

123.s:
punarnavāsamāyukto lepo 'yaṃ bhāskaro vaśe /
candanaṃ nāgapuṣpañca mañjiṣṭhā tagaraṃ vacā(5) //
123.d:
पुनर्नवासमायुक्तो लेपो ऽयं भास्करो वशे /
चन्दनं नागपुष्पञ्च मञ्जिष्ठा तगरं वचा(5) //
123.m: combined with punarnavā: this brilliant ointment is for subjugation. / Sandalwood, nāgapuṣpa, madder, tagara, vacā,

123.s:
lodhnapriyaṅgurajanīmāṃsītailaṃ vaśaṅkaraṃ /
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe nānāyogā nāma
trayoviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 oṃ namo bhagavate bhairavāyeti kha.. , gha.. ca
2,3 oṃ hūmiti kha.. , ja.. ca
4 sahadevā ceti ṅa..
5 mañjiṣṭhā tagarantatheti ka.. / mañjiṣṭhā bhallakaṃ vaceti
cha..
:p 45
:ś atha caturviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
123.d:
लोध्नप्रियङ्गुरजनीमांसीतैलं वशङ्करं /
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नानायोगा नाम
त्रयोविंशत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 ओं नमो भगवते भैरवायेति ख.. , घ.. च
2,3 ओं हूमिति ख.. , ज.. च
4 सहदेवा चेति ङ..
5 मञ्जिष्ठा तगरन्तथेति क.. / मञ्जिष्ठा भल्लकं वचेति
छ..
:प् 45
:श् अथ चतुर्विंशत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
123.m:
lodhra, priyaṅgu, turmeric, and māṃsī oil bring subjugation.
Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-third chapter, entitled "Various Magical Formulations," in the great Agni Purāṇa.
[Notes]
1 kha and gha read: oṃ namo bhagavate bhairavāya.
2, 3 kha and ja read: oṃ hūm.
4 ṅa reads: sahadevā ca.
5 ka reads: mañjiṣṭhā tagarantathā; cha reads: mañjiṣṭhā bhallakaṃ vacā.
Now, the one hundred and twenty-fourth chapter.

124.s:
yuddhajayārṇavīyajyotiḥśāstrasāraḥ
agnir uvāca
jyotiḥśāstrādisārañca vakṣye yuddhajayārṇave /
vinā mantroṣadhādyañca yathyomāmīśvaro 'bravīt(1) //
124.d:
युद्धजयार्णवीयज्योतिःशास्त्रसारः
अग्निर् उवाच
ज्योतिःशास्त्रादिसारञ्च वक्ष्ये युद्धजयार्णवे /
विना मन्त्रोषधाद्यञ्च यथ्योमामीश्वरो ऽब्रवीत्(1) //
124.m: The Essence of the Science of Astral Lore in the Ocean of Victory in War / Agni said: / I shall state the essence of the science of astral lore and other [teachings] in the Ocean of Victory in War, / without mantras, medicinal herbs, and so forth, just as Īśvara told Umā.

124.s:
devyuvāca
devair jitā dānavāś ca(2) yenopāyena tadvada /
śubhāśubhavivekādyaṃ jñānaṃ yuddhajayārṇavaṃ //
124.d:
देव्युवाच
देवैर् जिता दानवाश् च(2) येनोपायेन तद्वद /
शुभाशुभविवेकाद्यं ज्ञानं युद्धजयार्णवं //
124.m: The goddess said: / Tell that means by which the demons were conquered by the gods, / the knowledge [discriminating] auspicious and inauspicious, [called] the Ocean of Victory in War.

124.s:
īśvara uvāca
mūladeveccayā jātā śaktiḥ pañcādaśākṣarā /
carācaraṃ tato jātaṃ yāmārādhyākhilārthavit(3) //
124.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
मूलदेवेच्चया जाता शक्तिः पञ्चादशाक्षरा /
चराचरं ततो जातं यामाराध्याखिलार्थवित्(3) //
124.m: Īśvara said: / By the will of the Primal Deity, the fifteen-syllabled Śakti was born; / from her was born the moving and unmoving world. Having worshipped her, one knows all things.

124.s:
mantrapīṭhaṃ pravakṣyāmi pañcamantrasamudbhavaṃ /
te mantrāḥ sarvamantrāṇāṃ jīvite maraṇe sthitāḥ //
124.d:
मन्त्रपीठं प्रवक्ष्यामि पञ्चमन्त्रसमुद्भवं /
ते मन्त्राः सर्वमन्त्राणां जीविते मरणे स्थिताः //
124.m: I shall proclaim the throne of mantras, arisen from five mantras; / those mantras abide in the life and death of all mantras.

124.s:
ṛgyajuḥsāmātharvākhyadevamantrāḥ krameṇa te /
sadyojātādayo mantrā brahmā viṣṇuś ca rudrakaḥ //
124.d:
ऋग्यजुःसामाथर्वाख्यदेवमन्त्राः क्रमेण ते /
सद्योजातादयो मन्त्रा ब्रह्मा विष्णुश् च रुद्रकः //
124.m: They are the divine mantras named Ṛg, Yajus, Sāman, and Atharvan in order, / the mantras beginning with Sadyojāta, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra,

124.s:
īśaḥ saptaśikhā devāḥ śakrādyāḥ pañca ca svarāḥ /
a+i+u+e+o kalāś ca mūlaṃ brahmeti kīrtitaṃ //
124.d:
ईशः सप्तशिखा देवाः शक्राद्याः पञ्च च स्वराः /
अ+इ+उ+ए+ओ कलाश् च मूलं ब्रह्मेति कीर्तितं //
124.m: Īśa, the seven-crested deities, Indra and the others, and the five vowels: / a, i, u, e, o, and the kalās; this is declared to be the root, Brahman.

124.s:
kāṣṭhamadhye tathā vahnirapravṛddho na dṛśyate /
vidyamānā tathā dehe śivaśaktirna dṛśyate //
124.d:
काष्ठमध्ये तथा वह्निरप्रवृद्धो न दृश्यते /
विद्यमाना तथा देहे शिवशक्तिर्न दृश्यते //
124.m: Just as fire inside wood is not seen when unmanifest, / so the Śiva-Śakti present in the body is not seen.

124.s:
ādau śaktiḥ samutpannā oṅkārasvarabhūṣitā /
tato vindurmahādevi ekāreṇa vyavasthitaḥ //
:n
1 īśvaro 'vadat iti gha..
2 dānavādyā iti ja..
3 yāmārādhyākhilātmaviditi kha.. , ga.. ca
:p 46
124.d:
आदौ शक्तिः समुत्पन्ना ओङ्कारस्वरभूषिता /
ततो विन्दुर्महादेवि एकारेण व्यवस्थितः //
:न्
1 ईश्वरो ऽवदत् इति घ..
2 दानवाद्या इति ज..
3 यामाराध्याखिलात्मविदिति ख.. , ग.. च
:प् 46
124.m:
First arose Śakti, adorned with the sound of the syllable Om; / from that, O great goddess, the bindu was established with the letter E.
[Notes]
1 gha reads: īśvaro 'vadat.
2 ja reads: dānavādyāḥ.
3 kha and ga read: yāmārādhyākhilātmavit.

124.s:
jāto nāda ukārastu nadate hṛdi saṃsthitaḥ /
ardhacandra ikārastu mokṣamārgasya bodhakaḥ //
124.d:
जातो नाद उकारस्तु नदते हृदि संस्थितः /
अर्धचन्द्र इकारस्तु मोक्षमार्गस्य बोधकः //
124.m: Nāda arose, the letter U, which sounds abiding in the heart; / the half-moon is the letter I, which makes known the path to liberation.

124.s:
akāro vyakta utpanno bhogamokṣapradaḥ paraḥ(1) /
akāra aiśvare bhūmirnivṛttiś ca kalā smṛtā //
124.d:
अकारो व्यक्त उत्पन्नो भोगमोक्षप्रदः परः(1) /
अकार ऐश्वरे भूमिर्निवृत्तिश् च कला स्मृता //
124.m: The manifested letter A arose, supreme, granting worldly enjoyment and liberation. / In the sovereignty of the letter A, the earth and the kalā Nivṛtti are remembered;

124.s:
gandhonavījaḥ prāṇākhya iḍāśaktiḥ sthirā smṛtā /
ikāraś ca pratiṣṭhākhyo raso pālaś ca piṅgalā //
124.d:
गन्धोनवीजः प्राणाख्य इडाशक्तिः स्थिरा स्मृता /
इकारश् च प्रतिष्ठाख्यो रसो पालश् च पिङ्गला //
124.m: it is the seed of smell, named prāṇa; the iḍā channel is remembered as firm Śakti. / The letter I is named Pratiṣṭhā, taste, pāla, and piṅgalā;

124.s:
krūrā śaktirīvījaḥ syāddharavījo 'gnirūpavān /
vidyā samānā gāndhārī śaktiś ca dahanī smṛtā //
124.d:
क्रूरा शक्तिरीवीजः स्याद्धरवीजो ऽग्निरूपवान् /
विद्या समाना गान्धारी शक्तिश् च दहनी स्मृता //
124.m: the fierce Śakti is the seed Ī; the seed Hara has the form of fire; / Vidyā is samāna, gāndhārī; and the Śakti is remembered as the consuming fire.

124.s:
praśāntirvāryupaspṛśo yaścodānaś calā kriyā /
oṅkāraḥ śāntyatītākhyaḥ khaśabdayūthapāṇinaḥ //
124.d:
प्रशान्तिर्वार्युपस्पृशो यश्चोदानश् चला क्रिया /
ओङ्कारः शान्त्यतीताख्यः खशब्दयूथपाणिनः //
124.m: Praśānti is water, touching, and what is udāna, active motion. / The syllable Om is named Śāntyatītā; space, sound, herd, hands.

124.s:
pañca vargāḥ svarā jātāḥ kujajñagurubhārgavāḥ /
śaniḥ kramādakārādyāḥ kakārādyāstvadhaḥ sthitāḥ //
124.d:
पञ्च वर्गाः स्वरा जाताः कुजज्ञगुरुभार्गवाः /
शनिः क्रमादकाराद्याः ककाराद्यास्त्वधः स्थिताः //
124.m: The five classes [of consonants] and vowels arose, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, / and Saturn in order, beginning with the letter A; those beginning with the letter Ka are placed below.

124.s:
etanmūlamataḥ sarvaṃ jñāyate sacarācaraṃ /
vidyāpīṭhaṃ pravakṣyāmi praṇavaḥ śiva īritaḥ //
124.d:
एतन्मूलमतः सर्वं ज्ञायते सचराचरं /
विद्यापीठं प्रवक्ष्यामि प्रणवः शिव ईरितः //
124.m: From this root, everything moving and unmoving is known. / I shall explain the throne of knowledge; the praṇava is declared to be Śiva.

124.s:
umā somaḥ svayaṃ śaktirvāmā jyeṣṭhā ca raudrāpi /
brahmā viṣṇuḥ kramādrudro guṇāḥ sargādayastrayaḥ //
124.d:
उमा सोमः स्वयं शक्तिर्वामा ज्येष्ठा च रौद्रापि /
ब्रह्मा विष्णुः क्रमाद्रुद्रो गुणाः सर्गादयस्त्रयः //
124.m: Umā is the Moon, herself Śakti, and Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, and Raudrī; / Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra in order, the qualities, and the three beginning with creation.

124.s:
ratnanāḍītrayañcaiva(2) sthūlaḥ sūkṣmaḥ paro 'paraḥ /
cintayecchvetavarṇantaṃ muñcamānaṃ parāmṛtaṃ //
124.d:
रत्ननाडीत्रयञ्चैव(2) स्थूलः सूक्ष्मः परो ऽपरः /
चिन्तयेच्छ्वेतवर्णन्तं मुञ्चमानं परामृतं //
124.m: And the triad of jewel channels, gross, subtle, higher, and lower; / one should meditate on that white-colored form releasing supreme nectar.

124.s:
plavyamānaṃ yathātmānaṃ cintayettaṃ divāniśaṃ /
ajaratvaṃ bhaveddevi śivatvamupagacchati(3) //
:n
1 bhogamokṣapradaḥ śubha iti ja..
2 bahunāḍītrayañcaiveti ka.. , ṅa.. ca
3 śivatvamadhigacchatīti ja..
:p 47
124.d:
प्लव्यमानं यथात्मानं चिन्तयेत्तं दिवानिशं /
अजरत्वं भवेद्देवि शिवत्वमुपगच्छति(3) //
:न्
1 भोगमोक्षप्रदः शुभ इति ज..
2 बहुनाडीत्रयञ्चैवेति क.. , ङ.. च
3 शिवत्वमधिगच्छतीति ज..
:प् 47
124.m:
One should meditate on that day and night as flooding oneself; / agelessness will result, O goddess, and one attains the state of Śiva.
[Notes]
1 ja reads: bhogamokṣapradaḥ śubhaḥ.
2 ka and ṅa read: bahunāḍītrayañcaiva.
3 ja reads: śivatvamadhigacchati.

124.s:
aṅguṣṭhādau nyasedaṅgānnetraṃ madhye 'tha dehake /
mṛtyuñayaṃ tataḥ prārcya raṇādau vijayī bhavet //
124.d:
अङ्गुष्ठादौ न्यसेदङ्गान्नेत्रं मध्ये ऽथ देहके /
मृत्युञयं ततः प्रार्च्य रणादौ विजयी भवेत् //
124.m: One should place the bodily limbs beginning with the thumbs, and the eye in the center of the body; / having then worshipped Mṛtyuñjaya, one becomes victorious in battle and elsewhere.

124.s:
śūnyo nirālayaḥ śabdaḥ sparśaṃ tiryaṅnataṃ spṛśet /
rūpasyordhvagatiḥ proktā jalasyādhaḥ samāśritā //
124.d:
शून्यो निरालयः शब्दः स्पर्शं तिर्यङ्नतं स्पृशेत् /
रूपस्योर्ध्वगतिः प्रोक्ता जलस्याधः समाश्रिता //
124.m: Void and baseless is sound; touch contacts obliquely. / The movement of form is said to be upward; that of water rests downward.

124.s:
sarvasthānavinirmukto gandho madhye ca mūlakaṃ /
nābhimūle(1) sthitaṃ kandaṃ śivarūpantu maṇḍitaṃ //
124.d:
सर्वस्थानविनिर्मुक्तो गन्धो मध्ये च मूलकं /
नाभिमूले(1) स्थितं कन्दं शिवरूपन्तु मण्डितं //
124.m: Smell is free from all locations, and in the center is the root. / At the root of the navel rests the bulb, adorned with the form of Śiva,

124.s:
śaktivyūhena somo 'rko haristatra vyavasthitaḥ /
daśavāyusamopetaṃ pañcatanmātramaṇḍitaṃ //
124.d:
शक्तिव्यूहेन सोमो ऽर्को हरिस्तत्र व्यवस्थितः /
दशवायुसमोपेतं पञ्चतन्मात्रमण्डितं //
124.m: with an array of powers; the Moon, the Sun, and Hari reside there, / endowed with the ten winds, adorned with the five subtle elements,

124.s:
kālānalasamākāraṃ prasphurantaṃ śivātmakaṃ /
tajjīvaṃ jīvalokasya(2) sthāvarasya carasya ca //
124.d:
कालानलसमाकारं प्रस्फुरन्तं शिवात्मकं /
तज्जीवं जीवलोकस्य(2) स्थावरस्य चरस्य च //
124.m: resembling the fire of time, flashing forth, having the nature of Śiva. / That is the life of the world of living beings, of both the stationary and the moving.

124.s:
tasminnaṣṭe(3) mṛtaṃ manye mantrapīṭhe 'nilātmakaṃ //24//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe yuddhajayārṇave jyotiḥśāstrasāro nāma
caturviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha pañcaviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
yuddhajayārṇavīyanānācakrāṇi
īśvara uvāca
oṃ hrīṃ karṇamoṭāni bahurūpe bahudaṃṣṭre hrūṃ
:n
1 nāḍīmūle iti kha..
2 tatra vījaṃ jīvanāyeti kha.. , cha.. ca / tatra jīvaṃ jīvaloka iti
ṅa
3 tasminnaste iti gha..
:p 48
phaṭ(1) oṃ haḥ oṃ grasa grasa kṛnta kṛnta chaka chaka chaka
hrūṃ phaṭ(2) namaḥ
124.d:
तस्मिन्नष्टे(3) मृतं मन्ये मन्त्रपीठे ऽनिलात्मकं //24//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे युद्धजयार्णवे ज्योतिःशास्त्रसारो नाम
चतुर्विंशत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ पञ्चविंशत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
युद्धजयार्णवीयनानाचक्राणि
ईश्वर उवाच
ओं ह्रीं कर्णमोटानि बहुरूपे बहुदंष्ट्रे ह्रूं
:न्
1 नाडीमूले इति ख..
2 तत्र वीजं जीवनायेति ख.. , छ.. च / तत्र जीवं जीवलोक इति
ङ
3 तस्मिन्नस्ते इति घ..
:प् 48
फट्(1) ओं हः ओं ग्रस ग्रस कृन्त कृन्त छक छक छक
ह्रूं फट्(2) नमः
124.m:
When that is destroyed, I consider [life] dead in the throne of mantras, consisting of wind. // 24
Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-fourth chapter, entitled "The Essence of the Science of Astral Lore in the Ocean of Victory in War," in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now, the one hundred and twenty-fifth chapter.
Various Diagrams from the Ocean of Victory in War
Īśvara said:
Oṃ hrīṃ O Karṇamoṭī, O multiform one, O you with many fangs, hrūṃ
[Notes]
1 kha reads: nāḍīmūle.
2 kha and cha read: tatra vījaṃ jīvanāya; ṅa reads: tatra jīvaṃ jīvaloke.
3 gha reads: tasminnaste.
phaṭ, oṃ haḥ oṃ, devour, devour, cut, cut, chaka chaka chaka, hrūṃ phaṭ namaḥ.

125.s:
paṭhyamāno hy ayaṃ mantraḥ kruddhaḥ saṃraktalocanaḥ /
māraṇe pātane vāpi mohanoccāṭane bhavet //
125.d:
पठ्यमानो ह्य् अयं मन्त्रः क्रुद्धः संरक्तलोचनः /
मारणे पातने वापि मोहनोच्चाटने भवेत् //
125.m: When this mantra is recited, wrathful and with bloodshot eyes, / it serves for killing or striking down, or for deluding and driving away.

125.s:
karṇamoṭī mahāvidyā sarvavarṇeṣu rakṣikā /
nānāvidyā
pañcodayaṃ pravakṣyāmi svarodayasamaśritaṃ //
125.d:
कर्णमोटी महाविद्या सर्ववर्णेषु रक्षिका /
नानाविद्या
पञ्चोदयं प्रवक्ष्यामि स्वरोदयसमश्रितं //
125.m:
Karṇamoṭī is the great knowledge (mahāvidyā) that protects across all social classes.
Various knowledges.
I shall explain the five risings based upon the rising of the breath (svarodaya).

125.s:
nābhihṛdyantaraṃ yāvattāvaccarati mārutaḥ /
uccāṭayedraṇādau tu karṇākṣīṇi prabhedayet //
125.d:
नाभिहृद्यन्तरं यावत्तावच्चरति मारुतः /
उच्चाटयेद्रणादौ तु कर्णाक्षीणि प्रभेदयेत् //
125.m: As far as the space between the navel and the heart, so far does the wind move. / In battle and the like, one may cause expulsion (uccāṭana); one may split ears and eyes.

125.s:
karoti sādhakaḥ kruddho japahomaparāyaṇaḥ /
hṛdayātpāyukaṃ kaṇṭhaṃ jvaradāhārimāraṇe(3) //
125.d:
करोति साधकः क्रुद्धो जपहोमपरायणः /
हृदयात्पायुकं कण्ठं ज्वरदाहारिमारणे(3) //
125.m: The practitioner does [this] enraged, devoted to recitation and fire oblation, / [directing the wind] from the heart to the anus and the throat, in slaying enemies and [causing] fever and burning pain.

125.s:
kaṇṭhodbhavo raso vāyuḥ śāntikaṃ pauṣṭikaṃ rasaṃ /
divyaṃ stambhaṃ samākarṣaṃ gandho nāsāntiko bhruvaḥ //
125.d:
कण्ठोद्भवो रसो वायुः शान्तिकं पौष्टिकं रसं /
दिव्यं स्तम्भं समाकर्षं गन्धो नासान्तिको भ्रुवः //
125.m: The taste [water] and wind arising in the throat bring pacification (śāntika) and nourishment (pauṣṭika). / Celestial immobilization (stambha) and attraction (ākarṣa)—smell [earth] reaches from the nose to the eyebrows.

125.s:
gandhalīnaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā stambhayennātra saṃśayaḥ /
stambhanaṃ kīlanādyañca karotyeva hi sādhakaḥ //
125.d:
गन्धलीनं मनः कृत्वा स्तम्भयेन्नात्र संशयः /
स्तम्भनं कीलनाद्यञ्च करोत्येव हि साधकः //
125.m: Having dissolved the mind in smell, one immobilizes—there is no doubt about this; / indeed, the practitioner performs immobilization, pegging down, and so on.

125.s:
caṇḍaghaṇṭā karālī ca sumukhī durmukhī tathā /
revatī prathamā ghorā vāyucakreṣu tā yajet //
125.d:
चण्डघण्टा कराली च सुमुखी दुर्मुखी तथा /
रेवती प्रथमा घोरा वायुचक्रेषु ता यजेत् //
125.m: Caṇḍaghaṇṭā, Karālī, Sumukhī, Durmukhī, / and Revatī, first and terrible—one should worship them in the wind cakras.

125.s:
uccāṭakārikā devyaḥ sthitāstejasi saṃsthitāḥ /
saumyā ca bhīṣaṇī devī jayā ca vijayā tathā //
125.d:
उच्चाटकारिका देव्यः स्थितास्तेजसि संस्थिताः /
सौम्या च भीषणी देवी जया च विजया तथा //
125.m: The goddesses that effect expulsion abide in fire; / Saumyā, the goddess Bhīṣaṇī, Jayā, and Vijayā,

125.s:
ajitā cāparājitā mahākoṭī ca raudrayā /
śuṣkakāyā prāṇaharā rasacakre sthitā amūḥ //
:n
1,2 oṃ huṃ phaḍiti kha..
3 jvaradāhanivāraṇe iti gha..
:p 49
125.d:
अजिता चापराजिता महाकोटी च रौद्रया /
शुष्ककाया प्राणहरा रसचक्रे स्थिता अमूः //
:न्
1,2 ओं हुं फडिति ख..
3 ज्वरदाहनिवारणे इति घ..
:प् 49
125.m:
Ajitā, Aparājitā, Mahākoṭī with Raudrī, / Śuṣkakāyā, and Prāṇaharā—these abide in the water (rasa) cakra.
[Notes]
1, 2. "oṃ huṃ phaṭ" in manuscript kha.
3. "jvaradāhanivāraṇe" in manuscript gha. / [Page 49]

125.s:
virūpākṣī parā divyās tathā cākāśamātaraḥ /
saṃhārī jātahārī ca daṃṣṭrālā śuṣkarevatī //
125.d:
विरूपाक्षी परा दिव्यास् तथा चाकाशमातरः /
संहारी जातहारी च दंष्ट्राला शुष्करेवती //
125.m: Virūpākṣī, Parā, Divyā, and also the Mothers of the Sky (ākāśamātaraḥ): / Saṃhārī, Jātahārī, Daṃṣṭrālā, Śuṣkarevatī,

125.s:
pipīlikā puṣṭiharā mahāpuṣṭipravardhanā /
bhadrakālī subhadrā ca hadrabhīmā subhadrikā //
125.d:
पिपीलिका पुष्टिहरा महापुष्टिप्रवर्धना /
भद्रकाली सुभद्रा च हद्रभीमा सुभद्रिका //
125.m: Pipīlikā, Puṣṭiharā, Mahāpuṣṭipravardhanā, / Bhadrakālī, Subhadrā, Bhadrabhīmā, Subhadrikā,

125.s:
sthirā ca niṣṭhurā divyā niṣkampā gadinī tathā /
dvātriṃśanmātaraś cakre aṣṭāṣṭakramaśaḥ sthitāḥ //
125.d:
स्थिरा च निष्ठुरा दिव्या निष्कम्पा गदिनी तथा /
द्वात्रिंशन्मातरश् चक्रे अष्टाष्टक्रमशः स्थिताः //
125.m: Sthirā, Niṣṭhurā, Divyā, Niṣkampā, and Gadinī— / thirty-two Mothers reside in the cakra in groups of eight.

125.s:
eka eva raviś candra ekaś caikaikaśaktikā /
bhūtabhedena tīrthāni(1) yathā toyaṃ mahītale //
125.d:
एक एव रविश् चन्द्र एकश् चैकैकशक्तिका /
भूतभेदेन तीर्थानि(1) यथा तोयं महीतले //
125.m: There is only one Sun, only one Moon, and each has a single power; / [they divide] according to the elements [like] sacred fords [differing], just as water upon the earth.

125.s:
prāṇa eko maṇḍalaiś ca bhidyate bhūtapañjare /
vāmadakṣiṇayogena daśadhā sampravartate //
125.d:
प्राण एको मण्डलैश् च भिद्यते भूतपञ्जरे /
वामदक्षिणयोगेन दशधा सम्प्रवर्तते //
125.m: The single breath (prāṇa) is divided by the circles within the cage of the elements; / through the conjunction of left and right, it proceeds in ten ways.

125.s:
vindumuṇḍavicitrañca tattvavastreṇa veṣṭitaṃ /
brahmāṇḍena(2) kapālena piveta paramāmṛtaṃ //
125.d:
विन्दुमुण्डविचित्रञ्च तत्त्ववस्त्रेण वेष्टितं /
ब्रह्माण्डेन(2) कपालेन पिवेत परमामृतं //
125.m: Variegated with the point (bindu) and the skull, wrapped in the cloth of the principles of reality (tattva), / one should drink the supreme nectar from the skull of the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa).

125.s:
pañcavargabalādyuddhe jayo bhavati tacchṛṇu /
a+ākacaṭatapayāḥ śa āsyo varga īritaḥ //
125.d:
पञ्चवर्गबलाद्युद्धे जयो भवति तच्छृणु /
अ+आकचटतपयाः श आस्यो वर्ग ईरितः //
125.m: Hear that: victory in battle comes from the power of the five groups: / a, ā, ka, ca, ṭa, ta, pa, ya, śa—this is stated to be the face-group.

125.s:
i+īkhachaṭhathapharāḥ ṣo vargaś ca dvitīyakaḥ /
u+ūgajaḍadabalāḥ so vargaś ca tṛtīyakaḥ //
125.d:
इ+ईखछठथफराः षो वर्गश् च द्वितीयकः /
उ+ऊगजडदबलाः सो वर्गश् च तृतीयकः //
125.m: i, ī, kha, cha, ṭha, tha, pha, ra, ṣa—and this is the second group. / u, ū, ga, ja, ḍa, da, ba, la, sa—and this is the third group.

125.s:
e+aighajhaḍhadhabhavāḥ so vargaś ca caturthakaḥ /
o au aṃ aḥ ṅañaṇanā mo vargaḥ pañcamo bhavet //
125.d:
ए+ऐघझढधभवाः सो वर्गश् च चतुर्थकः /
ओ औ अं अः ङञणना मो वर्गः पञ्चमो भवेत् //
125.m: e, ai, gha, jha, ḍha, dha, bha, va, sa—and this is the fourth group. / o, au, aṃ, aḥ, ṅa, ña, ṇa, na, ma, ha—this is the fifth group.

125.s:
varṇāścābhyudaye nṝṇāṃ catvāriṃśacca pañca ca /
bālaḥ kumāro yuvā syādvṛddho mṛtyuś ca nāmataḥ //
:n
1 bhūtabhedena bhinnāni iti ṅa./ tāni bhedena bhinnāni iti gha..
2 brahmadaṇḍe iti ṅa..
:p 50
ātmapīdā śoṣakaḥ syādudāsīnaś ca kālakaḥ /
kṛttikā pratipadbhauma ātmano lābhadaḥ smṛtaḥ //
125.d:
वर्णाश्चाभ्युदये नॄणां चत्वारिंशच्च पञ्च च /
बालः कुमारो युवा स्याद्वृद्धो मृत्युश् च नामतः //
:न्
1 भूतभेदेन भिन्नानि इति ङ./ तानि भेदेन भिन्नानि इति घ..
2 ब्रह्मदण्डे इति ङ..
:प् 50
आत्मपीदा शोषकः स्यादुदासीनश् च कालकः /
कृत्तिका प्रतिपद्भौम आत्मनो लाभदः स्मृतः //
125.m:
And there are forty-five phonemes for the prosperity of men; / by name they are child, youth, adult, old man, and death.
[Notes]
1. "bhūtabhedena bhinnāni" in manuscript ṅa; "tāni bhedena bhinnāni" in manuscript gha.
2. "brahmadaṇḍe" in manuscript ṅa. / [Page 50]
[They are called] affliction of self, desiccator, indifferent, and death-dealer.
Kṛttikā, the first lunar day (pratipad), and Mars are remembered to grant gain to oneself.

125.s:
ṣaṣṭhī bhaumo maghā pīḍā ārdrā caikādaśī kujaḥ /
mṛtyurmaghā dvitīyā jño lābhaścārdrā ca saptamī //
125.d:
षष्ठी भौमो मघा पीडा आर्द्रा चैकादशी कुजः /
मृत्युर्मघा द्वितीया ज्ञो लाभश्चार्द्रा च सप्तमी //
125.m: The sixth lunar day, Mars, and Maghā bring affliction; Ārdrā, the eleventh lunar day, and Mars / bring death; Maghā, the second lunar day (dvitīyā), and Mercury bring gain; and Ārdrā and the seventh lunar day,

125.s:
budhe hānirbharaṇī jñaḥ śravaṇaṃ kāla īdṛśaḥ /
jīvo lābhāya ca bhavettṛtīyā pūrvaphalgunī //
125.d:
बुधे हानिर्भरणी ज्ञः श्रवणं काल ईदृशः /
जीवो लाभाय च भवेत्तृतीया पूर्वफल्गुनी //
125.m: under Mercury, bring loss; Bharaṇī and Mercury, [and] Śravaṇa [are] such a time of death. / Jupiter on the third lunar day and Pūrvaphalgunī leads to gain.

125.s:
jīvo 'ṣṭamī(1) dhaniṣṭhārdrā jīvo 'śleṣā trayodaśī /
mṛtyau śukraś caturthī syāt pūrvabhādrapadā śriye //
125.d:
जीवो ऽष्टमी(1) धनिष्ठार्द्रा जीवो ऽश्लेषा त्रयोदशी /
मृत्यौ शुक्रश् चतुर्थी स्यात् पूर्वभाद्रपदा श्रिये //
125.m: Jupiter on the eighth, Dhaniṣṭhā, Ārdrā, and Jupiter on Āśleṣā and the thirteenth / bring death; Venus on the fourth lunar day and Pūrvabhādrapadā brings fortune.

125.s:
pūrvāṣāḍhā ca navamī śukraḥ pīḍākaro bhavet /
bharaṇī bhūtajā śukro yamadaṇḍo hi hānikṛt //
125.d:
पूर्वाषाढा च नवमी शुक्रः पीडाकरो भवेत् /
भरणी भूतजा शुक्रो यमदण्डो हि हानिकृत् //
125.m: Venus on Pūrvāṣāḍhā and the ninth lunar day causes affliction; / Venus on Bharaṇī and the fourteenth lunar day (bhūtajā) is Yama's rod, causing loss.

125.s:
kṛttikāṃ pañcamī mando lābhāya tithirīritā /
aśleṣā daśamī mando yogaḥ pīḍākaro bhavet(2) //
125.d:
कृत्तिकां पञ्चमी मन्दो लाभाय तिथिरीरिता /
अश्लेषा दशमी मन्दो योगः पीडाकरो भवेत्(2) //
125.m: Saturn on Kṛttikā and the fifth lunar day is declared a lunar day for gain; / the combination of Saturn on Āśleṣā and the tenth lunar day causes affliction.

125.s:
maghā śaniḥ pūrṇimā ca yogo bhṛtyukaraḥ smṛtaḥ /
tithiyogaḥ
pūrvottarāgninairṛtyadakṣiṇānilacandramāḥ(3) //
125.d:
मघा शनिः पूर्णिमा च योगो भृत्युकरः स्मृतः /
तिथियोगः
पूर्वोत्तराग्निनैरृत्यदक्षिणानिलचन्द्रमाः(3) //
125.m:
The combination of Maghā, Saturn, and the full moon day is remembered to bring death.
The combination of lunar days.
East, north, Agni [southeast], Nirṛti [southwest], south, Vāyu [northwest], and the Moon [north]—

125.s:
brahmādyāḥ syurdṛṣṭayaḥ syuḥ(4)pratipannavamīmukhāḥ /
rāśibhiḥ sahitā dṛṣṭā grahādyāḥ siddhaye smṛtāḥ //
125.d:
ब्रह्माद्याः स्युर्दृष्टयः स्युः(4)प्रतिपन्नवमीमुखाः /
राशिभिः सहिता दृष्टा ग्रहाद्याः सिद्धये स्मृताः //
125.m: these are the aspects (dṛṣṭi) beginning with Brahmā, starting with the first and ninth lunar days. / The planets and others, beheld together with the zodiacal signs, are remembered to bring success.

125.s:
meṣādyāś caturaḥ kumbhā jayaḥ pūrṇe 'nyathā mṛtiḥ /
sūryādiriktā pūrṇā ca kramādevampradāpayet //
:n
1 jīve 'ṣṭamīti kha..
2 bharaṇītyādiḥ, pīḍākaro bhavetyantaḥ pāṭhaḥ cha.. pustake
nāsti
3 dakṣāgnyanilacandramā iti gha..
4 brahmādyāḥ syustridṛṣṭāḥ syuriti kha..
:p 51
125.d:
मेषाद्याश् चतुरः कुम्भा जयः पूर्णे ऽन्यथा मृतिः /
सूर्यादिरिक्ता पूर्णा च क्रमादेवम्प्रदापयेत् //
:न्
1 जीवे ऽष्टमीति ख..
2 भरणीत्यादिः, पीडाकरो भवेत्यन्तः पाठः छ.. पुस्तके
नास्ति
3 दक्षाग्न्यनिलचन्द्रमा इति घ..
4 ब्रह्माद्याः स्युस्त्रिदृष्टाः स्युरिति ख..
:प् 51
125.m:
The four water-pitchers starting with Aries [signify] victory when full, otherwise death. / One should assign them in order as empty and full, beginning with the Sun.
[Notes]
1. "jīve 'ṣṭamī" in manuscript kha.
2. The reading from "bharaṇī" up to "pīḍākaro bhavet" is missing in manuscript cha.
3. "dakṣāgnyanilacandramā" in manuscript gha.
4. "brahmādyāḥ syustridṛṣṭāḥ syur" in manuscript kha. / [Page 51]

125.s:
raṇe sūrye phalaṃ nāsti some bhaṅgaḥ praśāmyati /
kujena kalahaṃ vidyādbudhaḥ kāmāya vai guruḥ //
125.d:
रणे सूर्ये फलं नास्ति सोमे भङ्गः प्रशाम्यति /
कुजेन कलहं विद्याद्बुधः कामाय वै गुरुः //
125.m: In battle under the Sun, there is no result; under the Moon, defeat is pacified; / under Mars, one should expect conflict; Mercury leads to desire; Jupiter

125.s:
jayāya manase(1) śukro mande bhaṅgo raṇe bhavet /
deyāni piṅgalācakre sūryagāni ca bhāni hi //
125.d:
जयाय मनसे(1) शुक्रो मन्दे भङ्गो रणे भवेत् /
देयानि पिङ्गलाचक्रे सूर्यगानि च भानि हि //
125.m: leads to victory for the mind; under Venus, and under Saturn, defeat occurs in battle. / Indeed, the asterisms moving with the Sun are to be assigned to the Piṅgalā circle.

125.s:
mukhe netre lalāṭe 'tha śirohastorupādake /
pāde mṛtistriṛkṣe syāntrīṇi pakṣe 'rthanāśanam //
125.d:
मुखे नेत्रे ललाटे ऽथ शिरोहस्तोरुपादके /
पादे मृतिस्त्रिऋक्षे स्यान्त्रीणि पक्षे ऽर्थनाशनम् //
125.m: In the mouth, eyes, forehead, and then the head, hands, thighs, and feet: / with three asterisms in the feet there is death, with three in the flank there is destruction of wealth.

125.s:
mukhasthe ca bhavetyauḍā śirasthe kāryanāśanam /
kukṣisthite phalaṃ syācca rāhucakraṃ vadāmyaham //
125.d:
मुखस्थे च भवेत्यौडा शिरस्थे कार्यनाशनम् /
कुक्षिस्थिते फलं स्याच्च राहुचक्रं वदाम्यहम् //
125.m: When situated in the mouth there is affliction; when in the head, ruin of undertakings; / when situated in the belly there is fulfillment. I shall [now] declare the Rāhu cakra.

125.s:
indrācca nairṛtaṅgacchetrairṛtātsomameva ca /
somāddhutāśanaṃ vahnerāpyamāpyācchivālayaṃ //
125.d:
इन्द्राच्च नैरृतङ्गच्छेत्रैरृतात्सोममेव च /
सोमाद्धुताशनं वह्नेराप्यमाप्याच्छिवालयं //
125.m: From Indra [east] it goes to Nirṛti [southwest], and from Nirṛti to the Moon [north]; / from the Moon to the Fire-Consumer [southeast], from fire to the waters [west], and from the waters to Śiva's abode [northeast];

125.s:
rudrādyamaṃ yamādvāyuṃ vāyoś candraṃ vrajet punaḥ /
bhuṅkte catasro nāḍyastu rāhupṛṣṭe jayo raṇe //
125.d:
रुद्राद्यमं यमाद्वायुं वायोश् चन्द्रं व्रजेत् पुनः /
भुङ्क्ते चतस्रो नाड्यस्तु राहुपृष्टे जयो रणे //
125.m: from Rudra [northeast] to Yama [south], from Yama to Vāyu [northwest], and from Vāyu it proceeds again to the Moon. / It consumes four nāḍīs; when Rāhu is at one's back, there is victory in battle.

125.s:
agrato mṛtyumāpnoti tithirāhuṃ vadāmi te /
āgneyādiśivāntaṃ ca pūrṇimāmāditaḥ priye //
125.d:
अग्रतो मृत्युमाप्नोति तिथिराहुं वदामि ते /
आग्नेयादिशिवान्तं च पूर्णिमामादितः प्रिये //
125.m: Facing him, one meets death. I shall declare to you the Rāhu of lunar days: / from the southeast to the northeast, beginning from the full moon day, O dear one.

125.s:
pūrve kṛṣṇāṣṭamīṃ yāvat rāhudṛṣṭau bhayo bhavet /
aiśānyāgneyanairṛtyavāyavye phaṇirāhukaḥ //
125.d:
पूर्वे कृष्णाष्टमीं यावत् राहुदृष्टौ भयो भवेत् /
ऐशान्याग्नेयनैरृत्यवायव्ये फणिराहुकः //
125.m: In the east, up to the eighth day of the dark fortnight, there is danger when in Rāhu's gaze; / the serpent Rāhu resides in the northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest.

125.s:
meṣādyā diśi pūrvādau yatrādityo 'grato mṛtiḥ /
tṛtīyā kṛṣṇapakṣe tu saptamī daśamī tathā //
125.d:
मेषाद्या दिशि पूर्वादौ यत्रादित्यो ऽग्रतो मृतिः /
तृतीया कृष्णपक्षे तु सप्तमी दशमी तथा //
125.m: Aries and the other [signs] are in the east and other directions; where the Sun is in front, death occurs. / The third, seventh, and tenth lunar days in the dark fortnight,

125.s:
caturdaśī tathā śukre caturthyekādaśī tithiḥ /
pañcadaśī viṣṭayasyuḥ pūrṇimāgneyavāyave //
125.d:
चतुर्दशी तथा शुक्रे चतुर्थ्येकादशी तिथिः /
पञ्चदशी विष्टयस्युः पूर्णिमाग्नेयवायवे //
125.m: and the fourteenth, and on Friday the fourth and eleventh lunar days, / and the fifteenth are viṣṭi [inauspicious periods]; the full moon belongs to the southeast and northwest.

125.s:
akacaṭatapayaśā vargāḥ sūryādayo grahāḥ /
:n
1 maṇaye iti kha.. , ṅa.. ca
:p 52
gṛdhrolukaśyenakāś ca piṅgalaḥ kauśikaḥ kramāt //
125.d:
अकचटतपयशा वर्गाः सूर्यादयो ग्रहाः /
:न्
1 मणये इति ख.. , ङ.. च
:प् 52
गृध्रोलुकश्येनकाश् च पिङ्गलः कौशिकः क्रमात् //
125.m:
The groups beginning with a, ka, ca, ṭa, ta, pa, ya, and śa belong to the Sun and the other planets.
[Notes]
1. "maṇaye" in manuscripts kha and ṅa. / [Page 52]
The vulture, owl, falcon, screech-owl, and crow, respectively,

125.s:
sāsasaś ca mayūraś ca goraṅkuḥ pakṣiṇaḥ smṛtāḥ /
ādau sādhyo huto mantra(1) uccāṭe pallavaḥ smṛtaḥ //
125.d:
साससश् च मयूरश् च गोरङ्कुः पक्षिणः स्मृताः /
आदौ साध्यो हुतो मन्त्र(1) उच्चाटे पल्लवः स्मृतः //
125.m: the goose, peacock, and goraṅku bird are remembered as the birds. / The mantra with the person to be affected placed at the beginning, offered as an oblation, is known as the "sprout" in expulsion rites.

125.s:
vaśye jvare tathākarṣe prayogaḥ siddhikārakaḥ /
śānto prīto namaskāro vauṣaṭ puṣṭo vaśādiṣu //
125.d:
वश्ये ज्वरे तथाकर्षे प्रयोगः सिद्धिकारकः /
शान्तो प्रीतो नमस्कारो वौषट् पुष्टो वशादिषु //
125.m: In subjugation, fever, and attraction, the application brings success. / In calming and pleasing, "namas" [is used]; "vauṣaṭ" is for nourishment, subjugation, and so forth;

125.s:
huṃ mṛtyau(2) prītisannāśe vidveṣoccāṭane ca phaṭ /
vaṣaṭ sute ca dīptyādau(3) mantrāṇāṃ jātayaś ca ṣaṭ //
125.d:
हुं मृत्यौ(2) प्रीतिसन्नाशे विद्वेषोच्चाटने च फट् /
वषट् सुते च दीप्त्यादौ(3) मन्त्राणां जातयश् च षट् //
125.m: "huṃ" is for death, destruction of love, enmity, and "phaṭ" for expulsion; / "vaṣaṭ" is for offspring, radiance, and so on. These are the six classes (jāti) of mantras.

125.s:
oṣadhīḥ sampravakṣyāmi mahārakṣāvidhāyinīḥ /
mahākālī tathā caṇḍī vārāhī ceśvarī tathā //
125.d:
ओषधीः सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि महारक्षाविधायिनीः /
महाकाली तथा चण्डी वाराही चेश्वरी तथा //
125.m: I shall fully explain the medicinal herbs that provide great protection: / Mahākālī, Caṇḍī, Vārāhī, and likewise Īśvarī;

125.s:
sudarśanā tathendrāṇī gātrasthā rakṣayanti tam /
balā cātibalā bhīrurmusalī sahadevyapi //
125.d:
सुदर्शना तथेन्द्राणी गात्रस्था रक्षयन्ति तम् /
बला चातिबला भीरुर्मुसली सहदेव्यपि //
125.m: Sudarśanā and Indrāṇī—when placed upon the body, they protect him; / [so too] balā, atibalā, bhīru, musalī, and sahadevī;

125.s:
jātī ca mallikā yūthau gāruḍī bhṛṅgarājakaḥ /
cakrarūpā mahoṣadhyo dhāritā vijayādidāḥ //
125.d:
जाती च मल्लिका यूथौ गारुडी भृङ्गराजकः /
चक्ररूपा महोषध्यो धारिता विजयादिदाः //
125.m: jātī, mallikā, yūthī, gāruḍī, and bhṛṅgarāja. / These great herbs having the form of diagrams, when worn, grant victory and other [boons].

125.s:
grahaṇe ca mahādevi uddhṛtāḥ śubhadāyikāḥ /
mṛdā tu kuñjaraṅkṛtvā sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitam //
125.d:
ग्रहणे च महादेवि उद्धृताः शुभदायिकाः /
मृदा तु कुञ्जरङ्कृत्वा सर्वलक्षणलक्षितम् //
125.m: Uprooted during an eclipse, O great goddess, they bestow auspiciousness. / Having fashioned an elephant of clay endowed with all characteristic marks,

125.s:
tasya pādatale kṛtvā stambhayecchatrumātmanaḥ /
nagāgre caikavṛkṣe ca vajrāhatapradeśake //
125.d:
तस्य पादतले कृत्वा स्तम्भयेच्छत्रुमात्मनः /
नगाग्रे चैकवृक्षे च वज्राहतप्रदेशके //
125.m: and placing [the enemy's name] beneath its foot, one should immobilise one's enemy. / Taking clay from an anthill at the summit of a mountain, at an isolated tree,

125.s:
valmīkamṛdāmāhṛtya mātarau yojayettataḥ /
oṃ namo mahābhairavāya vikṛtadaṃṣṭrograrūpāya
piṅgalākṣāya triśūlakhaḍgadharāya(4) vauṣaṭ
:n
1 ādau hutāśano mantra iti kha..
2 huṃ mṛtau iti kha..
3 vaṣaṭ lābhe ca dīptyādāviti gha.. , cha.. ca
4 triśūlakhaṭvāṅgadharāyeti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , cha.. ca / triśūline
khaḍgakhaṭvāṅgadharāyeti ja..
:p 53
pūjayet kardamaṃ devi stambhayecchastrajālakam //
125.d:
वल्मीकमृदामाहृत्य मातरौ योजयेत्ततः /
ओं नमो महाभैरवाय विकृतदंष्ट्रोग्ररूपाय
पिङ्गलाक्षाय त्रिशूलखड्गधराय(4) वौषट्
:न्
1 आदौ हुताशनो मन्त्र इति ख..
2 हुं मृतौ इति ख..
3 वषट् लाभे च दीप्त्यादाविति घ.. , छ.. च
4 त्रिशूलखट्वाङ्गधरायेति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , छ.. च / त्रिशूलिने
खड्गखट्वाङ्गधरायेति ज..
:प् 53
पूजयेत् कर्दमं देवि स्तम्भयेच्छस्त्रजालकम् //
125.m:
or in a place struck by lightning, one should then unite the two mothers.
“Oṃ, salutation to Mahābhairava of deformed fangs and fierce form, / with reddish-brown eyes, who holds a trident and a sword, vauṣaṭ!”
[Footnote]
1. "ādau hutāśano mantraḥ" in manuscript kha.
2. "huṃ mṛtau" in manuscript kha.
3. "vaṣaṭ lābhe ca dīptyādau" in manuscripts gha. and cha.
4. "triśūlakhaṭvāṅgadharāya" in manuscripts kha., ga., gha., and cha.; "triśūline khaḍgakhaṭvāṅgadharāya" in manuscript ja.
[Page 53]
One should worship the clay [image], O goddess; he can thus immobilise an array of weapons.

125.s:
agnikāryaṃ pravakṣyāmi raṇādau jayavardhanam /
śmaśāne niśi kāṣṭhāgnau nagnī muktaśikho naraḥ //
125.d:
अग्निकार्यं प्रवक्ष्यामि रणादौ जयवर्धनम् /
श्मशाने निशि काष्ठाग्नौ नग्नी मुक्तशिखो नरः //
125.m: I shall explain the fire rite that increases victory in battle and the like. / At night in a cremation ground, over a fire of firewood, a naked man with loosened hair,

125.s:
dakṣiṇāsyastu juhuyānnṛmāṃsaṃ rundhiraṃ viṣaṃ /
tuṣāsthikhaṇḍamiśrantu śatrunāmnā śatāṣṭakam //
125.d:
दक्षिणास्यस्तु जुहुयान्नृमांसं रुन्धिरं विषं /
तुषास्थिखण्डमिश्रन्तु शत्रुनाम्ना शताष्टकम् //
125.m: facing south, should offer human flesh, blood, and poison / mixed with chaff and bone fragments, one hundred and eight times, with the enemy's name.

125.s:
oṃ namo bhagavati kaumāri lala lala lālaya lālaya ghaṇṭādevi amukaṃ
māraya sahasā namo 'stu te bhagavati vidye svāhā
anayā vidyayā homādbandhatvañjāyate ripoḥ(1) /
oṃ vajrakāya vajratuṇḍa kapilapiṅgala karālavadana ūrdhvakeśa
mahābala raktamukha(2) taḍijjihva mahāraudra daṃṣṭrotkaṭa kaha
karālina mahādṛḍhaprahāra laṅgeśvarasetubandha śailapravāha
gaganacara ehyehi bhavaganmahābalaparākrama bhairavo jñāpayati ehyehi
mahāraudra dīrghalāṅgūlena amukaṃ veṣṭaya veṣṭaya jambhaya
jambhaya khana khana vaite hrūṃ phaṭ(3)
aṣṭatriṃśacchatandevi hanumān sarvakumbhakṛt //
125.d:
ओं नमो भगवति कौमारि लल लल लालय लालय घण्टादेवि अमुकं
मारय सहसा नमो ऽस्तु ते भगवति विद्ये स्वाहा
अनया विद्यया होमाद्बन्धत्वञ्जायते रिपोः(1) /
ओं वज्रकाय वज्रतुण्ड कपिलपिङ्गल करालवदन ऊर्ध्वकेश
महाबल रक्तमुख(2) तडिज्जिह्व महारौद्र दंष्ट्रोत्कट कह
करालिन महादृढप्रहार लङ्गेश्वरसेतुबन्ध शैलप्रवाह
गगनचर एह्येहि भवगन्महाबलपराक्रम भैरवो ज्ञापयति एह्येहि
महारौद्र दीर्घलाङ्गूलेन अमुकं वेष्टय वेष्टय जम्भय
जम्भय खन खन वैते ह्रूं फट्(3)
अष्टत्रिंशच्छतन्देवि हनुमान् सर्वकुम्भकृत् //
125.m: “Oṃ, salutation to the revered Kaumārī! Lala lala, fondle, fondle! O goddess of the bell, kill so-and-so swiftly! Salutation to you, revered Vidyā, svāhā!” / By oblations with this vidyā, the enemy is bound. / “Oṃ, you whose body is adamantine, whose mouth is adamantine, who are tawny and reddish-brown, with a terrible face, bristling hair, of great might, red-faced, lightning-tongued, exceedingly fierce, with formidable fangs, laugh! O terrifying one! O you of exceedingly firm strike! O builder of the bridge to the lord of Laṅkā! O torrent of mountains! O sky-walker! Come, come, Lord of great strength and valor! Bhairava commands: Come, come, exceedingly fierce one, entwine, entwine so-and-so with your long tail! Crush, crush! Dig, dig, vaite hrūṃ phaṭ!” / [Thus] the one hundred and thirty-eight syllables, O goddess; Hanumān accomplishes all retention.

125.s:
/
paṭe hanūmatsandarśanādbhaṅgamāyānti śatravaḥ
//52//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe yuddhajayārṇave nānācakrāṇi nāma
pañcaviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 dagdhatvaṃ jāyate kṣaṇāt iti gha.. , ja.. ca
2 vajramukha iti gha..
3 huṃphaḍiti kha..
:p 54
:ś atha ṣaḍviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
nakṣatranirṇayaḥ
125.d:
/
पटे हनूमत्सन्दर्शनाद्भङ्गमायान्ति शत्रवः
//52//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे युद्धजयार्णवे नानाचक्राणि नाम
पञ्चविंशत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 दग्धत्वं जायते क्षणात् इति घ.. , ज.. च
2 वज्रमुख इति घ..
3 हुंफडिति ख..
:प् 54
:श् अथ षड्विंशत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
नक्षत्रनिर्णयः
125.m:
/ By seeing Hanūmat on a cloth, enemies fall into defeat. //52
Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-fifth chapter, titled “Various Diagrams”, in the Great Agni Purāṇa, in the “Ocean of Victory in War”.
[Footnote]
1. "dagdhatvaṃ jāyate kṣaṇāt" in manuscripts gha. and ja.
2. "vajramukha" in manuscript gha.
3. "huṃphaṭ" in manuscript kha.
[Page 54]
Now, the one hundred and twenty-sixth chapter:
Determination of Asterisms.

126.s:
īśvara uvāca
vakṣyāmyṛkṣātmakaṃ piṇḍaṃ śubhāśubhavibuddhaye /
yasminnṛkṣe bhavet sūryastadādau trīṇi mūrdhani(1) //
126.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
वक्ष्याम्यृक्षात्मकं पिण्डं शुभाशुभविबुद्धये /
यस्मिन्नृक्षे भवेत् सूर्यस्तदादौ त्रीणि मूर्धनि(1) //
126.m: The Lord said: / I shall explain the body consisting of asterisms for discerning good and bad fortune. / In whichever asterism the Sun is situated, three [asterisms] starting from that are on the head;

126.s:
ekammukhe dvayannetre hastapāde catuṣṭayaṃ /
hṛdi pañca sute jānau āyurbuddhiṃ vicintayet //
126.d:
एकम्मुखे द्वयन्नेत्रे हस्तपादे चतुष्टयं /
हृदि पञ्च सुते जानौ आयुर्बुद्धिं विचिन्तयेत् //
126.m: one is on the face, two on the eyes, four on the hands and feet, / five on the heart; on the son and knee one should consider lifespan and intellect.

126.s:
śirasthe tu bhavedrājyaṃ piṇḍato vaktrayogataḥ /
netrayoḥ kāntasaubhāgyaṃ hṛdaye dravyasaṅgrahaḥ //
126.d:
शिरस्थे तु भवेद्राज्यं पिण्डतो वक्त्रयोगतः /
नेत्रयोः कान्तसौभाग्यं हृदये द्रव्यसङ्ग्रहः //
126.m: When situated on the head, kingship arises from the body through connection with the mouth; / on the eyes, charm and good fortune; on the heart, acquisition of wealth;

126.s:
haste dhṛtaṃ taskaratvaṅgatāsuradhvagaḥ(2) pade /
kumbhāṣtake bhāni likhya(3) sūryakumbhastu riktakaḥ //
126.d:
हस्ते धृतं तस्करत्वङ्गतासुरध्वगः(2) पदे /
कुम्भाष्तके भानि लिख्य(3) सूर्यकुम्भस्तु रिक्तकः //
126.m: borne on the hand, thievery; on the foot, a traveler whose life is gone. / In eight pots having drawn the asterisms, the pot of the Sun is empty.

126.s:
aśubhaḥ sūryakumbhaḥ syācchubhaḥ pūrvādisaṃsthitaḥ /
phaṇirāhuṃ(4) pravakṣyāmi jayājayavivekadaṃ //
126.d:
अशुभः सूर्यकुम्भः स्याच्छुभः पूर्वादिसंस्थितः /
फणिराहुं(4) प्रवक्ष्यामि जयाजयविवेकदं //
126.m: The pot of the Sun is inauspicious; that placed in the east and other [directions] is auspicious. / I shall explain the serpent Rāhu, which grants discernment of victory and defeat.

126.s:
aṣṭāviṃśāṃllikhedvindūn punarbhājyastribhstribhiḥ /
atha ṛkṣāṇi catvāri rekhāstatraiva dāpayet //
126.d:
अष्टाविंशांल्लिखेद्विन्दून् पुनर्भाज्यस्त्रिभ्स्त्रिभिः /
अथ ऋक्षाणि चत्वारि रेखास्तत्रैव दापयेत् //
126.m: One should draw twenty-eight dots, and divide them again by threes; / then four asterisms; lines should be drawn right there.

126.s:
yasminnṛkṣe sthito rāhustadṛkṣaṃ phaṇimūrdhani(5) /
tadādi vinyased bhāni saptaviṃśakrameṇa tu //
126.d:
यस्मिन्नृक्षे स्थितो राहुस्तदृक्षं फणिमूर्धनि(5) /
तदादि विन्यसेद् भानि सप्तविंशक्रमेण तु //
126.m: In whichever asterism Rāhu is stationed, that asterism is on the head of the serpent; / starting from that, one should arrange the asterisms in the sequence of twenty-seven.

126.s:
vaktre saptagate ṛkṣe mriyate sarva āhave /
:n
1 trīṇi mastake iti ja..
2 gatāyuradhvagaḥ pade iti kha..
3 bhāni likhediti gha.. , ja.. ca
4 kālarāhumiti ṅa..
5 kālamūrdhanīti ṅa.. , ja, ca
:p 55
skandhe bhaṅgaṃ vijānīyātsaptameṣu ca madhyataḥ //
126.d:
वक्त्रे सप्तगते ऋक्षे म्रियते सर्व आहवे /
:न्
1 त्रीणि मस्तके इति ज..
2 गतायुरध्वगः पदे इति ख..
3 भानि लिखेदिति घ.. , ज.. च
4 कालराहुमिति ङ..
5 कालमूर्धनीति ङ.. , ज, च
:प् 55
स्कन्धे भङ्गं विजानीयात्सप्तमेषु च मध्यतः //
126.m:
When the seventh asterism enters the mouth, everyone dies in battle;
[Footnote]
1. "trīṇi mastake" in manuscript ja.
2. "gatāyuradhvagaḥ pade" in manuscript kha.
3. "bhāni likhet" in manuscripts gha. and ja.
4. "kālarāhum" in manuscript ṅa.
5. "kālamūrdhani" in manuscripts ṅa. and ja.
[Page 55]
on the shoulder, one should know defeat; and among the seventh [asterisms] from the middle,

126.s:
udarasthena(1) pūjā ca jayaś caivātmanas tathā /
kaṭideśe sthite yodhe āhave harate parān //
126.d:
उदरस्थेन(1) पूजा च जयश् चैवात्मनस् तथा /
कटिदेशे स्थिते योधे आहवे हरते परान् //
126.m: by one situated in the belly, there is honor and indeed victory for oneself. / When a warrior stands in the region of the waist, he overcomes the enemies in battle.

126.s:
pucchasthitena kīrtiḥ syādrāhudṛṣṭe ca bhe mṛtiḥ /
punaranyaṃ pravakṣyāmi ravirāhubalantava //
126.d:
पुच्छस्थितेन कीर्तिः स्याद्राहुदृष्टे च भे मृतिः /
पुनरन्यं प्रवक्ष्यामि रविराहुबलन्तव //
126.m: By one situated on the tail there is fame, and in an asterism aspected by Rāhu there is death. / Again, I will declare to you another: the strength of the Sun and Rāhu.

126.s:
raviḥ śukro budhaś caiva somaḥ saurirgurus tathā(2) /
lohitaḥ saṃhikaś caiva ete yāmārdhabhāginaḥ //
126.d:
रविः शुक्रो बुधश् चैव सोमः सौरिर्गुरुस् तथा(2) /
लोहितः संहिकश् चैव एते यामार्धभागिनः //
126.m: The Sun, Venus, Mercury, the Moon, Saturn, and Jupiter, / Mars, and Rāhu—these have a share of half a watch.

126.s:
sauriṃ raviñca rāhuñca kṛtvā yatnena pṛṣṭhataḥ /
sa jayet sainyasaṅghātaṃ dyūtamadhvānamāhavaṃ //
126.d:
सौरिं रविञ्च राहुञ्च कृत्वा यत्नेन पृष्ठतः /
स जयेत् सैन्यसङ्घातं द्यूतमध्वानमाहवं //
126.m: Keeping Saturn, the Sun, and Rāhu carefully behind [oneself], / one conquers a host of armies, gambling, a journey, and a battle.

126.s:
rohiṇī cottarāstisro mṛgaḥ pañca sthirāṇi hi /
aśvinī revatī svātī dhaniṣṭhā śatatārakā //
126.d:
रोहिणी चोत्तरास्तिस्रो मृगः पञ्च स्थिराणि हि /
अश्विनी रेवती स्वाती धनिष्ठा शततारका //
126.m: Rohiṇī and the three Uttarās, and Mṛgaśīrṣa: these five are fixed; / Aśvinī, Revatī, Svātī, Dhaniṣṭhā, and Śatabhiṣaj,

126.s:
kṣiprāṇi pañcabhānyeva yātrārthī caiva(3) yojayet /
anurādhāhastamūlaṃ mṛgaḥ puṣyaṃ punarvasuḥ //
126.d:
क्षिप्राणि पञ्चभान्येव यात्रार्थी चैव(3) योजयेत् /
अनुराधाहस्तमूलं मृगः पुष्यं पुनर्वसुः //
126.m: are the five swift asterisms; one desiring to journey should employ them. / Anurādhā, Hasta, Mūla, Mṛgaśīrṣa, Puṣya, and Punarvasu,

126.s:
sarvakāryeṣu caitāni jyeṣṭhā citrā viśākhayā /
purvāstisro 'gnirbharaṇī maghārdrāśleṣādāruṇāḥ //
126.d:
सर्वकार्येषु चैतानि ज्येष्ठा चित्रा विशाखया /
पुर्वास्तिस्रो ऽग्निर्भरणी मघार्द्राश्लेषादारुणाः //
126.m: these are for all undertakings. Jyeṣṭhā, Citrā, with Viśākhā, / the three Pūrvās, Kṛttikā, Bharaṇī, Maghā, Ārdrā, and Āśleṣā are fierce.

126.s:
sthāvareṣu sthiraṃ hy ṛkṣaṃ yātrāyāṃ kṣipramuttamaṃ /
saubhāgyārthe mṛdūnyeva ugreṣūgrantu kārayet //
126.d:
स्थावरेषु स्थिरं ह्य् ऋक्षं यात्रायां क्षिप्रमुत्तमं /
सौभाग्यार्थे मृदून्येव उग्रेषूग्रन्तु कारयेत् //
126.m: For immovable [undertakings], a fixed asterism [is best]; for a journey, a swift one is excellent; / for the sake of good fortune, gentle ones; in fierce matters, one should perform a fierce rite;

126.s:
dāruṇe dāruṇaṃ kuryādvakṣye cādhomukhādikaṃ /
kṛtrikā bharaṇyaśleṣā viśākhā pitṛnairṛtam //
:n
1 udarasthe ceti kha..
2 kaṭideśa ity ādiḥ, saurirgurustathetyantaḥ pāṭhaḥ gha.. pustake
nāsti
3 yātrādhvani ceti kha.. , gha.. ca
:p 56
126.d:
दारुणे दारुणं कुर्याद्वक्ष्ये चाधोमुखादिकं /
कृत्रिका भरण्यश्लेषा विशाखा पितृनैरृतम् //
:न्
1 उदरस्थे चेति ख..
2 कटिदेश इत्य् आदिः, सौरिर्गुरुस्तथेत्यन्तः पाठः घ.. पुस्तके
नास्ति
3 यात्राध्वनि चेति ख.. , घ.. च
:प् 56
126.m:
in cruel matters, one should act in a cruel [asterism]. And I shall declare the downward-facing and other [asterisms]. / Kṛttikā, Bharaṇī, Āśleṣā, Viśākhā, Maghā, Mūla,
[Footnote]
1. "udarasthe ca" in manuscript kha.
2. The reading beginning with "kaṭideśa" and ending with "saurirgurustathā" is missing in manuscript gha.
3. "yātrādhvani ca" in manuscripts kha. and gha.
[Page 56]

126.s:
pūrvātrayamadhovaktraṃ karma cādhomukhañcaret(1) /
eṣu kūpataḍāgādi vidyākarma bhiṣakkriyā //
126.d:
पूर्वात्रयमधोवक्त्रं कर्म चाधोमुखञ्चरेत्(1) /
एषु कूपतडागादि विद्याकर्म भिषक्क्रिया //
126.m: and the triad of Pūrvās are downward-facing; one should perform downward-facing work [under them]. / In these [occur] wells, ponds, and the like, rites of learning, and medical treatments,

126.s:
sthāpanannaukābhūpādividhānaṃ(2) khananantathā /
revatī cāśvinī citrā hastā svātī punarvasuḥ //
126.d:
स्थापनन्नौकाभूपादिविधानं(2) खननन्तथा /
रेवती चाश्विनी चित्रा हस्ता स्वाती पुनर्वसुः //
126.m: installation, the management of boats, kings, and the like, as well as excavation. / Revatī, Aśvinī, Citrā, Hasta, Svātī, Punarvasu,

126.s:
anurādhā mṛgo jyeṣṭhā nava vai pārśvatomukhāḥ /
eṣu rājyābhiṣekañca paṭṭabandhaṅgajāśvayoḥ //
126.d:
अनुराधा मृगो ज्येष्ठा नव वै पार्श्वतोमुखाः /
एषु राज्याभिषेकञ्च पट्टबन्धङ्गजाश्वयोः //
126.m: Anurādhā, Mṛgaśīrṣa, and Jyeṣṭhā: these nine indeed face sideways. / In these [should be performed] royal consecration, the binding of diadem on elephants and horses,

126.s:
ārāmagṛhaprāsādaṃ prākāraṃ kṣetratoraṇaṃ /
dhvajacihnapatākāś ca(3) sarvānetāṃś ca kārayet //
126.d:
आरामगृहप्रासादं प्राकारं क्षेत्रतोरणं /
ध्वजचिह्नपताकाश् च(3) सर्वानेतांश् च कारयेत् //
126.m: groves, houses, temples, enclosures, fields, and arched gateways; / banners, emblems, and flags—all these one should have made.

126.s:
dvādaśī sūryadagdhā tu candreṇaikadaśī tathā /
bhaumena daśamī dagdhā tṛtīyā vai budhena ca //
126.d:
द्वादशी सूर्यदग्धा तु चन्द्रेणैकदशी तथा /
भौमेन दशमी दग्धा तृतीया वै बुधेन च //
126.m: The twelfth lunar day is burned by the Sun, and the eleventh by the Moon; / the tenth is burned by Mars, and the third indeed by Mercury;

126.s:
ṣaṣṭī ca guruṇā dagdhā dvitīyā bhṛguṇā tathā /
saptamī sūryaputreṇa tripuṣkaramatho vade //
126.d:
षष्टी च गुरुणा दग्धा द्वितीया भृगुणा तथा /
सप्तमी सूर्यपुत्रेण त्रिपुष्करमथो वदे //
126.m: the sixth is burned by Jupiter, and the second by Venus; / the seventh by Saturn. Now I will speak of the Tripuṣkara.

126.s:
dvitīyā dvādaśī caiva saptamī vai tṛtīyayā(4) /
ravirbhaumas tathā(5) śauriḥ ṣaḍetāstu tripuṣkarāḥ(6) //
126.d:
द्वितीया द्वादशी चैव सप्तमी वै तृतीयया(4) /
रविर्भौमस् तथा(5) शौरिः षडेतास्तु त्रिपुष्कराः(6) //
126.m:
The dvitīyā, the dvādaśī, and the saptamī, as well as the tṛtīyā,
together with the Sun, Mars, and Saturn—these six make up the tripuṣkara.

126.s:
viśākhā kṛttikā caiva uttare dve punarvasuḥ /
pūrvabhādrapadā caiva ṣaḍete tu tripuṣkarāḥ //
126.d:
विशाखा कृत्तिका चैव उत्तरे द्वे पुनर्वसुः /
पूर्वभाद्रपदा चैव षडेते तु त्रिपुष्कराः //
126.m:
Viśākhā, Kṛttikā, the two Uttarās, Punarvasu,
and Pūrvabhādrapadā—these six constellations also make up the tripuṣkara.

126.s:
lābho hānirjayo vṛddhiḥ putrajanma tathaiva ca /
naṣṭaṃ bhraṣṭaṃ vinaṣṭaṃ vā tatsarvantriguṇaṃ(7) bhavet //
:n
1 cādhomukhaṃ bhavediti kha..
2 naukādyūtādividhānamiti ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. ca
3 vajracihnapatākāśceti jha..
4 tṛtīyaketi ṅa.. , ja.. ca
5 gururbhaumastatheti ka.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. ca
6 ṣaḍetāstriṣu puṣkarā iti ka.. , kha.. , ṅa.. , cha.. ca
7 tatsarvaṃ dviguṇamiti kha.. , cha.. ca
:p 57
126.d:
लाभो हानिर्जयो वृद्धिः पुत्रजन्म तथैव च /
नष्टं भ्रष्टं विनष्टं वा तत्सर्वन्त्रिगुणं(7) भवेत् //
:न्
1 चाधोमुखं भवेदिति ख..
2 नौकाद्यूतादिविधानमिति ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. च
3 वज्रचिह्नपताकाश्चेति झ..
4 तृतीयकेति ङ.. , ज.. च
5 गुरुर्भौमस्तथेति क.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. च
6 षडेतास्त्रिषु पुष्करा इति क.. , ख.. , ङ.. , छ.. च
7 तत्सर्वं द्विगुणमिति ख.. , छ.. च
:प् 57
126.m:
Profit, loss, victory, increase, and the birth of a son—
whatever is lost, fallen, or destroyed—all that becomes threefold.
[Notes]
1. "cādhomukhaṃ bhavediti" in manuscript kha.
2. "naukādyūtādividhānamiti" in manuscripts ga, gha, and ṅa.
3. "vajracihnapatākāśceti" in manuscript jha.
4. "tṛtīyaketi" in manuscripts ṅa and ja.
5. "gururbhaumastatheti" in manuscripts ka, ga, gha, and ṅa.
6. "ṣaḍetāstriṣu puṣkarā iti" in manuscripts ka, kha, ṅa, and cha.
7. "tatsarvaṃ dviguṇamiti" in manuscripts kha and cha.
[Page 57]

126.s:
aśvinī bharaṇī caiva aśleṣā puṣyameva ca /
khātiś caiva viśākhā ca śravaṇaṃ saptamaṃ punaḥ //
126.d:
अश्विनी भरणी चैव अश्लेषा पुष्यमेव च /
खातिश् चैव विशाखा च श्रवणं सप्तमं पुनः //
126.m:
Aśvinī, Bharaṇī, Āśleṣā, Puṣya,
Svātī, Viśākhā, and Śravaṇa as the seventh:

126.s:
etāni dṛḍhacakṣūṃṣi paśyanati ca diśo daśa /
yātrāsu dūragasyāpi āgamaḥ puṇyagocare //
126.d:
एतानि दृढचक्षूंषि पश्यनति च दिशो दश /
यात्रासु दूरगस्यापि आगमः पुण्यगोचरे //
126.m:
these are the 'strong-eyed' [asterisms], and they look toward the ten directions.
In journeys, even for one gone far away, there is a return under an auspicious transit.

126.s:
āṣāḍhe revatī citrā kekarāṇi punarvasuḥ /
eṣu pañcasu ṛkṣeṣu(1) nirgatasyāgamo bhavet //
126.d:
आषाढे रेवती चित्रा केकराणि पुनर्वसुः /
एषु पञ्चसु ऋक्षेषु(1) निर्गतस्यागमो भवेत् //
126.m:
The two Āṣāḍhās, Revatī, Citrā, and Punarvasu are the 'squint-eyed' [asterisms].
Under these five asterisms, one who has departed will return.

126.s:
kṛttikā rohiṇī saumyaṃ phalgunī ca maghā tathā /
mūlaṃ jyeṣṭhānurādhā ca dhaniṣṭhā śatatārakāḥ //
126.d:
कृत्तिका रोहिणी सौम्यं फल्गुनी च मघा तथा /
मूलं ज्येष्ठानुराधा च धनिष्ठा शततारकाः //
126.m:
Kṛttikā, Rohiṇī, Mṛgaśīrṣa, Phalgunī, Maghā,
Mūla, Jyeṣṭhā, Anurādhā, Dhaniṣṭhā, and Śatabhiṣaj,

126.s:
pūrvabhādrapadā caiva cipiṭāni ca tāni hi(2) /
adhvānaṃ vrajamānasya punarevāgamo bhavet //
126.d:
पूर्वभाद्रपदा चैव चिपिटानि च तानि हि(2) /
अध्वानं व्रजमानस्य पुनरेवागमो भवेत् //
126.m:
along with Pūrvabhādrapadā—these are the 'flat-eyed' [asterisms].
For one traveling on a journey, there will surely be a return.

126.s:
hasta uttarabhādraś ca ārdrāṣāḍhā tathaiva ca /
naṣṭārthāś caiva dṛśyante saṅgrāmo naiva vidyate //
126.d:
हस्त उत्तरभाद्रश् च आर्द्राषाढा तथैव च /
नष्टार्थाश् चैव दृश्यन्ते सङ्ग्रामो नैव विद्यते //
126.m:
Hastā, Uttarabhādrapadā, Ārdrā, and Uttarāṣāḍhā:
under these, lost goods are found, and no battle takes place.

126.s:
punarvakṣyāmi gaṇḍāntamṛkṣamadhye yathā sthitam /
revatyante caturnāḍī(3) aśvinyādicatuṣṭayam //
126.d:
पुनर्वक्ष्यामि गण्डान्तमृक्षमध्ये यथा स्थितम् /
रेवत्यन्ते चतुर्नाडी(3) अश्विन्यादिचतुष्टयम् //
126.m:
Next I will speak of the gaṇḍānta situated between the asterisms.
Four nāḍīs at the end of Revatī and four at the beginning of Aśvinī:

126.s:
ubhayoryāmamātrantu varjayettat prayatnataḥ /
aśleṣānte maghādau tu ghaṭikānāṃ catuṣṭayam //
126.d:
उभयोर्याममात्रन्तु वर्जयेत्तत् प्रयत्नतः /
अश्लेषान्ते मघादौ तु घटिकानां चतुष्टयम् //
126.m:
one should carefully avoid that period of just one watch (yāma) between both.
Four ghaṭikās at the end of Āśleṣā and at the beginning of Maghā

126.s:
dvitīyaṃ gaṇḍamākhyātaṃ tṛtīyaṃ bhairavi śṛṇu /
jyeṣṭhābhamūlayormadhye ugrarūpantu yāmakam //
:n
1 kekareṣu ca ṛkṣeṣu iti cha..
2 cipiṭāni ca bhāni hi iti ka.. , cha.. ca
3 revatyante catuṣkantu iti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , cha.. , ja.. ca
:p 58
126.d:
द्वितीयं गण्डमाख्यातं तृतीयं भैरवि शृणु /
ज्येष्ठाभमूलयोर्मध्ये उग्ररूपन्तु यामकम् //
:न्
1 केकरेषु च ऋक्षेषु इति छ..
2 चिपिटानि च भानि हि इति क.. , छ.. च
3 रेवत्यन्ते चतुष्कन्तु इति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , छ.. , ज.. च
:प् 58
126.m:
is declared to be the second gaṇḍa; hear of the third, O Bhairavī:
between the asterism Jyeṣṭhā and Mūla, a watch of terrible nature.
[Notes]
1. "kekareṣu ca ṛkṣeṣu iti" in manuscript cha.
2. "cipiṭāni ca bhāni hi iti" in manuscripts ka and cha.
3. "revatyante catuṣkantu iti" in manuscripts kha, ga, gha, ṅa, cha, and ja.
[Page 58]

126.s:
na kuryācchubhakarmāṇi yadīcchedātmajīvitaṃ /
dārake jātakāle ca(1) mriyete pitṛmātaro //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe nakṣatranirṇayo nāma
ṣaḍviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha saptaviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
nānābalāni
īśvara uvāca(2)
126.d:
न कुर्याच्छुभकर्माणि यदीच्छेदात्मजीवितं /
दारके जातकाले च(1) म्रियेते पितृमातरो //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नक्षत्रनिर्णयो नाम
षड्विंशत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ सप्तविंशत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
नानाबलानि
ईश्वर उवाच(2)
126.m:
One should not undertake auspicious deeds if one desires life for oneself.
When a child is born [at such a time], both mother and father die.
Thus ends the one hundred twenty-sixth chapter, named "Determination of Asterisms," in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the one hundred twenty-seventh chapter:
Various planetary strengths.
The Lord said:

127.s:
viṣkumbhe ghaṭikāstisraḥ śūle pañca vivarjayet(3) /
ṣaṭ ṣaṭ(4) gaṇḍe 'nigaṇḍe ca nava vyādyātavajrayoḥ //
127.d:
विष्कुम्भे घटिकास्तिस्रः शूले पञ्च विवर्जयेत्(3) /
षट् षट्(4) गण्डे ऽनिगण्डे च नव व्याद्यातवज्रयोः //
127.m:
In the Viṣkumbha [yoga], one should avoid three ghaṭikās; in Śūla, five;
six each in Gaṇḍa and Atigaṇḍa; and nine in Vyāghāta and Vajra.

127.s:
parighe ca vyatīpāte ubhayorapi taddinam /
vaidhṛte taddinañcaiva yātrāyuddhādikantyajet //
127.d:
परिघे च व्यतीपाते उभयोरपि तद्दिनम् /
वैधृते तद्दिनञ्चैव यात्रायुद्धादिकन्त्यजेत् //
127.m:
In Parigha and Vyatīpāta, the whole day in both cases,
and likewise the whole day in Vaidhṛta, one must avoid journeys, battles, and the like.

127.s:
grahaiḥ śubhāśubhaṃ vakṣye devi meṣādirāśitaḥ(5) /
candraśukrau ca janmasthyau varjitau śubhadāyakau //
:n
1 jātake cāpīti kha..
2 agniruvāceti cha..
3 pañca ca varjayediti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. ca
4 ṣaṭ ca gaṇḍe 'tigaṇḍe ceti kha.. , gha.. , cha.. ca / sapta
gaṇḍetigaṇḍe ceti ga.. , ṅa.. ca
5 meṣādirāśibhiriti ja..
:p 59
127.d:
ग्रहैः शुभाशुभं वक्ष्ये देवि मेषादिराशितः(5) /
चन्द्रशुक्रौ च जन्मस्थ्यौ वर्जितौ शुभदायकौ //
:न्
1 जातके चापीति ख..
2 अग्निरुवाचेति छ..
3 पञ्च च वर्जयेदिति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. च
4 षट् च गण्डे ऽतिगण्डे चेति ख.. , घ.. , छ.. च / सप्त
गण्डेतिगण्डे चेति ग.. , ङ.. च
5 मेषादिराशिभिरिति ज..
:प् 59
127.m:
I shall speak of the auspicious and inauspicious [effects] caused by the planets, O goddess, from Aries and the other signs.
The Moon and Venus situated in the natal sign, when free [from affliction], bestow good fortune.
[Notes]
1. "jātake cāpīti" in manuscript kha.
2. "agniruvāceti" in manuscript cha.
3. "pañca ca varjayediti" in manuscripts kha, ga, gha, and ṅa.
4. "ṣaṭ ca gaṇḍe 'tigaṇḍe ceti" in manuscripts kha, gha, and cha; "sapta gaṇḍetigaṇḍe ceti" in manuscripts ga and ṅa.
5. "meṣādirāśibhiriti" in manuscript ja.
[Page 59]

127.s:
dvitīyo maṅgalo 'thārkaḥ sauriś caiva tu saiṃhikaḥ /
dravyanāśamalābhañca āhave bhaṅgamādiśet //
127.d:
द्वितीयो मङ्गलो ऽथार्कः सौरिश् चैव तु सैंहिकः /
द्रव्यनाशमलाभञ्च आहवे भङ्गमादिशेत् //
127.m:
Mars in the second house, as well as the Sun, Saturn, and Rāhu,
indicates loss of wealth, lack of gain, and defeat in battle.

127.s:
somo budho bhṛgurjīmo dvitīyasthāḥ śubhāvahāḥ /
tṛtīyastho yadā bhānuḥ śanirbhaumo bhṛgus tathā //
127.d:
सोमो बुधो भृगुर्जीमो द्वितीयस्थाः शुभावहाः /
तृतीयस्थो यदा भानुः शनिर्भौमो भृगुस् तथा //
127.m:
The Moon, Mercury, Venus, and Jupiter situated in the second bring auspiciousness.
When the Sun, Saturn, Mars, and Venus are in the third,

127.s:
budhaś caivendū rāhuś ca sarve te phaladā grahāḥ /
budhaśukrau caturthau tu śeṣāś caiva bhayāvahāḥ //
127.d:
बुधश् चैवेन्दू राहुश् च सर्वे ते फलदा ग्रहाः /
बुधशुक्रौ चतुर्थौ तु शेषाश् चैव भयावहाः //
127.m:
as well as Mercury, the Moon, and Rāhu—all these are fruit-yielding planets.
Mercury and Venus in the fourth [are good], but the rest cause fear.

127.s:
pañcamastho yadā jīvaḥ śukraḥ saumyaś ca candramāḥ /
dadeta(1) cepsitaṃ lābhaṃ ṣaṣṭhe sthāne śubho raviḥ //
127.d:
पञ्चमस्थो यदा जीवः शुक्रः सौम्यश् च चन्द्रमाः /
ददेत(1) चेप्सितं लाभं षष्ठे स्थाने शुभो रविः //
127.m:
When Jupiter, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon are in the fifth,
they grant desired gain; the Sun in the sixth house is auspicious.

127.s:
candraḥ saurirmaṅgalaś ca grahā devi svarāśitaḥ /
budhaś ca śubhadaḥ ṣaṣṭhe tyajet ṣaṣṭhaṃ guruṃbhṛguṃ //
127.d:
चन्द्रः सौरिर्मङ्गलश् च ग्रहा देवि स्वराशितः /
बुधश् च शुभदः षष्ठे त्यजेत् षष्ठं गुरुंभृगुं //
127.m:
The Moon, Saturn, and Mars, O goddess, [are auspicious] when in their own signs.
Mercury in the sixth also brings good fortune; one should avoid Jupiter and Venus in the sixth.

127.s:
saptamo 'rkaḥ śanirbhaumo rāhurhānyai sukhāya ca /
jīvo bhṛguś ca saumyaś ca jñaśukro cāṣṭamau śubhau //
127.d:
सप्तमो ऽर्कः शनिर्भौमो राहुर्हान्यै सुखाय च /
जीवो भृगुश् च सौम्यश् च ज्ञशुक्रो चाष्टमौ शुभौ //
127.m:
The Sun, Saturn, Mars, and Rāhu in the seventh bring loss, but happiness [is brought by]
Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury; Mercury and Venus in the eighth are auspicious.

127.s:
śeṣā grahās tathā hānyai jñabhṛgū navamau śubhau /
śeṣā hānyai ca lābhāya daśamau bhṛgubhāskarau //
127.d:
शेषा ग्रहास् तथा हान्यै ज्ञभृगू नवमौ शुभौ /
शेषा हान्यै च लाभाय दशमौ भृगुभास्करौ //
127.m:
The remaining planets likewise bring loss; Mercury and Venus in the ninth are auspicious.
The rest bring loss; Venus and the Sun in the tenth bring gain.

127.s:
śanirbhaumaś ca rāhuś ca candraḥ saumyaḥ śubhāvahaḥ /
śubhāś caikādaśe sarve varjayeddaśame(2) gurum //
127.d:
शनिर्भौमश् च राहुश् च चन्द्रः सौम्यः शुभावहः /
शुभाश् चैकादशे सर्वे वर्जयेद्दशमे(2) गुरुम् //
127.m:
Saturn, Mars, Rāhu, the Moon, and Mercury bring auspiciousness [in the tenth];
all planets are auspicious in the eleventh; one should avoid Jupiter in the tenth.

127.s:
budhaśukrau dvādaśasthau śeṣān dvādaśagāṃstyajet /
ahorātre dvādaśa syū rāśayastān vadāmyaham //
127.d:
बुधशुक्रौ द्वादशस्थौ शेषान् द्वादशगांस्त्यजेत् /
अहोरात्रे द्वादश स्यू राशयस्तान् वदाम्यहम् //
127.m:
Mercury and Venus are [favorable] in the twelfth; one should avoid the rest when in the twelfth.
There are twelve signs in a day and night; I shall speak of them:

127.s:
mīno meṣo 'tha mithunañcatasro nāḍayo vṛṣaḥ /
ṣaṭ karkasiṃhakanyāś ca tulā pañca ca vṛścikaḥ //
127.d:
मीनो मेषो ऽथ मिथुनञ्चतस्रो नाडयो वृषः /
षट् कर्कसिंहकन्याश् च तुला पञ्च च वृश्चिकः //
127.m:
Pisces, Aries, Gemini, and Taurus have four nāḍīs;
Cancer, Leo, and Virgo have six; Libra and Scorpio have five;

127.s:
dhanurnakro ghaṭaś caiva sūryago rāśirādyakaḥ /
:n
1 dadātīti kha..
2 varjayeddaśamiti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. ca
:p 60
carasthiradviḥsvabhāvā meṣādyāḥ syuryathākramam //
127.d:
धनुर्नक्रो घटश् चैव सूर्यगो राशिराद्यकः /
:न्
1 ददातीति ख..
2 वर्जयेद्दशमिति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. च
:प् 60
चरस्थिरद्विःस्वभावा मेषाद्याः स्युर्यथाक्रमम् //
127.m:
Sagittarius, Capricorn, and Aquarius—the first sign is that occupied by the Sun.
[Notes]
1. "dadātīti" in manuscript kha.
2. "varjayeddaśamiti" in manuscripts kha, ga, gha, and ṅa.
[Page 60]
Movable, fixed, and dual signs follow in order, beginning with Aries.

127.s:
kulīro makaraś caiva tulāmeṣādayaś carāḥ /
carakāryaṃ jayaṃ kāmamācarecca śubhaśubham //
127.d:
कुलीरो मकरश् चैव तुलामेषादयश् चराः /
चरकार्यं जयं काममाचरेच्च शुभशुभम् //
127.m:
Cancer, Capricorn, Libra, Aries, and so forth are movable;
in them one should undertake movable undertakings, victory, desired ends, and both auspicious and inauspicious deeds.

127.s:
sthiro vṛṣo hariḥ kumbho vṛścikaḥ sthirakāryake /
śīghraḥ samāgamo nāsti rogārto nauva mucyate //
127.d:
स्थिरो वृषो हरिः कुम्भो वृश्चिकः स्थिरकार्यके /
शीघ्रः समागमो नास्ति रोगार्तो नौव मुच्यते //
127.m:
Taurus, Leo, Aquarius, and Scorpio are fixed; in a fixed undertaking [they are used].
[Under them] there is no swift arrival, and one stricken with sickness is not released.

127.s:
mithunaṃ kanyakā maunī dhanuś ca dviḥsvabhāvakaḥ /
dviḥsvabhāvāḥ śubhāś caite sarvakāryeṣu nityaśaḥ //
127.d:
मिथुनं कन्यका मौनी धनुश् च द्विःस्वभावकः /
द्विःस्वभावाः शुभाश् चैते सर्वकार्येषु नित्यशः //
127.m:
Gemini, Virgo, Pisces, and Sagittarius are dual;
these dual signs are always auspicious for all undertakings:

127.s:
yātrāvāṇijyasaṅgrāme vivāhe rājadarśane /
vṛddhiṃ jayantathā lābhaṃ yuddhe jayamavāpnuyāt //
127.d:
यात्रावाणिज्यसङ्ग्रामे विवाहे राजदर्शने /
वृद्धिं जयन्तथा लाभं युद्धे जयमवाप्नुयात् //
127.m:
on journeys, in trade, in battle, in marriage, and in audience with the king;
one will obtain increase, triumph, gain, and victory in war.

127.s:
aśvinī viṃśatārāś ca turagasyākṛtiryathā /
yadyatra kurute vṛṣṭimekarātraṃ pravarṣati //
127.d:
अश्विनी विंशताराश् च तुरगस्याकृतिर्यथा /
यद्यत्र कुरुते वृष्टिमेकरात्रं प्रवर्षति //
127.m:
Aśvinī has twenty stars, like the shape of a horse;
if it causes rain on this asterism, it rains for a single night.

127.s:
yamabhe tu yadā vṛṣṭiḥ pakṣamekantu varṣati //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe yuddhajayārṇave nānābalāni nāma
saptaviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha aṣṭāviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
koṭacakram
127.d:
यमभे तु यदा वृष्टिः पक्षमेकन्तु वर्षति //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे युद्धजयार्णवे नानाबलानि नाम
सप्तविंशत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ अष्टाविंशत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
कोटचक्रम्
127.m:
When there is rain on the asterism of Yama (Bharaṇī), it rains for an entire fortnight.
Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-seventh chapter, entitled “Various Armies”, in the Ocean of Victory in Battle in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now, the one hundred and twenty-eighth chapter:
[The Fort Diagram]

128.s:
īavara uvāca
koṭacakraṃ pravakṣyāmi caturasraṃ puraṃ likhet /
caturasraṃ punarmadhye tanmadhye caturasrakam //
:p 61
128.d:
ईअवर उवाच
कोटचक्रं प्रवक्ष्यामि चतुरस्रं पुरं लिखेत् /
चतुरस्रं पुनर्मध्ये तन्मध्ये चतुरस्रकम् //
:प् 61
128.m:
The Lord said: / I will declare the fort diagram. One should draw a square city, / a square again inside it, and a square inside that.
:p 61

128.s:
nāḍītritayacihnāḍhyaṃ meṣādyāḥ pūrvadiṅmukhāḥ /
kṛttikā pūrvabhāge tu aśleṣāgneyagocare //
128.d:
नाडीत्रितयचिह्नाढ्यं मेषाद्याः पूर्वदिङ्मुखाः /
कृत्तिका पूर्वभागे तु अश्लेषाग्नेयगोचरे //
128.m: Marked with a triad of channels, the signs beginning with Aries face east. / Kṛttikā is in the eastern division, while Āśleṣā is in the south-eastern sector;

128.s:
bharaṇī dakṣiṇe deyā viśākhāṃ nairṛte nyaset /
anurādhāṃ paścime ca śravaṇaṃ vāyugocare //
128.d:
भरणी दक्षिणे देया विशाखां नैरृते न्यसेत् /
अनुराधां पश्चिमे च श्रवणं वायुगोचरे //
128.m: Bharaṇī is to be placed in the south; one should assign Viśākhā in the south-west, / Anurādhā in the west, and Śravaṇa in the north-western sector;

128.s:
dhanbiṣṭhāñcottare nyasya aiśānyāṃ revatīṃ tathā /
vāhyanāḍyāṃ sthitānyeva aṣṭau hy ṛkṣāṇi yatnataḥ //
128.d:
धन्बिष्ठाञ्चोत्तरे न्यस्य ऐशान्यां रेवतीं तथा /
वाह्यनाड्यां स्थितान्येव अष्टौ ह्य् ऋक्षाणि यत्नतः //
128.m: and having placed Dhaniṣṭhā in the north, Revatī likewise in the north-east. / Indeed, these eight asterisms are positioned carefully in the outer channel.

128.s:
rohiṇīpuṣyaphalguṇyaḥ svātī jyeṣṭhā krameṇa tu /
abhijicchatatārā tu aśvinī madhyanāḍikā //
128.d:
रोहिणीपुष्यफल्गुण्यः स्वाती ज्येष्ठा क्रमेण तु /
अभिजिच्छततारा तु अश्विनी मध्यनाडिका //
128.m: Rohiṇī, Puṣya, the Phalgus, Svātī, and Jyeṣṭhā in sequence, / Abhijit, Śatatārā, and Aśvinī are in the middle channel.

128.s:
koṭamadhye tu yā nāḍī kathayāmi prayatnataḥ /
mṛgaścābhyantare pūrvaṃ tasyāgneye punarvasuḥ //
128.d:
कोटमध्ये तु या नाडी कथयामि प्रयत्नतः /
मृगश्चाभ्यन्तरे पूर्वं तस्याग्नेये पुनर्वसुः //
128.m: The channel which is inside the fort, I declare with diligence: / Mṛgaśīrṣa is in the interior to the east; Punarvasu is to its south-east;

128.s:
uttarāphalgunī yāmye citrā nairṛtasaṃsthitā /
mūlantu paścime nyasyottarāṣāḍhāntu vāyave //
128.d:
उत्तराफल्गुनी याम्ये चित्रा नैरृतसंस्थिता /
मूलन्तु पश्चिमे न्यस्योत्तराषाढान्तु वायवे //
128.m: Uttarāphalgunī is in the south; Citrā is situated in the south-west; / having placed Mūla in the west, [one should place] Uttarāṣāḍhā in the north-west;

128.s:
pūrvabhādrapadā saumye revatī īśagocare /
