koṭasyābhyantare nāḍī hy ṛkṣāṣṭakasamanvitā //
128.d:
पूर्वभाद्रपदा सौम्ये रेवती ईशगोचरे /
कोटस्याभ्यन्तरे नाडी ह्य् ऋक्षाष्टकसमन्विता //
128.m: Pūrvabhādrapadā is in the north, and Revatī in the north-eastern quarter. / The channel inside the fort is endowed with this set of eight asterisms.

128.s:
ārdrā hastā tathāṣāḍhā catuṣkañcottarātrikam /
madhye stambhacatuṣkantu dadyāt koṭasya koṭare //
128.d:
आर्द्रा हस्ता तथाषाढा चतुष्कञ्चोत्तरात्रिकम् /
मध्ये स्तम्भचतुष्कन्तु दद्यात् कोटस्य कोटरे //
128.m: Ārdrā, Hastā, also [Pūrv]āṣāḍhā, and Uttarābhādrapadā form a group of four. / One should place the four pillars in the middle, in the cavity of the fort.

128.s:
evaṃ durgasya vinyāsaṃ vāhye sthānaṃ diśādhipāt /
āgantuko yadā yoddhā ṛkṣavān syātphalānvitaḥ //
128.d:
एवं दुर्गस्य विन्यासं वाह्ये स्थानं दिशाधिपात् /
आगन्तुको यदा योद्धा ऋक्षवान् स्यात्फलान्वितः //
128.m: Thus is the arrangement of the fortress; its outer place is determined by the regent of the direction. / When an arriving warrior is endowed with his asterism, he will possess success.

128.s:
koṭamadhye grahāḥ saumyā yadā ṛkṣānvitāḥ punaḥ /
jayaṃ madhyasthitānāntu bhaṅgamāgāmino viduḥ //
128.d:
कोटमध्ये ग्रहाः सौम्या यदा ऋक्षान्विताः पुनः /
जयं मध्यस्थितानान्तु भङ्गमागामिनो विदुः //
128.m: When beneficent planets are situated in the middle of the fort and united with their asterisms, / they know victory for those stationed inside, and defeat for the attacker.

128.s:
praveśabhe praveṣṭavyaṃ nirgamabhe ca nirgamet /
bhṛguḥ saumyas tathā bhauma ṛkṣāntaṃ sakalaṃ yadā //
128.d:
प्रवेशभे प्रवेष्टव्यं निर्गमभे च निर्गमेत् /
भृगुः सौम्यस् तथा भौम ऋक्षान्तं सकलं यदा //
128.m: One should enter under an entry-asterism, and depart under an exit-asterism. / When Venus, Mercury, and Mars are wholly at the end of the asterisms,

128.s:
tadā bhaṅgaṃ vijānīyājjayamāgantukasya ca /
:p 62
praveśarkṣacatuṣke tu saṅgrāmañcārabhed yadā //
128.d:
तदा भङ्गं विजानीयाज्जयमागन्तुकस्य च /
:प् 62
प्रवेशर्क्षचतुष्के तु सङ्ग्रामञ्चारभेद् यदा //
128.m:
then one should know defeat [for the defenders] and victory for the attacker.
:p 62
When one initiates battle under the four entry-asterisms,

128.s:
tadā siddhyati taddurgaṃ na kuryāttatra vismayam //14//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe yuddhajayārṇave koṭacakraṃ
nāmāṣṭāviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athonatriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
arghakāṇḍam
128.d:
तदा सिद्ध्यति तद्दुर्गं न कुर्यात्तत्र विस्मयम् //14//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे युद्धजयार्णवे कोटचक्रं
नामाष्टाविंशत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथोनत्रिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
अर्घकाण्डम्
128.m:
that fort is taken; one need not feel wonder at this.
Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-eighth chapter, entitled “The Fort Diagram”, in the Ocean of Victory in Battle in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now, the one hundred and twenty-ninth chapter:
[The Fluctuation of Prices]

129.s:
īśvara uvāca
arghamānaṃ pravakṣyāmi ulkāpāto 'tha bhūś calā /
nirghāto grahaṇaṃ veśo diśāṃ dāho bhavedyadā //
129.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
अर्घमानं प्रवक्ष्यामि उल्कापातो ऽथ भूश् चला /
निर्घातो ग्रहणं वेशो दिशां दाहो भवेद्यदा //
129.m: The Lord said: / I will declare the measure of prices. When a meteor falls, the earth shakes, / there is an atmospheric explosion, an eclipse, a halo, or a burning of the quarters,

129.s:
lakṣayenmāsi māsyevaṃ yadyete syuś ca caitrake /
alaṅkārādi saṅgṛhya ṣaḍbhirmāsaiś caturguṇam //
129.d:
लक्षयेन्मासि मास्येवं यद्येते स्युश् च चैत्रके /
अलङ्कारादि सङ्गृह्य षड्भिर्मासैश् चतुर्गुणम् //
129.m: one should observe thus month by month: if these occur in Caitra, / having hoarded ornaments and the like, [their value will be] fourfold in six months.

129.s:
vaiśākhe cāṣṭame māsi ṣaḍguṇaṃ sarvasaṅgrahaṃ /
jyaiṣṭhe māsi tathāṣāḍhe yavagodhūmadhānyakaiḥ //
129.d:
वैशाखे चाष्टमे मासि षड्गुणं सर्वसङ्ग्रहं /
ज्यैष्ठे मासि तथाषाढे यवगोधूमधान्यकैः //
129.m: In Vaiśākha, every collection [gains] sixfold in the eighth month; / in the month of Jyaiṣṭha and in Āṣāḍha, with barley, wheat, and grains;

129.s:
śrāvaṇe ghṛtatailādyair āśvine vastradhānyakaiḥ /
kārttike dhānyakaiḥ krītair māse syānmārgaśīrṣake //
129.d:
श्रावणे घृततैलाद्यैर् आश्विने वस्त्रधान्यकैः /
कार्त्तिके धान्यकैः क्रीतैर् मासे स्यान्मार्गशीर्षके //
129.m: in Śrāvaṇa, with ghee, oil, and the like; in Āśvina, with cloth and grain; / in Kārttika, with purchased grains, [there is profit] in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa;

129.s:
puṣye kuṅkumagandhādyair lābho dhānyaiś ca māghake /
gandhādyaiḥ phālgune krītair arghakāṇḍamudāhṛtam //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe arghakāṇḍaṃ nāma
ūnatriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:p 63
:ś atha triṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
ghātacakraṃ
129.d:
पुष्ये कुङ्कुमगन्धाद्यैर् लाभो धान्यैश् च माघके /
गन्धाद्यैः फाल्गुने क्रीतैर् अर्घकाण्डमुदाहृतम् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अर्घकाण्डं नाम
ऊनत्रिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:प् 63
:श् अथ त्रिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
घातचक्रं
129.m:
in Puṣya, with saffron, perfumes, and the like, and profit with grains in Māgha; / with perfumes and the like bought in Phālguna. The section on prices has thus been told.
Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-ninth chapter, entitled “The Section on Prices”, in the great Agni Purāṇa.
:p 63
Now, the one hundred and thirtieth chapter:
[The Slaughter Diagram]

130.s:
īśvara uvāca
maṇḍalāni pravakṣyāmi caturdhā vijayāya hi /
kṛttikā ca maghā puṣpaṃ pūrvā caiva tu phalgunī //
130.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
मण्डलानि प्रवक्ष्यामि चतुर्धा विजयाय हि /
कृत्तिका च मघा पुष्पं पूर्वा चैव तु फल्गुनी //
130.m: The Lord said: / I will declare the fourfold spheres for the sake of victory. / Kṛttikā, Maghā, Puṣya, Pūrvaphalgunī,

130.s:
viśākhā bharaṇī caiva pūrvabhādrapadā tathā /
āgneyamaṇḍalaṃ bhadre tasya vakṣyāmi lakṣaṇaṃ //
130.d:
विशाखा भरणी चैव पूर्वभाद्रपदा तथा /
आग्नेयमण्डलं भद्रे तस्य वक्ष्यामि लक्षणं //
130.m: Viśākhā, Bharaṇī, and Pūrvabhādrapadā / form the fire-sphere, O auspicious lady; I will declare its characteristics.

130.s:
yadyatra calate vāyurveṣṭanaṃ śaśisūryayoḥ /
bhūmikampo 'tha nirghāto grahaṇaṃ candrasūryayoḥ //
130.d:
यद्यत्र चलते वायुर्वेष्टनं शशिसूर्ययोः /
भूमिकम्पो ऽथ निर्घातो ग्रहणं चन्द्रसूर्ययोः //
130.m: If wind shifts here, [or if there is] a halo around the moon or the sun, / an earthquake, an atmospheric crash, an eclipse of the moon or the sun,

130.s:
dhūmajvālā diśāṃ dāhaḥ ketoś caiva pradarśanaṃ /
raktavṛṣṭiścopatāpaḥ pāṣāṇapatanantathā //
130.d:
धूमज्वाला दिशां दाहः केतोश् चैव प्रदर्शनं /
रक्तवृष्टिश्चोपतापः पाषाणपतनन्तथा //
130.m: smoke and flames, a burning of the cardinal points, the sighting of a comet, / a shower of blood, heatwaves, and the falling of stones;

130.s:
netrarogo 'tisāraś ca agniś ca prabalo bhavet /
svalpakṣīrās tathā gāvaḥ svalpapuṣpaphalā drumāḥ //
130.d:
नेत्ररोगो ऽतिसारश् च अग्निश् च प्रबलो भवेत् /
स्वल्पक्षीरास् तथा गावः स्वल्पपुष्पफला द्रुमाः //
130.m: eye disease, diarrhoea, and fire will become intense; / cows will yield little milk, and trees will have few blossoms and fruits;

130.s:
vināśaś caiva śasyānāṃ svalpavṛṣṭiṃ vinirdiśet /
cāturvarṇāḥ prapīḍyante kṣudhārtā akhilā narāḥ //
130.d:
विनाशश् चैव शस्यानां स्वल्पवृष्टिं विनिर्दिशेत् /
चातुर्वर्णाः प्रपीड्यन्ते क्षुधार्ता अखिला नराः //
130.m: there will be destruction of crops, and one should predict scant rainfall. / The four social classes will be afflicted, and all men will suffer hunger.

130.s:
saindhavā yāmunāś caiva gurjakā bhojavāhṇikāḥ /
jālandharaṃ ca kāśmīraṃ saptamañcottarāpatham //
130.d:
सैन्धवा यामुनाश् चैव गुर्जका भोजवाह्णिकाः /
जालन्धरं च काश्मीरं सप्तमञ्चोत्तरापथम् //
130.m: The Saindhavas, the Yāmunas, the Gurjaras, the Bhojas, the Bāhlīkas, / Jālandhara, Kāśmīra, and the northern region as the seventh—

130.s:
deśāś caite vinaśyanti tasminnutpātadarśane /
hastā citrā maghā svātī mṛgo vātha punarvasuḥ //
130.d:
देशाश् चैते विनश्यन्ति तस्मिन्नुत्पातदर्शने /
हस्ता चित्रा मघा स्वाती मृगो वाथ पुनर्वसुः //
130.m: these regions will perish upon the appearance of that portent. / Hastā, Citrā, Maghā, Svātī, Mṛgaśīrṣa, or Punarvasu,

130.s:
uttarāphalgunī caiva aśvinī ca tathaiva ca /
:p 64
yadātra bhavate(1) kiñcidvāyavyantaṃ vinirdiśet //
130.d:
उत्तराफल्गुनी चैव अश्विनी च तथैव च /
:प् 64
यदात्र भवते(1) किञ्चिद्वायव्यन्तं विनिर्दिशेत् //
130.m:
Uttarāphalgunī, and Aśvinī as well:
:p 64
when any [portent] occurs among these, one should designate it as the wind-sphere.

130.s:
naṣṭadharmāḥ prajāḥ sarvā hāhābhūtā vicetasaḥ /
ḍāhalaḥ kāmarūpañca kaliṅgaḥ kośalas tathā //
130.d:
नष्टधर्माः प्रजाः सर्वा हाहाभूता विचेतसः /
डाहलः कामरूपञ्च कलिङ्गः कोशलस् तथा //
130.m: All subjects will lose their righteousness, wailing in distress and bewildered. / Ḍāhala, Kāmarūpa, Kaliṅga, Kośala,

130.s:
ayodhyā ca avantī ca naśyante koṅkaṇāndhrakāḥ /
aśleṣā caiva mūlantu pūrvāṣāḍhā tathaiva ca //
130.d:
अयोध्या च अवन्ती च नश्यन्ते कोङ्कणान्ध्रकाः /
अश्लेषा चैव मूलन्तु पूर्वाषाढा तथैव च //
130.m: Ayodhyā, Avantī, the Koṅkaṇas, and the Andhras will be destroyed. / Āśleṣā, Mūla, Pūrvāṣāḍhā,

130.s:
revatī vāruṇaṃ hy ṛkṣantathā bhādrapadottarā /
yadātra calate(2) kiñcidvāruṇaṃ taṃ vinirdiśet //
130.d:
रेवती वारुणं ह्य् ऋक्षन्तथा भाद्रपदोत्तरा /
यदात्र चलते(2) किञ्चिद्वारुणं तं विनिर्दिशेत् //
130.m: Revatī, Śravaṇa, and Uttarabhādrapadā: / when any [portent] moves here, one should designate it as the water-sphere.

130.s:
bahukṣīraghṛtā gāvo bahupuṣpaphalā drumāḥ /
ārogyaṃ tatra jāyeta bahuśasyā ca medinī //
130.d:
बहुक्षीरघृता गावो बहुपुष्पफला द्रुमाः /
आरोग्यं तत्र जायेत बहुशस्या च मेदिनी //
130.m: Cows will have abundant milk and clarified butter; trees will bear abundant flowers and fruit; / freedom from disease will arise there, and the earth will produce abundant crops.

130.s:
dhānyāni ca samarghāni sukhikṣaṃ pārthiva bhavet /
pparasparaṃ narendrāṇāṃ saṅgrāmo dāruṇo bhavet //
130.d:
धान्यानि च समर्घानि सुखिक्षं पार्थिव भवेत् /
प्परस्परं नरेन्द्राणां सङ्ग्रामो दारुणो भवेत् //
130.m: Grains will be of fair value, and there will be abundance for the king. / [Yet] between the kings, there will be fierce warfare.

130.s:
jyeṣṭhā ca rohiṇī caiva anurādhā ca vaiṣṇavam /
dhaniṣṭhā cottarāṣāḍhā abhijit saptamantathā //
130.d:
ज्येष्ठा च रोहिणी चैव अनुराधा च वैष्णवम् /
धनिष्ठा चोत्तराषाढा अभिजित् सप्तमन्तथा //
130.m: Jyeṣṭhā, Rohiṇī, Anurādhā, Śravaṇa, / Dhaniṣṭhā, Uttarāṣāḍhā, and Abhijit as the seventh:

130.s:
yadātra śalate(3) kiñcin māhendraṃ taṃ vinirdiśet /
prajāḥ samuditāstasmin sarvarogavivarjitāḥ //
130.d:
यदात्र शलते(3) किञ्चिन् माहेन्द्रं तं विनिर्दिशेत् /
प्रजाः समुदितास्तस्मिन् सर्वरोगविवर्जिताः //
130.m: when any [portent] moves here, one should designate it as Indra's sphere. / In this, the people will be delighted and free from all diseases;

130.s:
sandhiṃ kurvanti rājānaḥ subhikṣaṃ pārthivaṃ śubham /
grāmastu dvividho jñeyo mukhapucchakaro mahān //
130.d:
सन्धिं कुर्वन्ति राजानः सुभिक्षं पार्थिवं शुभम् /
ग्रामस्तु द्विविधो ज्ञेयो मुखपुच्छकरो महान् //
130.m: kings make peace, and there is auspicious abundance for the king. / An eclipse is known to be of two kinds: the great one causing a head and a tail.

130.s:
candro rāhus tathāditya ekarāśau yadi sthitaḥ(4) /
mukhagrāmastu vijñeyo yāmitre puccha ucyate //
:n
1 yadyatra bhvate iti ja..
2,3 yadātra labhate iti cha..
4 yathā sthita iti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , ja.. ca / yadā sthita iti ja.. , jha.. ca
:p 65
130.d:
चन्द्रो राहुस् तथादित्य एकराशौ यदि स्थितः(4) /
मुखग्रामस्तु विज्ञेयो यामित्रे पुच्छ उच्यते //
:न्
1 यद्यत्र भ्वते इति ज..
2,3 यदात्र लभते इति छ..
4 यथा स्थित इति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , ज.. च / यदा स्थित इति ज.. , झ.. च
:प् 65
130.m:
If the Moon, Rāhu, and the Sun are situated in the same zodiacal sign, / it is known as an eclipse at the head; it is said to be at the tail in the seventh house.
:n
1. "yadyatra bhavate" according to ja.
2,3. "yadātra labhate" according to cha.
4. "yathā sthitaḥ" according to kha, ga, gha, ṅa, and ja; "yadā sthitaḥ" according to ja and jha.
:p 65

130.s:
bhānoḥ pañcadaśe hy ṛkṣe yadā carati candramāḥ /
tithicchede(1) tu samprāpte somagrāmaṃ vinirdiśet //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe yuddhajayārṇave maṇḍalaṃ nāma
triṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athaikatriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
ghātacakrādiḥ
130.d:
भानोः पञ्चदशे ह्य् ऋक्षे यदा चरति चन्द्रमाः /
तिथिच्छेदे(1) तु सम्प्राप्ते सोमग्रामं विनिर्दिशेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे युद्धजयार्णवे मण्डलं नाम
त्रिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथैकत्रिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
घातचक्रादिः
130.m:
When the Moon moves in the fifteenth asterism from the Sun / at the arrival of the division of lunar days, one should designate it as a lunar eclipse.
Thus ends the one hundred and thirtieth chapter, entitled "The Maṇḍala in the Ocean of Victory in Battle", in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now, the one hundred and thirty-first chapter.
The Hurt Wheel and related topics.

131.s:
īśvara uvāca
pradakṣiṇamakārādīn svarān pūrvādito likhet /
caitrādyaṃ bhramaṇāccakraṃ pratipat pūrṇimā tithiḥ //
131.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
प्रदक्षिणमकारादीन् स्वरान् पूर्वादितो लिखेत् /
चैत्राद्यं भ्रमणाच्चक्रं प्रतिपत् पूर्णिमा तिथिः //
131.m:
The Lord said:
One should write clockwise the vowels beginning with "a", starting from the east.
From the rotation [of the diagram] starting with Caitra, the wheel [is drawn, marking] the tithis: the pratipad and the full-moon day,

131.s:
trayodaśī caturdaśī aṣṭamyekā ca saptamī /
pratipattrayodaśyantāstithayo dvādaśa smṛtāḥ //
131.d:
त्रयोदशी चतुर्दशी अष्टम्येका च सप्तमी /
प्रतिपत्त्रयोदश्यन्तास्तिथयो द्वादश स्मृताः //
131.m:
the thirteenth, the fourteenth, the eighth, and the seventh.
The twelve tithis are remembered as ending with the pratipad and the thirteenth.

131.s:
caitracakre tu saṃsparśājjayalābhādikaṃ viduḥ /
ciṣame tu śubhaṃ jñeyaṃ same cāśubhamīritam //
131.d:
चैत्रचक्रे तु संस्पर्शाज्जयलाभादिकं विदुः /
चिषमे तु शुभं ज्ञेयं समे चाशुभमीरितम् //
131.m:
They know that victory, gain, and the like [are indicated] through contact on the Caitra wheel;
it is to be known as auspicious on an odd [space], and pronounced inauspicious on an even one.

131.s:
yuddhakāle samutpatre yasya nama hy udāhṛtam /
mātrārūḍhantu yannāma ādityo gurureva ca //
:n
1 tithibhede iti jha..
:p 66
131.d:
युद्धकाले समुत्पत्रे यस्य नम ह्य् उदाहृतम् /
मात्रारूढन्तु यन्नाम आदित्यो गुरुरेव च //
:न्
1 तिथिभेदे इति झ..
:प् 66
131.m:
Whose name is uttered when the battle has commenced,
and whose name has long vowels, the Sun and Jupiter [favor him];
[Footnote]
1. Variant reading: "tithibhede" in jha..
[Page 66]

131.s:
jayastasya sadākālaṃ saṅgrāme caiva bhīṣaṇe /
hrasvanāma yadā yodho mriyate hy anivāritaḥ(1) //
131.d:
जयस्तस्य सदाकालं सङ्ग्रामे चैव भीषणे /
ह्रस्वनाम यदा योधो म्रियते ह्य् अनिवारितः(1) //
131.m:
victory belongs to him at all times, even in terrifying battle.
When a warrior has a short-vowelled name, he dies without prevention.

131.s:
prathamo dīrgha ādistho dvitīyo madhye antakaḥ /
dvau madhyena prathamāntau jāyete nātra saṃśayaḥ //
131.d:
प्रथमो दीर्घ आदिस्थो द्वितीयो मध्ये अन्तकः /
द्वौ मध्येन प्रथमान्तौ जायेते नात्र संशयः //
131.m:
The first is long, placed at the beginning; the second is in the middle, [and one is] final.
Two intermediate ones are born with the initial and final; there is no doubt about this.

131.s:
punaścānte yadā cādau(2) svarārūḍhantu dṛśyate /
hrasvasya maraṇaṃ vidyād dīrghasyaiva jayo bhavet //
131.d:
पुनश्चान्ते यदा चादौ(2) स्वरारूढन्तु दृश्यते /
ह्रस्वस्य मरणं विद्याद् दीर्घस्यैव जयो भवेत् //
131.m:
Moreover, when at the end or at the beginning [the name] is seen to be mounted with vowels,
one should know that death comes to the short [name], while victory belongs only to the long.

131.s:
naracakraṃ pravakṣyāmi hy ṛkṣapiṇḍātmakaṃ yathā /
pratimāmālikhet pūrvaṃ padyādṛkṣāṇi vinyaset //
131.d:
नरचक्रं प्रवक्ष्यामि ह्य् ऋक्षपिण्डात्मकं यथा /
प्रतिमामालिखेत् पूर्वं पद्यादृक्षाणि विन्यसेत् //
131.m:
I shall explain the Man Wheel, which consists of a cluster of asterisms.
One should first draw the figure; then one should deposit the asterisms beginning with the feet:

131.s:
śīrṣe trīṇi mukhe caikaṃ dve ṛkṣe netrayornyaset /
vedasaṅkhyāni hastābhyāṃ karṇe ṛkṣadvayaṃ punaḥ //
131.d:
शीर्षे त्रीणि मुखे चैकं द्वे ऋक्षे नेत्रयोर्न्यसेत् /
वेदसङ्ख्यानि हस्ताभ्यां कर्णे ऋक्षद्वयं पुनः //
131.m:
three on the head, one on the face, and two asterisms one should deposit on the two eyes;
four on the two hands, and again two asterisms on the ear;

131.s:
hṛdaye bhūtasaṅkhyāni ṣaḍṛkṣāṇi tu pādayoḥ /
nāma hy ṛkṣaṃ sphuṭaṃ kṛṭvā cakramadhye tu vinyaset //
131.d:
हृदये भूतसङ्ख्यानि षडृक्षाणि तु पादयोः /
नाम ह्य् ऋक्षं स्फुटं कृट्वा चक्रमध्ये तु विन्यसेत् //
131.m:
five on the heart, and six asterisms on the feet.
Having made clear the asterism of the name, one should place it in the center of the wheel:

131.s:
netre śirodakṣakarṇe yāmyahaste ca pādayoḥ /
hṛdgrīvāvāmahaste tu punarguhye tu pādayoḥ //
131.d:
नेत्रे शिरोदक्षकर्णे याम्यहस्ते च पादयोः /
हृद्ग्रीवावामहस्ते तु पुनर्गुह्ये तु पादयोः //
131.m:
on the eye, head, right ear, right hand, and the two feet,
on the heart, neck, left hand, and again on the private parts and the two feet.

131.s:
yasminnṛkṣe sthitaḥ sūryaḥ saurirbhaumastu saiṃhikaḥ /
tasmin sthāne sthite vidyād ghātameva na saṃśayaḥ //
131.d:
यस्मिन्नृक्षे स्थितः सूर्यः सौरिर्भौमस्तु सैंहिकः /
तस्मिन् स्थाने स्थिते विद्याद् घातमेव न संशयः //
131.m:
The asterism in which the Sun, Saturn, Mars, or Rāhu is situated—
when [the name-asterism] is placed in that position, one should know there will be slaughter, without doubt.

131.s:
jayacakraṃ pravakṣyāmi ādihāntāṃś ca vai likhet /
rekhāstrayodaśālikhya ṣaḍrekhāstiryagālikhet //
131.d:
जयचक्रं प्रवक्ष्यामि आदिहान्तांश् च वै लिखेत् /
रेखास्त्रयोदशालिख्य षड्रेखास्तिर्यगालिखेत् //
131.m:
I shall explain the Victory Wheel: one should draw [the letters] beginning with "a" and ending with "ha".
Having drawn thirteen lines, one should draw six crosswise lines.

131.s:
dig grahā munayaḥ sūryā ṛtvigrudrastithiḥ kramāt /
mūrchanāsmṛtivedarkṣajinā(3) akaḍamā hy adhaḥ //
:n
1 mriyate hy avicārita iti kha.. / mriyate hy avicārata iti ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. ca
2 yathā cādau iti ka.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. ca
3 mūrchanāsmṛtivedāṅgajinā iti ña..
:p 67
131.d:
दिग् ग्रहा मुनयः सूर्या ऋत्विग्रुद्रस्तिथिः क्रमात् /
मूर्छनास्मृतिवेदर्क्षजिना(3) अकडमा ह्य् अधः //
:न्
1 म्रियते ह्य् अविचारित इति ख.. / म्रियते ह्य् अविचारत इति ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. च
2 यथा चादौ इति क.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. च
3 मूर्छनास्मृतिवेदाङ्गजिना इति ञ..
:प् 67
131.m:
Ten, nine, seven, twelve, sixteen, eleven, fifteen in order;
seven, eighteen, four, twenty-seven, twenty-four—[and the letters] a, ka, ḍa, ma underneath.
[Footnote]
1. Variant reading: "mriyate hy avicāritaḥ" in kha..; "mriyate hy avicārataḥ" in ga.., gha.., and ṅa..
2. Variant reading: "yathā cādau" in ka.., ga.., gha.., and ṅa..
3. Variant reading: "mūrchanāsmṛtivedāṅgajinā" in ña..
[Page 67]

131.s:
ādityādyāḥ saptahṛte nāmānte balino grahāḥ /
ādityasauribhaumākhyā jaye saumyāś ca sandhaye //
131.d:
आदित्याद्याः सप्तहृते नामान्ते बलिनो ग्रहाः /
आदित्यसौरिभौमाख्या जये सौम्याश् च सन्धये //
131.m:
Beginning with the Sun, the planets are strong at the end of a name when divided by seven.
Those called the Sun, Saturn, and Mars bring victory, and the gentle planets bring peace.

131.s:
rekhā dvādaśa coddhṛtya ṣaṭ ca yāsyāstathottarāḥ /
manuś caiva tu(1) ṛkṣāṇi netre ca ravimaṇḍalaṃ //
131.d:
रेखा द्वादश चोद्धृत्य षट् च यास्यास्तथोत्तराः /
मनुश् चैव तु(1) ऋक्षाणि नेत्रे च रविमण्डलं //
131.m:
Having raised twelve lines, six facing south and six facing north:
fourteen, and the asterisms [twenty-seven], two, and the orb of the Sun [twelve];

131.s:
tithayaś ca rasā vedā agniḥ saptadaśāthavā /
vasurandhrāḥ samākhyātā akaṭapānadho nyaset //
131.d:
तिथयश् च रसा वेदा अग्निः सप्तदशाथवा /
वसुरन्ध्राः समाख्याता अकटपानधो न्यसेत् //
131.m:
and the tithis [fifteen], six, four, three, or seventeen;
eight and nine are declared; one should place [the letters] a, ka, ṭa, pa underneath.

131.s:
ekaikamakṣarannyastvā śeṣāṇyevaṅkramān nyaset /
nāmākṣarakṛtaṃ piṇḍaṃ vasubhirbhājayettataḥ //
131.d:
एकैकमक्षरन्न्यस्त्वा शेषाण्येवङ्क्रमान् न्यसेत् /
नामाक्षरकृतं पिण्डं वसुभिर्भाजयेत्ततः //
131.m:
Having placed the letters one by one, one should place the remaining ones in this sequence.
One should then divide the sum made by the letters of the name by eight.

131.s:
vāyasānmaṇḍalo 'tyagro maṇḍalādrāsabho varaḥ /
rāsabhādvṛṣabhaḥ śreṣṭhā vṛṣabhāt kuñjaro varaḥ //
131.d:
वायसान्मण्डलो ऽत्यग्रो मण्डलाद्रासभो वरः /
रासभाद्वृषभः श्रेष्ठा वृषभात् कुञ्जरो वरः //
131.m:
The dog is fiercer than the crow; the donkey is superior to the dog;
the bull is superior to the donkey; the elephant is superior to the bull;

131.s:
kuñjarāccaiva punaḥ siṃhaḥ siṃhāś caiva kharurvaraḥ /
kharoś caiva balī dhūmraḥ evamādi balābalaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe
ghātacakrādirnāmaikatriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha dvātriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
sevācakraṃ
131.d:
कुञ्जराच्चैव पुनः सिंहः सिंहाश् चैव खरुर्वरः /
खरोश् चैव बली धूम्रः एवमादि बलाबलं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे
घातचक्रादिर्नामैकत्रिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ द्वात्रिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
सेवाचक्रं
131.m:
and the lion is [superior] to the elephant; the kharu is superior to the lion;
and the smoky-colored one is stronger than the kharu; such is strength and weakness.
Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-first chapter, entitled "The Hurt Wheel and Others", in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now, the one hundred and thirty-second chapter.
The Service Wheel.
